title: Report: Daron Payne out for season with Jones fracture
summary: Daron Payne’s foot injury will keep him out for the rest of the season.
full_text: Daron Payne’s foot injury will keep him out for the rest of the season. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Payne’s significant injury is a Jones fracture, which will sideline him through the remainder of 2026. Payne had been added to the injury report on Friday after suffering the injury in practice. The No. 13 overall pick in 2018, Payne is Washington’s longest-tenured player. He did not miss a game from 2020-2024 and missed just two contests in 2025. In his nine seasons, he’s recorded 38.0 sacks, 67 tackles for loss, and 86 quarterback hits. His 2026 will end having tallied 14 total tackles, two tackles for loss, five QB hits, and one sack.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Josh Jacobs could be on thin ice in Green Bay
summary: Throughout his off-field incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery, the Packers have remained steadfast in their support of running back Josh Jacobs.
full_text: '' Throughout his off-field incident that resulted in a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery, the Packers have remained steadfast in their support of running back Josh Jacobs. That could now be changing. The persistent presence of the Packers as one of the teams that have expressed some degree of interest in trading for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor suggests that they've at least pondered the possibility of swapping out Jacobs for Taylor. Recent developments don't help Jacobs's cause. Beyond the handcuff celebration that Jacobs tried to say wasn’t a handcuff celebration (but that video of the full celebration suggests was a handcuff celebration ), Friday's release of police records indicating that at least three other women have accused Jacobs of domestic violence could shake the team's apparent resolve to keep him. Throw in the fact that Jacobs is averaging 2.3 yards per carry in his two games back from a six-game stint on paid leave — including 1.9 yards per carry against the worst run defense in the league entering Thursday night's game — and it's possible that the Packers will realize that Jacobs is no longer good enough to justify a stubborn circling of the wagons. Cutting Jacobs would raise the issue of termination pay as to the balance of his $10.2 million salary, and it would short-circuit the team's ability to seek partial repayment of signing-bonus money if/when (when) he's eventually suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy. For now, we won't delve into the full extent of the niceties of Article 30 of the CBA; at a minimum, the Packers would have some potential arguments aimed at cutting off his right to any termination pay. Even if the Packers ultimately are on the hook for termination pay, it's a sunk cost. The question is whether they want to keep him on the team, in light of recent developments. Again, they've been linked in multiple reports from ESPNFL to a trade for Jonathan Taylor. That alone is substantial evidence that they're considering a future without Jacobs that could begin sooner rather than later.
author: Mike Florio

title: Reports: Packers targeting Week 12 for Micah Parsons return
summary: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said this week that he hopes defensive end Micah Parsons starts practicing with the team next week and the team reportedly has a goal in mind for Parsons's return to game action.
full_text: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said this week that he hopes defensive end Micah Parsons starts practicing with the team next week and the team reportedly has a goal in mind for Parsons's return to game action. According to multiple reports, the team is targeting Week 12 for Parsons to play his first game since tearing his ACL last season. The Packers will be in Los Angeles to face the Rams in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday, November 25. If Parsons does return to practice next week, it would open a 21-day window for him to work with the team ahead of being activated. The Packers, who beat the Panthers on Thursday night this week, face the Patriots and Vikings before a bye week in Week 11. That timeline would have Parsons back for the final seven games of the regular season and his presence should boost the chances of the Packers following up those games with playoff action.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: John Harbaugh called Amy Adams Strunk directly in an effort to land Jeffery Simmons
summary: Harbaugh's unconventional move failed to prevent Bears from doing deal with Titans.
full_text: The trade that sent defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans to the Bears has an interesting — and unusual — postscript. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reports that Giants coach John Harbaugh directly called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an effort to get Simmons to New York. The call reportedly came after Giants G.M. Joe Schoen had contacted Titans G.M. Mike Borgonzi about Simmons, only to be told that the Titans weren't trading him. As Jones notes, another G.M. who learned about the effort said it "violates a code" among football's decision-makers. One source in a key football position with one of the NFL's teams dubbed the effort "shameful." Despite Borgonzi's claim from Thursday that the Titans weren't looking to trade Simmons until the Bears called on Wednesday night, Jones reports that the Titans' "braintrust" had a meeting on Tuesday during which they decided to start listening to offers for Simmons. It's unclear whether Harbaugh made the call to Adams before or after Bears G.M. Ryan Poles offered a package that included a pair of first-round picks. We're told the Giants were willing to offer more than what the Bears ultimately sent to the Titans. (Of course, that's easy to say at this point.) The entire situation underscores the value of pre-existing relationships when it comes to getting deals done. It was a point we discussed on Friday's PFT Live . In 2021, the trade that sent quarterback Matthew Stafford from the Lions to the Rams had a distinct "inside job" feel to it, given that Lions G.M. Brad Holmes had recently been hired from the Rams. Other teams that would have been interested in attempting to acquire Stafford were surprised to learn that he had been quietly and quickly dealt to the Rams, who were able to tuck quarterback Jared Goff into the deal — and to discreetly attach extra compensation to get the Lions to take on a contract that, after only two seasons, the Rams had come to regret. The outcome prompted former Commanders G.M. Martin Mayhew to call every team in the league the following offseason to inquire as to whether their starting quarterback may be available in trade. The ultimate question, when trades like this happen, is whether the relationship angle results in the team that gives up a key player getting as much as it could. If the Giants would have indeed offered more, shouldn't the Titans have fully explored that avenue? Ultimately, the longstanding relationship between Poles and Borgonzi may have superseded the effort to get as much as possible for Simmons.
author: Mike Florio

title: Reports: Jets aren't open to trading Garrett Wilson
summary: The Jets made a pair of big trades ahead of the 2025 trade deadline and they've got a player whose name has come up as a possible target for other teams this year.
full_text: ' The Jets made a pair of big trades ahead of the 2025 trade deadline and they've got a player whose name has come up as a possible target for other teams this year. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson would make several offenses better equipped to make a run at postseason success and his frustration with the way this Jets season is playing out boiled over on the sideline during last Sunday's loss to the Dolphins. Wilson followed that up by saying he loves playing for the Jets, but would also like to experience life on a winning team. At the moment, it looks like he'll have to hope that happens while he's in a Jets uniform. Multiple reports say the Jets have told other teams that Wilson is not available ahead of the November 10 deadline. The Jets already have three first-round picks in 2027 and believe that Wilson's presence along with additions they can make with those assets will better position the team to win games than dealing him away. Word was similar out of Tennessee before the Bears offered a pair of first-rounders for Jeffery Simmons, so it's possible someone could change the Jets' minds but, for now, Wilson appears set to stay put.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonathan Taylor trade talks are "active and ongoing"
summary: Seahawks, Packers, Broncos, Vikings, Giants are pegged as potential destinations.
full_text: There are two ways to handle the trade of a cornerstone player. One, talk quietly to a minimal number of teams. Like the Titans did with defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Two, throw the doors open and try to get the best possible package of draft picks and/or players in return. Like the Colts are now doing with running back Jonathan Taylor. Indianapolis has officially declared that Taylor is available , via a selective and strategic leak to ESPNFL. Trade talks are "active and ongoing," per the report. The teams that have "expressed at least some level of interest" are the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants, and Seahawks. Last weekend's Sunday Splash! report that operated as the "everything must go" sign for the Colts pegged the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, and Seahawks as potentially interested teams in Taylor. The Giants (who are believed, we're told by multiple sources, to have been pursuing Simmons) are a new arrival. Which would possibly be bad news for second-year running back Cam Skattebo, who emerged from the doghouse last week with 124 rushing yards. (It wouldn't be a surprise if the Giants offered Skattebo to the Colts as part of the trade package, frankly.) To the extent that tying four teams to the trade talks doesn't get the Colts maximum compensation, the new report notes that the Colts "would prefer" that Taylor stick around for their "rebuild." If they really wanted Taylor, they wouldn't be fielding trade offers fo him. The Colts reportedly are looking for a package similar to what the 49ers sent to the Panthers in 2022 for running back Christian McCaffrey: a second-round pick, a third-round pick, and a fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft and a fifth-round pick in the 2024 draft. The next question is whether Taylor will play on Sunday. It's possible, in our view, the Colts will hold Taylor out of action on Sunday at Jacksonville, like the Cardinals did three weeks ago when they had a deal in place to trade receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans. Even without a deal, keeping Taylor out of the game would ensure that he won't get injured. If that happens, rookie Seth McGowan would be the likely starter in Week 8. Last Sunday, the seventh-rounder who played for Kentucky last year had 11 carries for 48 yards in a 16-10 loss to the Vikings. And the Vikings continue to make the most sense for Taylor. Especially since they had the best possible opportunity to scout him six days ago, when he had 18 carries for 95 yards and an Adrian Peterson-style 38-yard touchdown run. If the Vikings add Taylor in the coming days, he'd likely make his debut as soon as next Monday night, when the Vikings host the Bills. And when they put Peterson in the team's Ring of Honor.
author: Mike Florio

title: Philip Rivers on NC State job: "Nothing's imminent"
summary: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers has reportedly "emerged as the focus" of the NC State coaching search.
full_text: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers has reportedly " emerged as the focus " of the NC State coaching search. On Friday night, he didn't do much to throw water on the possibility. "I mean, shoot, NC State’s special to me ," Rivers said after coaching his latest high-school game (via Ben Thomas of AL.com), "and, you know, Coach [Dave] Doren, shoot, what he did over 14 years, and all-time winningest coach is a — ton of respect and appreciation, you know, for how he went about it with the university, and, you know, there's nothing there at this point. No, you understand — like I told you earlier in the week — you understand the chatter is out there. Gotta take it one day at a time, you know, is all I know. I'm excited this postseason with these guys here, and I guess it's like I told you last year, you know, you never say never, but there's nothing imminent." Rivers said "nothing" three times before choosing "imminent" as the next word. He could have just stopped with "nothing," if there was nothing. Clearly there's something. Even more clearly, Rivers wants to delay things until the playoff run is over at St. Michael's, the high school where he has coached since 2021. Indeed, Rivers specifically mentioned that he's "really looking forward to trying to send this last group off" with a state championship. He obviously wants to minimize distractions as they try to finish the job — and, more importantly, he's fully committed to not pulling a Lane Kiffin on his current team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jeffery Simmons excited to play in prime time for Bears, something Titans rarely do
summary: Jeffery Simmons is ready for prime time.
full_text: Jeffery Simmons is ready for prime time. Simmons, who was traded from the Titans to the Bears this week, will play on Monday night against the Seahawks, and then he'll play next week on Sunday night against the Buccaneers. The Bears are one of the NFL's marquee teams, the league puts them in marquee time slots, and that's a big change for Simmons, who hasn't played a prime time game since 2023. The Titans have no prime time games on the schedule this year. They had none last year, either. They had one prime time game in 2024, but Simmons missed that one with an elbow injury. The last time Simmons played in prime time was 2023, as the Titans just haven't been a team the NFL wants to promote. "It's exciting. I haven't played in a prime time game since 2023," Simmons said. "It's been that long since I've played in prime time. I think it was Thursday night against the Steelers, was the last time I actually played in one. It's exciting. When you've got a prime time game it means you're doing something right. With this team, with last year's success and this year, what more can you ask for? To come into this situation, to help this team win big games, meaningful football this time of the year, and also my first game being here in Chicago I get to play on Monday night. I think that's the dream of every NFL player, to come into a situation like this. I'm so excited. I'm excited to be able to go out there Monday night." Simmons said he's so accustomed to playing at noon Nashville time on Sunday and then getting home in time to watch Sunday Night Football that he sees the prime time games as special, just like the fans do. "I play at 12 o'clock every Sunday," Simmons said. "To be able to get home and watch the prime time games, then the Thursday night games, you're watching." A huge national TV audience will be watching Simmons, something that has rarely been the case during his eight-year NFL career.
author: Michael David Smith

title: After Josh Jacobs was arrested, three other women told police he had abused them, too
summary: Police records released late on Friday show three women contacted police after Jacobs' May arrest to report similar incidents.
full_text: '' While police were investigating Josh Jacobs following a domestic violence accusation in May, multiple other women reported similar incidents of Jacobs abusing them. NBC 26 in Green Bay received previously unreleased files in connection with the Jacobs case from the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department late Friday, and those files showed that officers heard from at least three other women who said they had been victims of violence at the hands of Jacobs . One woman contacted police in June after hearing of Jacobs' May arrest, saying she had been the victim of a similar incident with Jacobs years earlier and was reporting it to police for the first time because she wanted people to believe the woman accusing him in May. That woman said that in January of 2022, Jacobs slapped her across the face, grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down, threw her onto the floor, spit on her and grabbed her by the throat. She also said Jacobs took her phone as she attempted to leave his home. Another woman also contacted police later in June and said that in April of 2021, Jacobs grabbed her by the arms, pushed her against a wall near a window and threw her belongings outside the home. She said she suffered bruising to her arms and pain and swelling in her rib area. She said she had reported it to the police in a different municipality, and the records released by Hobart-Lawrence Police to NBC 26 indicate that they confirmed with another police department that it did receive that report, but Jacobs apparently was not arrested because the woman had no visible signs of injury. A third woman told Hobart/Lawrence Police in July that in May of 2022, Jacobs placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest, and took her phone. She said she suffered bruising to her arm and scratches to her chest. She said she did not report the incident to police or seek medical attention because Jacobs had told her she could be deported if she had any contact with the authorities. Jacobs eventually pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property in connection with the May arrest. The NFL placed him on paid leave for the first six games of the season, then allowed him to play starting in Week 7. Jacobs remains subject to a potential NFL suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy, and the accusations brought by the three other women could be considered by the NFL in determining league discipline.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: Philip Rivers has "emerged as the focus" of NC State coaching search
summary: Six days ago, former NFL (and NC State) quarterback Philip Rivers was identified as a person "expected to be in the mix" for the now-vacant Wolfpack head-coaching job.
full_text: Six days ago, former NFL (and NC State) quarterback Philip Rivers was identified as a person " expected to be in the mix " for the now-vacant Wolfpack head-coaching job. He has now " emerged as the focus " of the search, according to On3.com. There's reportedly no timetable for the hire, given that Rivers continues to coach high-school football in Alabama. Rivers's son, Gunner, has committed to attend NC State as a member of the class of 2027. NC State fired Dave Doeren last Saturday. Rivers played for the Wolfpack from 2000 to 2003. He was the fourth pick in the 2004 NFL draft, technically selected by the Giants before being sent to the Chargers as part of the Eli Manning trade. Rivers starred for the Chargers from 2004 through 2019. Rivers spent 2020 with the Colts before retiring. He returned last year to start three games for the Colts, after Indianapolis lost starter Daniel Jones to a torn Achilles tendon. Rivers has been coaching high-school football since 2021. He interviewed for the Bills' head-coaching vacancy earlier this year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jeffery Simmons says calling Caleb Williams "Painted Nails" was "just smack talk"
summary: New Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said his nickname for Caleb Williams two years ago was nothing more than gamesmanship.
full_text: New Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said his nickname for Caleb Williams two years ago was nothing more than gamesmanship. Simmons, then with the Titans, jokingly referred to Williams as "Painted Nails" in an interview with The Rich Eisen Show. He said Friday that he thought Bears fans were "going to crash my Instagram" after that. Now, Simmons, Williams and Bears fans are on the same side after the trade from Tennessee. “ I’ve been a fan of Caleb ,” Simmons said, via Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times . “Of course, being on the other side and having to play against him, I’m not going to tell him that. I’m going to talk as much smack as I can. “But now he’s on my team. Any teammate you ask about me, man, I have my teammate’s back, no matter if he’s on the other side of the ball or not. I’m going to talk the most smack to you when you’ve got a different color jersey on, but when we’re on the same team on Sundays, I go to war for any of my guys in the locker room. I hope Caleb would know that.” Simmons said he and Williams talked after a joint practice in August and again on Friday morning before meetings. Williams doesn't hold the comment against Simmons. “The comments a couple years ago about the nails is all part of my game, with the smack talk,” Simmons said. “I don’t know if you guys have heard, but I’m probably one of the best smack talkers. I talk a lot of smack when I’m on the field. I’m looking forward to being his teammate. We all know what type of player he is.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Daron Payne has a significant foot injury
summary: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne was expected to have serious trade interest before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
full_text: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne was expected to have serious trade interest before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Alas, Payne, who is in the final year of his contract, is heading to injured reserve instead. The Commanders added Payne to the injury report Friday, listing him as questionable with a foot injury. Payne, 29, was diagnosed with a significant injury after injuring his foot in Friday's practice, NFL Media reports. He will undergo an MRI on Sunday to confirm what X-rays showed. Payne has possibly played his final game this season, per NFL Media. Washington drafted Payne with the 13th overall pick in 2018, making him the team's longest-tenured player. He started every possible game from 2020-24 and missed only two games last season. He totaled 14 tackles, five quarterback hits and one sack in six games. Payne has 38 sacks in his career.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jordan Love passes Brett Favre for multi-touchdown games to start season
summary: The Packers have had three starting quarterbacks since Brett Favre replaced Don Majkowski in Week 3 of the 1992 season.
full_text: The Packers have had three starting quarterbacks since Brett Favre replaced Don Majkowski in Week 3 of the 1992 season. Favre is in the Hall of Fame, Aaron Rodgers will get in on the first ballot, and Jordan Love is still crafting his legacy. Love has had some special performances, and some solid runs. His three-touchdown performance on Thursday night gives him the second-longest streak of games with two or more touchdowns to start a season in Packers history, with eight. Rodgers set the Packers record in 2011, with 15 straight games of two or more touchdowns. Favre had seven straight to start the 1995 season. Both won the NFL MVP in those seasons. Love is currently at 25-1 to win the 2026 MVP award. On Thursday night, he completed 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception. For the year, Love currently leads the league in attempts (312), completions (192), yards (2,246), and touchdown passes (16).
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean Payton goes for his 200th career win on Sunday
summary: Broncos coach Sean Payton, with five wins in 2026, now sits one win short of a milestone only 11 other NFL coaches have achieved.
full_text: Broncos coach Sean Payton, with five wins in 2026, now sits one win short of a milestone only 11 other NFL coaches have achieved. Payton's next win will give him 200 for his career, including the postseason. His first crack at No. 200 comes on Sunday against the Chiefs. He has coached 319 games, generating a record of 199-120. He's 189-110 in the regular season and 10-10 in the playoffs. With two more wins, Payton will catch Dan Reeves and Mike Tomlin for 10th on the all-time list. Four more wins after that will put Payton even with Marty Schottenheimer, at 205. Chuck Noll is No. 8 with 209. Paul Brown is No. 7 with 222. Payton, 62, could eventually catch Tom Landry at No. 5, at 270. He's also angling to be the first coach to win a Super Bowl with two different teams. Other coaches currently in position to chase that distinction include Giants coach John Harbaugh and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons sixth-round rookie Anterio Thompson says he was told he'll never play again
summary: Falcons rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson, who has been on the non-football injury list since the start of training camp, has disclosed that his career is over.
full_text: Falcons rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson, who has been on the non-football injury list since the start of training camp, has disclosed that his career is over. Via Marc Raimondi of ESPN, Thompson recently disclosed on social media that he has been told he’ll never play football again , due to a genetic mutation of his spinal cord. Coincidentally, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski was asked about Thompson on Friday, before Thompson's Instagram post circulated. "Mentally, I've been better than anyone would be in my situation," Thompson wrote. "As a football player you know one day you'll have to hang up your cleats but you just hope it's on your own terms. It's hard to explain what it feels like to go through the highest of highs to the lowest of lows in the [sic] matter of seconds." Thompson, who played college football at Washington in 2025, was a sixth-round pick in the 2026 draft.
author: Mike Florio

title: Budda Baker says he's focused on the Cowboys, not trade talk
summary: The trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Cardinals could be sellers.
full_text: ' The trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Cardinals could be sellers. They surely will get calls on safety Budda Baker. The question is: Will they get an offer they can't refuse? "I just live in the present , like today having a great time with [the media], and going to have a great Friday practice," Baker said, while wearing a Halloween mask, via Darren Urban of the team website. "I'm going to just focus on playing the Dallas Cowboys at their stadium." Baker, 30, has totaled 44 tackles, an interception, four pass breakups and a career-best 3.5 sacks this season. He told ESPN this week that he has not asked for a trade, but he hasn't asked not to be traded either. He is under contract through 2027.
author: Charean Williams

title: Video seems to contradict Josh Jacobs's explanation of TD celebration
summary: After Packers running back Josh Jacobs scored his first of two touchdowns on Thursday night, he seemed to celebrate by pretending to be in handcuffs.
full_text: '' After Packers running back Josh Jacobs scored his first of two touchdowns on Thursday night, he seemed to celebrate by pretending to be in handcuffs. That sparked widespread criticism of his apparent effort to trivialize the event that resulted in his May 2026 arrest — an altercation that resulted in a no-contest plea to battery of a female. Jacobs explained the celebration after the game, claiming it was part of a more elaborate display that the TV cameras didn't fully capture, one that had nothing to do with Jacobs's arrest. A more lengthy video of the celebration was surfaced, and it doesn't seem to support Jacobs's explanation. At first, Jacobs has his hands behind his back. Later, Jacobs moves his hands to the front. Teammate Savion Williams seems to unlock the handcuffs that Jacobs says weren't handcuffs. Even if Jacobs is telling the truth, it's a stunning lack of awareness as to how the celebration would be perceived. And his decision to react to the question by complaining that Prime Video showed "fuckin' one second" of the celebration and that the media is "gonna make it something that it wasn’t" is hardly the kind of contrition he should be displaying, given the broader circumstances.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys list Kenny Clark, George Pickens as questionable
summary: The Cowboys added defensive tackle Kenny Clark to the injury report on Friday.
full_text: The Cowboys added defensive tackle Kenny Clark to the injury report on Friday. He had a limited practice with a back injury and is questionable to play Sunday. Defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard (calf) is also questionable. He is in his 21-day return-to-practice window. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (hamstring) does not have an injury designation after a full practice Friday. The Cowboys ruled out wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf). Neither practiced this week. Wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is questionable after a third consecutive limited practice. Safety P.J. Locke (foot), tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) and outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) are also questionable. Rookie safety Caleb Downs (ankle) returned to full participation on Friday and is good to go.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaylen Waddle questionable, RJ Harvey ruled out for Broncos-Chiefs
summary: At this point, it’s still unclear whether or not the Broncos will have receiver Jaylen Waddle for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs.
full_text: At this point, it’s still unclear whether or not the Broncos will have receiver Jaylen Waddle for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. But they will not have two key players. Waddle (chest) has been listed as questionable while running back RJ Harvey (knee) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) have been ruled out. Waddle was limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. The Broncos added Harvey to the report as limited on Thursday and he did not participate on Friday. Waddle leads the team with 276 yards on 26 receptions. Harvey is second on the club in both categories, with 25 catches for 217 yards. He’s also rushed for 87 yards on 24 carries. Defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring), offensive tackle Garrett Bolles (hip), and safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) are also questionable. Receiver Marvin Mims Jr. (ankle), inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) are all off the injury report and set to play.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Commanders add DT Daron Payne to injury report as questionable
summary: The Commanders had already ruled out defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw (knee).
full_text: The Commanders had already ruled out defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw (knee). He missed practice all week. Now they could be without another defensive tackle. The Commanders added Daron Payne to the practice report on Friday with a foot injury that has him questionable to play. Payne was limited in Friday's practice. Tight end John Bates (shoulder), wide receiver Treylon Burks (foot) and defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) are also questionable. All three were limited in Friday's practice. The Commanders added wide receiver Luke McCaffrey (hip) to the injury report as a limited participant Friday, but he has no injury designation. Quarterbacks Jayden Daniels (left elbow) and Marcus Mariota (knee) and wide receiver Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) are good to go as well.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams list Trent McDuffie, Coleman Shelton as questionable
summary: The Rams didn't rule anyone out on their final injury report of the week, but they're not sure they'll have cornerback Trent McDuffie against the Chargers on Sunday.
full_text: The Rams didn't rule anyone out on their final injury report of the week, but they're not sure they'll have cornerback Trent McDuffie against the Chargers on Sunday. McDuffie has been listed as questionable because of a groin injury. McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all three days this week. Center Coleman Shelton (hip) returned for a limited practice on Friday after missing the first two days of the week. He's also listed as questionable. Tight end Colby Parkinson (rib) did not practice at all this week, but he has a chance to play after joining McDuffie, Shelton, and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) with a questionable tag. Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is listed as doubtful. The Rams have Jake McQuaide on the practice squad to fill in for him this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ladd McConkey set to play, Derwin James out vs. Rams
summary: The Chargers will have two of their key receivers for Sunday's game against the Rams.
full_text: The Chargers will have two of their key receivers for Sunday's game against the Rams. First, Ladd McConkey (concussion) is off the injury report and set to play after going through three full practices this week. McConkey was injured against the Chiefs in Week 6 but has recovered after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye. McConkey is second on the team with 13 receptions and 200 receiving yards so far in 2026. Receiver Tre’ Harris (hamstring) is also off the injury report and set to play. While he was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, he was a full participant on Friday. Safety Derwin James (hamstring), defensive back Deane Leonard (concussion), guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), and receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) are all out. Cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) and cornerback Rodney Shelley (hamstring) are both questionable.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Dolphins claim DE Jamree Kromah off waivers
summary: The Dolphins made a roster change a couple of days before their Week 8 game against the Patriots.
full_text: ' The Dolphins made a roster change a couple of days before their Week 8 game against the Patriots. They announced that they have claimed defensive end Jamree Kromah off of waivers. Kromah was cut by the Bears after they traded for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on Thursday. Kromah had two tackles and a tackle for loss while playing 28 defensive snaps for the Bears in two appearances this season. That marked his first regular season action since signing with Chicago as an undrafted free agent in 2024. The Dolphins waived defensive end Rob Beal to make room for Kromah. Beal had 37 tackles and a sack in 27 games for Miami over the last four seasons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders G Jackson Powers-Johnson is questionable for Sunday
summary: The Raiders aren't sure if they'll have one of their starting offensive linemen for Sunday's game against the Jets.
full_text: ' The Raiders aren't sure if they'll have one of their starting offensive linemen for Sunday's game against the Jets. Right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson has been listed as questionable because of a back injury. title: Commanders' Daron Payne suffers season-ending foot fracture, ending any trade speculation
summary: Payne was thought to be a potential trade candidate
full_text:
Commanders defensive lineman Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in practice Friday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported .
It's a bit of a double whammy for Washington, which, at 1-4-1 this season, desperately needs a win coming off a bye Sunday night against the Eagles . Payne, 29, is a crucial part of the Commanders' defense. He has played nearly three-quarters of the team's defensive snaps this season and has one sack, 14 tackles, two tackles for loss and five quarterback hits. His stats only tell a very small part of the story, as he is key defending the run and occupying opposing offensive linemen.
Making matters worse, Payne's fellow interior defensive lineman, Javon Kinlaw , is out with a knee injury. Johnny Newton , who has not played all year with a pec injury is questionable. That leaves the Commanders with Tim Settle and Shy Tuttle as the only interior defensive linemen on the active roster.
Furthermore, this takes a potential trade candidate off the board. Payne, who has played his entire career with the Commanders since being drafted 13th overall in 2018, is in the final year of a four-year, $90 million extension. With Washington struggling, he could have been an attractive target for a defensive tackle-needy team. Instead, he will be sidelined for the rest of the year.
It's yet another tough injury for the Commanders, who have not had left tackle Laremy Tunsil (triceps) all season and lost Terry McLaurin (torn patellar tendon) for the season in Week 6. Quarterback Jayden Daniels missed two and a half games with a dislocated elbow, and guard Sam Cosmi, wide receiver Stefon Diggs and running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (currently on IR) have also missed time. Linebacker Leo Chenal and wide receiver/returner Jaylin Lane are also done for the season.

title: Colts actively engaged in Jonathan Taylor trade talks: Five teams reportedly interested in star running back
summary: The Colts have already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor and are actively engaging with teams about a deal, according to ESPN and NFL Network .
The news comes amid a Colts' fire sale that has seen Indianapolis (2-5) trade two cornerstones this week. The Colts traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick and traded DeForest Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick.
The return stands to be much bigger for Taylor. The Colts have already received at least one offer that includes a second-round pick plus additional compensation, per ESPN. Taylor, who said Thursday he's proud to wear the horseshoe and hasn't requested a trade, remains one of the league's most productive backs. He has twice led the NFL in rushing touchdowns, including last season, and led the league in rushing yards in 2021 on his way to first-team All-Pro honors. He has eight rushing touchdowns through seven games this year, putting him on pace to threaten his career high of 18.
ESPN reports the teams with at least some interest include the Broncos , Packers , Vikings , Giants and Seahawks . Here's how each could fit:
The Packers (5-3) recently got Josh Jacobs back from the commissioner-exempt list, but Green Bay's rushing struggles are reaching historic proportions. Green Bay is last in rushing yards per game (60.6) and yards per rush (2.9). The former is on pace to be the worst since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, the latter on pace to be the second-worst. That has put an enormous weight on quarterback Jordan Love : Currently, nearly 82% of Green Bay's yards have come via the pass, on pace for the highest rate since the merger.
John Harbaugh has fiddled with New York's running back rotation this season but is on the record that he would "love" a bell cow a la Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley on his team. The Giants (4-2-1) lead a wide-open NFC East, and Taylor could not only take the load off new starter J.J. McCarthy but also be a boon; playing next to Jaxson Dart would be an enticing look next year. Cam Skattebo's bounce-back Week 7 performance after getting no touches in Week 6 might have placated previous backfield worries, but clearly New York is willing to poke around for an upgrade.
The Broncos (5-2) sent a first-round pick to Miami for Jaylen Waddle this offseason, though it hasn't really worked out yet. Would they make another big move, this time for a running back? Denver has struggled to muster much on the ground, which has only exacerbated Bo Nix's struggles. Broncos running backs rank 10th in yards before first contact per rush, suggesting good blocking, but 30th in yards after first contact per rush. Rookie Jonah Coleman has impressed but also dealt with injuries. Denver does have an extra fourth-round pick in 2027.
Seattle (4-3) already did business with Indianapolis this week, and perhaps reuniting Nelson with Taylor could be the boost their attempt for a second straight Super Bowl title needs. The Seahawks very much miss Kenneth Walker III , the Super Bowl MVP, and haven't found much on the ground without him. Zach Charbonnet is on his way back, as is first-round pick Jadarian Price , but Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have both had devastating fumbles in the interim. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was with the 49ers when they acquired Christian McCaffrey midseason, so he knows the value of a great top running back.
The Vikings are 6-0, but their 10 touchdowns are the fewest by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions . Minnesota has moved the ball decently but hasn't found the finishing touch to get into the end zone. Taylor has 40 touchdowns over the past three seasons, the third-most in the NFL, and pairing him with a mobile quarterback like Kyler Murray would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Minnesota also has draft capital to spare, including an extra third-round pick, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.

title: Kordell Stewart reflects on whether playing QB for Steelers cost him Hall of Fame career as WR
summary: Stewart showed early signs of promise at receiver before becoming a Pro Bowl quarterback for the Steelers
full_text:
Kordell Stewart achieved his goal of becoming a starting NFL quarterback. But did it cost him a chance at being a Hall of Famer at a different position?
At quarterback, Stewart helped lead the Steelers to AFC Championship game appearances in 1997 and in 2001. Some, however, feel that Stewart may have had a Hall of Fame-worthy career if he had switched to receiver, a move he volunteered to make during his first two seasons in Pittsburgh.
"Everybody in that city, I'm sure the majority probably said I could have gone to the Hall of Fame if I'd have stayed there," Stewart recently told CBS Sports while discussing his new HBO documentary that chronicles his one-of-a-kind NFL journey.
A star quarterback at Colorado, Stewart wanted the chance to compete for the starting job when he entered the NFL in 1995. During NFL Combine interviews, Stewart told the Steelers and other teams that he would be willing to play other positions because he knew that would increase a team's interest in drafting him.
It didn't take long for the Steelers -- who picked him with the 60th overall pick -- to take Stewart up on his offer. Stewart was already having success as a receiver in practice when then-Steelers coach Bill Cowher asked him if he would consider playing other positions for the time being. Stewart agreed, with the understanding that he would eventually get a chance to be the Steelers' quarterback.
An agreement was made, and when Stewart made his NFL debut midway through his rookie season, Cowher listed him as a quarterback/wide receiver.
"And I'll just call you Slash," Cowher recalled telling Stewart at the time.
It didn't take long for Slash to take Pittsburgh by storm. Stewart flourished in that role, which was a key ingredient in the Steelers' AFC championship run. Stewart's emergence as Slash coincided with the Steelers winning eight of their final nine games after a 3-4 start.
Stewart became a nightmare for opposing defensive coordinators, who never knew where he would line up or how he would impact the game. His first NFL touchdown actually came against a Bill Belichick-coached defense.
The most electric WR/QB hybrid in modern NFL history. Kordell Stewart: Slash & Burn now streaming on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zD2jZI1hjq
Stewart scored touchdowns in each of his roles that season, but he made his biggest impact as a receiver.
In his first game, Stewart caught a 27-yard pass in an overtime win in Chicago. He caught a 21-yard pass a week later in a game that helped the Steelers win their final game in Cleveland before the Browns moved to Baltimore.
In Cincinnati a week later, Stewart scored his first touchdown as a receiver while helping the Steelers turn a 31-13 deficit into a 49-31 come-from-behind win. At Green Bay in the regular season finale, Stewart caught six passes against a Packers team that needed to win to make the playoffs (Green Bay won a close game and ultimately got to within a game of the Super Bowl ).
In the AFC Championship game, Stewart gave the Steelers' offense a much-needed boost. On Pittsburgh's final drive of the first half, Stewart converted three third downs on the ground before catching the game's first touchdown to give the Steelers a 10-6 halftime lead. It proved to be a pivotal sequence in Pittsburgh's eventual 20-16 win over the Colts that sent the Steelers to their first Super Bowl since 1979.
Stewart reprised his role as Slash the following season, and despite having more success in that role (he scored 10 touchdowns that included three as a receiver), Stewart felt it was time for Cowher to pay the piper.
Cowher, like Stewart had two years earlier, made good on his promise and named Stewart as the Steelers' new starting quarterback entering the 1997 season. Once again, Stewart quickly had success in his new role. In the process, he helped revolutionize the position as a quarterback who could beat you with both his arm and his legs.
Stewart led the Steelers to a fourth consecutive division title and an AFC Championship game appearance during his first season at quarterback. He made history that year by becoming the first player to throw at least 20 touchdowns and run for at least 10 scores in the same season.
Stewart also became the first player in NFL history to have multiple games with three touchdown passes and two touchdown runs. Bills quarterback Josh Allen is the only player that has since joined Stewart with having multiple games with three touchdown passes and multiple touchdown runs.
Stewart spent the majority of six seasons as the Steelers' starting quarterback. Over that span, Pittsburgh went 48-29 with Stewart as the starter. Stewart helped the Steelers win two playoff games, but there were also two painful losses in AFC championship games that were decided by a combined seven points. In both games, the Steelers lost to the eventual Super Bowl champions.
Stewart occasionally reprised his role at Slash, and whenever he did, he continued to make plays while showing his potential at receiver.
December 15, 1996 at Three Rivers Stadium. The Steelers lost 25-15 against the 49ers but this 42 yard one handed TD reception by Kordell Stewart was the play of the game. pic.twitter.com/KzynIYdteb
Stewart knows that the decision to play quarterback may have cost him a career as a Hall of Fame receiver. For Stewart, though, what he and the Steelers accomplished together during those years was more than worth it. He takes pride in being able to transition from a playmaking receiver into a record-setting quarterback, something that was just as unique then as it would be now.
"I don't think we'll ever have a chance to see that type of player ever again," Stewart said. "I don't think we'll ever have to see someone line up against Merton Hanks, Blaine Bishop, Chris Dishman, and Rod Woodson in the slot, and actually beat those dudes with touchdowns and catching the ball. Then, being cerebral enough coming from that position to be a starting quarterback and beat out the guys who were considered as quarterbacks throughout their entire career, while everyone else is looking at me as a wide receiver."
Slash's skillset as a black mobile quarterback was ahead of its time. #KordellStewart : Slash & Burn premieres tonight at 9 PM EST on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fUWOBFbi1S
How did Stewart do it? By embracing the work that was required to be the starting quarterback of the Pittsburgh Steelers.
"I kept my head down and worked," he said, "and handled myself with a level of dignity and honoring the game and respecting the organization and the city. Dealing with everything with this acronym of sacrifice, leadership, adaptability, standard, and honor.
"I like the city to identify with that. Some won't, and that's OK, but when you ask me what I thought and how I wanted to be perceived, I think that's a Hall of Fame type speech right there."
HBO's new original documentary "Kordell Stewart/ Slash & Burn" is now streaming on HBO Max. It tackles Stewart's career and the devastating rumor that has followed him for decades.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: LOOK: Cardinals' Budda Baker addresses trade rumors while wearing Halloween costume
summary: Baker isn't letting trade speculation spoil his Halloween spirit
full_text:
For several years, Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker has worn a costume to practice around Halloween. Baker continued the tradition on Friday and quickly went viral after fielding questions about his future with the Cardinals while wearing his costume.
It's easy to see why the moment quickly went viral. While Baker gave a standard answer, his appearance while addressing a relatively serious matter was funny ... even if you're a Cardinals fan.
"I just live in the present," Baker responded. "You know, look like today, having a great time with you guys, and gonna have a great Friday practice and just focus on playing against the Dallas Cowboys and trying to get a W at their stadium."
Budda Baker fielding trade deadline questions with a full Halloween costume on is one of the funniest things I’ve ever seen pic.twitter.com/nqzXQCaWHA
Costume aside, Baker's future with the Cardinals is no laughing matter. While the Cardinals would potentially get sizable assets in a trade involving him, it's safe to say that a large portion of Arizona fans would be sad to see him go given his status as one of the greatest players in franchise history.
A lifetime Cardinal, Baker is in the middle of his 10th season in Arizona. He's an eight-time Pro Bowler and has been named to the Pro Bowl each of the last seven years. Baker is also a two-time All-Pro.
Unfortunately for Cardinals/Baker fans, the NFL is a business, and teams in the midst of a bad season (Arizona is 2-5) often trade talented veterans before the trade deadline in exchange for future draft picks. If the Cardinals trade Baker this season, they have until now and November 10 at 4 p.m. ET.
There is, however, a chance that the Cardinals don't trade Baker before the deadline. This isn't the first time that there have been rumblings about his future with the team; he reportedly requested a trade in 2023 , over a year before he signed a lucrative long-term contract with the team. It would also require a team making Arizona a pretty sweet deal for the 30-year-old Baker.
For now, Baker is still a Cardinal. And, based on Friday's press conference, he doesn't appear to be terribly worried about his status in Arizona ahead of the trade deadline.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: CeeDee Lamb says Cowboys have a Cardinals boogeyman: 'They've punched us in the mouth every single time'
summary: Dallas five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb has never beaten Arizona, and they have won eight of the last nine matchups
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys (3-4) have an Arizona Cardinals (2-5) problem they're looking to halt in Week 8. Arizona has won four consecutive games against Dallas as part of a larger span of success that includes wins in eight of the last matchups dating back to 2008.
Cowboys five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , who is in his seventh NFL season in 2026, has never beaten Arizona, losing all four matchups since he was drafted by Dallas in 2020. Why has Dallas struggled so much against the Cardinals? CBS Sports asked Lamb about that and if he has a heightened focus entering the matchup. Lamb's answer? The Cardinals have seemingly wanted it more.
"I've never beaten the Cardinals since I've been in the league. So that's fair to say," Lamb said after practice on Thursday. "I wouldn't say [we have a] heightened focus, but it's definitely a note to take. It's just crazy. We've been very relaxed, and they've punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy.
"Just coming into the game, they're more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o'clock [1 Eastern], Monday night, Sunday night. We played them in primetime; they beat us there. Just coming in and treating them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be. Hats off to them in their prep. We just have to go match them, if not overpower that."
Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer disagreed with his top target's assessment, instead pointing to "the ball." The Cowboys have a -11 turnover margin (15 turnovers to four) across the nine matchups since 2008. In Dallas' "Monday Night Football" home loss in Week 9 last season, the Cowboys committed three turnovers and didn't generate a takeaway. Quarterback Dak Prescott had an interception, and both running back Javonte Williams and tight end Jake Ferguson lost fumbles. That put the Cowboys in a 17-point hole minutes into the second half.
Arizona's win against Dallas in 2025 was the only victory in 12 starts for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett in 2025.  Schottenheimer has a point. Across all three of the Cowboys' wins this season, they have committed zero turnovers. All four of Dallas' losses in 2026 involve at least one turnover.
"I'll disagree with CeeDee a little bit," said Schottenheimer on Friday. "I know why: minus-11 turnover differential in those games. Last year, we were minus-three. So the ball is what this game is going to come down to. I don't think it has to do with energy."
Dallas should be able to stop the slide on Sunday as seven-point home favorites, according to DraftKings Sportsbook. The Cardinals enter Week 8 as the NFL's worst scoring defense, allowing 29.7 points per game. Offensively, Arizona enters Week 8 as the league's worst red zone offense, scoring touchdowns on just 42.9% of its red zone drives.
Dallas enters Week 8 as the NFL's No. 5 scoring offense (27.0 points per game), with new cornerback Joey Porter Jr . helping calm things down for Dallas' defense . There's only one way for the Cowboys to bury their Cardinals boogeyman narrative: just win.
"We got to win," said Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott after practice on Thursday. "They've had our number these last couple of years. Credit to their defense, credit to the way that those guys come in and play and execute. It's a new year. We just have to make sure we go out and take care of business."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter confirms Lamar Jackson will return from ankle injury, start vs. Bills
summary: The two-time MVP hasn't played since Week 4 after suffering a high ankle sprain
full_text:
After a 4-1 start, the Baltimore Ravens have quickly lost ground in what is arguably the NFL's most competitive division. The Ravens have gone from first to last place in the AFC North after dropping their last two games. Both of those games were played without Lamar Jackson , who hasn't played since Week 4 after suffering a high ankle sprain.
But there's good news coming for the Ravens. Jackson will return from his three-plus-game absence and start on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills , Ravens coach Jesse Minter said during his Friday media availability. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz had previously reported that Jackson was expected to play this week.
Jackson himself said Friday that he still feels pain when he plants his foot but described it as "bearable," according to ESPN . Apparently, he can bear it well enough to play for the first time since appearing to injure the ankle on the final play of the first half of Baltimore's win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4.
Jackson, 29, put up solid numbers during the season's first four games. In the games he's played, he's completed a whopping 70.8% of his passes (which is nearly six points higher than his career average) with six touchdowns against just one interception. He's also run for 144 yards and a score while averaging a gaudy 7.6 yards-per-carry, 1.5 yards higher than his career YPC average.
Jackson's return will be a big boost for a Ravens offense that was blanked during the second half of last Sunday's blowout loss to the Bengals . With Tyler Huntley at quarterback, Baltimore led 13-0 at halftime before being outscored 35-0 in the second half.
The 35 points Baltimore allowed in the final 30 minutes tied a franchise mark for points allowed in a second half. It was the most points the Ravens have allowed in a second half since Week 6 of the 1997 season. Baltimore led 21-0 in the first half of that game before being on the wrong side of a 42-34 final score.
On Sunday, Baltimore will face a Bills defense that has struggled this season. Buffalo is currently giving up an average of 28.5 points per game, the third-highest total in the NFL. It's allowed at least 30 points in five of its first six games.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Browns trying to end stunning 38-year drought against Steelers in Week 8 AFC North showdown
summary: A win in Pittsburgh would secure Cleveland's first season sweep of its rival since 1988
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns will be heading to Pittsburgh this weekend to try and pull off something they haven't done in nearly 40 years: A clean sweep of the Steelers.
The Browns beat the Steelers back in Week 4, and if they on Sunday, that will give the Browns their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. That is not a typo. It has been 38 years since the Browns won both regular-season games against the Steelers. The last sweep was so long ago that there's only one player on either team's roster who was even alive when it happened and that's Aaron Rodgers, who at age 42, is the oldest player in the NFL this year.
The Browns finished the sweep with a win Nov. 20, 1988, which came just two weeks before Rodgers' fifth birthday. That was so long ago that the Browns and Steelers played in a division that no longer exists (AFC Central).
Since that sweep back in 1988, the Steelers have absolutely dominated the series. The two teams have played 69 times in the regular season since the sweep and the Steelers have gone 52-17 in those games.
One reason why this series has been so lopsided is because the Browns can't figure out how to win in Pittsburgh, which is where this week's game will be played. The Browns' last win at Acrisure Stadium/Heinz Field came all the way back in 2003 when Tim Couch was their starting quarterback.
Since then, playing in Pittsburgh has been a never-ending nightmare for the Browns. During Cleveland's 22-game losing streak, there have only been six games that have been decided by seven points or less. Every other game has essentially been a blowout.
If the Browns can pull out a win, not only would they pick up their first sweep since 1988 and first win in Pittsburgh since 2003, but they would also improve to 6-2, something they haven't done this century. If you want to stump an NFL fan with some trivia this weekend, just ask them if they know the year of the last time the Browns started 6-2
Since the start of the Super Bowl era in 1966, the Browns have only started the season with a 6-2 record ONE time and that came in 1994 when Bill Belichick was still the head coach. That gives the Browns the NFL record for fewest 6-2 starts since 1966. The Jaguars and Panthers have more 6-2 starts than the Browns, even though those two teams didn't exist until 1995, and the Texans have more 6-2 starts than the Browns, even though they didn't start playing until 2002.
The Browns have gone 28 seasons without a 6-2 start, which is the longest active drought and the second-longest drought in NFL history (The Browns actually hold the record for longest drought, going from 1966 to 1993 without a 6-2 start).
Basically, it's been a long, painful history for the Browns.
The Browns' defense has been good enough to keep them in games over the past few years, but now, they have an offense that's also coming up with big plays, and that's been the big difference.
For one, they have two unstoppable rookie receivers in Denzel Boston (372 yards on the season) and KC Concepcion Jr. (317 yards). Those two have combined to become just the second rookie duo in NFL history to have at least 300 receiving yards each through a team's first seven games.
The Browns raised some eyebrows around the NFL when they selected those two in the NFL Draft back in April and that's mainly because of when they selected them. Concepcion was the 29th overall pick in the draft while Boston was the 39th overall pick, which made the Browns the first team since 1996 to take two receivers in the top 40.
In the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers, the rookie duo caught fire: They combined for nine catches and 154 yards. Concepcion caught a six-yard pass on Deshaun Watson's final completion of the game that set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning 56-yard field goal.
Watson also deserves some credit for Cleveland's resurgence. He's led a game-winning drive in all five of Cleveland's wins, making him just the third quarterback since 1970 to lead a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season, joining Troy Aikman (1990 Cowboys) and Matthew Stafford (2016 Lions).
There's a reason that Mike Tomlin used to say that "the Browns are gonna Browns. The Steelers have dominated this series for almost four decades, but new head coach Todd Monken has changed the culture in Cleveland.
"Browns are gonna Browns f--- that. ... The guys took that to heart." Browns HC Todd Monken at the end of his press conference after a win over the Buccaneers. pic.twitter.com/vo52i2L0om
If Monken can lead his team to Cleveland's first sweep over the Steelers since 1988, the rest of the NFL might have to stop looking at the Browns as a pushover and start taking them seriously as an actual playoff threat.
If the Browns win this game, it could put them on the path to winning the division title, which they haven't won since 1989. The Browns could bury a lot of ugly history with a win on Sunday and they'll try to get it at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+ .

title: Bryce Young and the Panthers' passing game are running into familiar problems, can they be fixed?
summary: Young struggled again as Carolina lost to the Packers and fell below .500
full_text:
The last time the Carolina Panthers appeared in primetime, Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns in a 32-26 win over the Lions . Young was both efficient and impressive, hitting on all the new, creative solutions offensive coordinator Brad Idzik had installed and making some big-time throws needed. An 18-yard sideline dart to Tetairoa McMillan on a third and 14 late in the game epitomized everything that was going right for the Panthers' passing offense, led by a massive step by Young.
By the end of the night, Young was leading the NFL in passing yards.
But that was then, and this is now. After a 27-19 loss to the Packers , the Panthers are 3-4 and have produced back-to-back offensive stinkers. Just four days earlier, they were blown out 43-13 by the Buccaneers , a game in which Young threw two interceptions and took five sacks. Thursday, Young took six sacks and threw a pick.
Teams have bad games and even bad stretches. But this stretch has been particularly worrisome for the Panthers for a bevy of reasons: Young's play, yes, but also a crumbling offensive line and opponents figuring out some of Idzik's and Young's tendencies. Given Young's rocky career path thus far, there are big questions arising, the same big questions that have followed him his entire career. Do the Panthers have answers?
Young's biggest strength has always been his mind. He is terrific at dissecting defenses both pre- and post-snap. This week was always going to be a challenge. Short weeks on the road leave far less time to prepare, and it often becomes a "players, not plays" scenario when it comes to determining a winner; physical skill wins out.
Young, because of some of his physical limitations, has a thin margin for error. And when the Panthers trot out an offensive line like this, especially against a blitz-heavy, disguise-heavy Packers defense, that margin for error completely disappears.
Ekwonu is injured (torn patellar tendon)
Moton is injured (broken leg/ankle)
This group doesn't cut it. Walker was particularly brutal, allowing four pressures and a sack and committing two penalties. Fortner and Freeling allowed three pressures, and Hunt allowed two. In fact, the only players who didn't allow a pressure, according to PFF, were Bullock (who left early with an injury) and Jake Curhan , who was called up from the practice squad.
Injuries have completely destroyed this unit. The Panthers knew they'd be without Ekwonu for most of, if not all of, this season. Walker was supposed to be a suitable replacement. He had been an established starter for the Packers. Instead, his 30 pressures allowed are the most in the NFL.
At the other tackle spot, Moton has been a steady presence for years. But he missed the start of the year with blood clots and then broke his leg and suffered ankle ligament damage that ended his season after two games . Freeling, a first-round pick who was viewed as a project and is coming off a knee injury, has played a ton. He currently ranks 65th out of 71 tackles in PFF's grades (Walker is tied for 58th).
On Thursday, Amazon Prime commentators Kirk Herbstreit and Al Michaels discussed the Panthers trying to "protect" their tackles. But really, there was nowhere to hide and, for Young, nowhere to escape. What is he supposed to do when three offensive linemen -- including both tackles -- get beat immediately?
SWARMED 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/CT4vF4IaUk
Or when Freeling gets beat so easily it's like he was hardly there?
Barryn Sorrell gets the fifth sack of the night for the Packers! CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0MBS9KVmSV
The tackles are far from the only problem. Fortner has given up 18 pressures, six more than any other center. The left guard spot currently belongs to Bullock, who only joined Carolina after not surviving the Ravens ' final cuts.
As such, Young has faced the ...
That's impossible to survive. While he isn't faultless for his sack problems, PFF says the offensive line has been at least partially responsible on 83% of the pressures he's faced, the 10th-highest rate in the NFL.
Perhaps the play most illustrative of this problem was actually one of Young's better plays Thursday. On an RPO throw, Young nearly ripped it to Tetairoa McMillan immediately. The problem? Packers linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper was standing right there. He knew what was coming. Young double-clutched, McMillan worked his way into a tiny sliver of space, and Young fired for a first down.
Still, it showed that one of the solutions Idzik implemented this offseason, these quick-hitting passes, are getting more challenging and less effective.
Bryce Young -- Passes under 2.5 seconds
When you're trying to protect your offensive line, quick throws make sense. But an over-reliance on them makes them too easy to defend. Young threw 20 passes that came out in 2.5 seconds or faster Thursday, the most of the season, and his 40% success rate on these throws was his worst of the season.
Smart opponents are basically saying, "Want to beat us over the top? Prove it." Two of Young's worst games this year have been against the Browns and the Packers, who rank first and third, respectively, in press coverage snaps. The other was against the Buccaneers, who knew they didn't need to press or blitz because they were constantly wreaking havoc up front (42% pressure rate) even without doing so.
There's a game plan here to compress everything in front of Young and see if he can win deep, which he can't under current conditions. Thursday, Young went 1 for 6 on passes 10+ yards downfield and only attempted one pass 20+ yards downfield.
Completions 10+ yards downfield
Using net yards per attempt, Young is on par with Daniel Jones and Jalon Daniels in those three bad games and on par with Drake Maye and Trevor Lawrence in every other game.
The problem? Teams are starting to pick up on the weaknesses.
Young was ninth in net yards per attempt through six weeks (7.4). He's averaging 4.5 net yards per attempt over the past two weeks.
Another problem? Young isn't 100%. He's been on the injury report with a knee issue the past several weeks, and though he hasn't missed any practice time, coach Dave Canales thinks it's impacting him.
"I would say that he certainly doesn't look like he's got that quick, make you miss type of deal, but he was able to create some space for himself," Canales said, per the team's transcript.
Young's sack rate and sack-to-pressure rate are way up, indicators of a lack of protection and a lack of escapability. Opponents will attack each and every weakness relentlessly, and right now, both Young and Carolina have many.
The short answer is yes, but the ceiling is low.
If it feels like every week is a referendum on Young, it's because he walks such a fine line between success and failure. He is not going to overcome suboptimal surroundings consistently. He is very smart and accurate in tight spaces when not under pressure, but he is rarely going to win deep, and his arm-strength issues prevent him from accessing all areas of the field. That's why it feels like defenses are closing in so much. They are challenging Young to win in places he doesn't usually win.
The line has to get better for Young to have any chance. Canales is confident it will.
"I just think it comes down to a protection plan deal for us, because when we give Bryce time he's shown his ability to be able to spread the ball around, distribute it, find accurate throws in traffic and all those things, and I'm confident if we shore that thing up, which we will -- when we shore that part up -- Bryce will be back in his rhythm making the throws that he can."
Idzik will come up with some solutions, too, and a mini-bye here should help. But we've seen throughout Young's career that the ceiling is relatively low. Even at his best, he's a middle-of-the-league quarterback, and those "at his best" stretches are fragile. That much is clearly and obviously on display right now.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Cam Skattebo says he feared amputation after gruesome injury that ended his 2025 season
summary: In a new documentary about his recovery, he also said he had a pregame premonition about his injury
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is coming off his best game of the season, having rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown against the Houston Texans last week. Skattebo had been unceremoniously benched in the previous game, taking just six snaps and recording zero carries following a costly fumble the week before, so it was good to see him get back to form.
Early in the season, Skattebo was running extremely inefficiently and averaged just 3.6 yards per carry over the Giants' first five games. That was perhaps unsurprising when you consider that his 2025 season ended with a right ankle dislocation, an open tibia fracture and a ruptured deltoid ligament. That's a scary injury, and one that can obviously affect a running back's performance, given how important cutting and changing direction are to succeeding at the position.
Skattebo said earlier this year that he had considered retirement in the wake of the injury, and this week he and the Giants released an hour-long documentary detailing his recovery. He revealed more about his situation, including that he was afraid his foot would have to be amputated and that he had a premonition about a potential injury before the game.
"Before the game, I actually had an out-of-body experience," Skattebo said, via GiantsWire . "We were all praying in the showers. I was holding both my teammates' hands. It almost felt like, when we were praying, my body was lifted out of my own body. It was weird. I didn't feel like I was in the present me. I didn't feel like myself."
Once he saw what the injury looked like, he feared doctors would have to amputate his foot.
"When I first got hurt, like I'm asking the doctors, like, they're going to have to cut my foot off," he said, via The New York Post .
"As soon as the doctor touched my foot, I felt pain. He snapped (my ankle) back into place, and it was like, 'A sigh of relief.' Once I got in the X-Ray room, they cut my shoe off, they cut my sock off, I was a half-second from passing out because I had dislocated it so far that the skin ripped."
Skattebo obviously did not get his foot amputated and did not retire, and is now back on the field and looks like the lead back for the Giants — especially after the team cut Najee Harris and placed Tyrone Tracy Jr . on injured reserve. He will need to maintain the improved efficiency he showed against the Texans, but just being back on the field and playing at all is pretty impressive considering the extent of the injury he sustained.
author: Jared Dubin

title: NFL Week 8 schedule: Why you should watch these three underrated games
summary: Here are three games you should watch that people may not be talking about
full_text:
It's Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season, and this is just about the time when the window for teams' playoff possibilities starts to close. We saw some significant results last week, both good and bad.
The Texans losing another and falling to 2-5 raises questions about whether their season is done for. The Seahawks had a very redeeming win, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season in a blowout. Staying in that division, the Rams made things interesting in the standings by getting a check in the win column as well. The Falcons also kept their season hopes trending positive by handing the 49ers their first loss of the season.
This all just proves that even if a team isn't on the top of the playoff picture, their games may end up being the most interesting ones of the week.
Which brings us to why we are here: it's time for the weekly edition of underrated NFL games . Here are three games you should keep on your radar:
Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)
It's the battle of the Los Angeles teams this week, and it always adds an interesting layer when squads who share a stadium face each other. While they both call SoFi home, one team does have to be dubbed the home team and this time it's the Rams, meaning the Chargers will have the visiting locker room in their own stadium.
The Chargers are basically playing for the No. 1 seed at this point. No NFL team has ever started the season 0-6 and made the playoffs. The worst start for a team that ended up in the postseason was by the 1992 San Diego Chargers, who went 0-4 and finished 11-5.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh is on the hot seat and needs to get his team looking somewhat better if he wants to keep his job, and 0-7 doesn't look great to front offices.
The Rams are also not off to the best start, though it seems amazing compared to their Week 8 opponent. There are many 3-4 teams in the league that are in the playoffs, and Super Bowl chances seem slim, but that's not the case for the Rams.
Despite their wildly underwhelming start, they still have the fifth-best odds of winning the Super Bowl (+1100), per DraftKings Sportsbook. If they fall to the no-win Chargers, however, those odds may plummet. This is a big game for both teams, as one looks to avoid going 0-7 and the other fights to reach .500.
Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
We know how much I love divisional games, because they are the most unpredictable, have the most history and carry the most weight. The Dolphins are 1-5, so this likely won't affect the final divisional standings between these two teams, but it could have a significant impact elsewhere.
The Patriots could still win the AFC East, though they are behind the Bills , they did win their first head-to-head against Buffalo. New England retook their AFC East throne last year, after a few years of the Bills getting that hat and t-shirt feeling when Tom Brady left. If the records are close down the line, these divisional games will mean a lot, and right now the Patriots need that boost.
The other interesting thing about this game is that, even though the Patriots are on paper a better team in every category, they historically struggle in Miami. The Patriots have lost five of their last six games in Miami. Will the Patriots lose to the Dolphins? Most likely not, but it could get closer than people think; divisional games tend to do that.
The Patriots are looking to bounce back from a 30-24 loss against the Chicago Bears . They beat themselves in the game numerous times and an easier opponent will be a good test of whether they can correct those mistakes and look dominant enough to be a threat in the AFC.
Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)
The NFC South includes the 3-3 Panthers, 3-4 Atlanta Falcons, 2-5 Buccaneers and 2-5 Saints.
This game will likely have significant implications for the divisional rankings. This is also a matchup between two teams who struggled in the beginning of the year and have found a resurgence. The similarities don't end there; both teams had quarterbacks sidelined for multiple weeks, with the Falcons' Michael Penix Jr . sidelined while recovering from an ACL injury and the Bucs' Baker Mayfield sidelined due to a thumb injury.
The Falcons are coming off a huge win against the San Francisco 49ers, handing them their first win. The Bucs are coming off a win against the Panthers. I think these teams will have a lot of fight in them this week and it will make for a very competitive game.
