title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: One position of need and potential options for all 32 teams
summary: Following Chicago's blockbuster deal for Jeffery Simmons, contenders and sellers across the league have less than two weeks to reshape their rosters
full_text:
Less than two weeks remain until the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10 at 4 pm ET. Each team has one or two more games to gather additional intel on whether they should be buyers, sellers or hold steady.
Some teams are decidedly out of the postseason race, whereas others are being aggressive to facilitate a deep playoff run. An example with teams at opposite ends of the spectrum: Tennessee elected to send All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a trade package that included two first-round picks.
Who could be dealt next in a stunning move? Below is one position each team should target, as well as potential options.
Cincinnati has been linked to a potential trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , but aside from Taylor, linebacker aid would likely have a greater impact on the roster. The Bengals have given a long runway to youngsters Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter , but they would benefit from a more stable veteran who would also improve depth. Defensive tackle improvement takes some of the burden off the linebackers.
Safety was another consideration.
Potential options : Jordyn Brooks , Dolphins; Daiyan Henley , Chargers
Edge rusher and tight end have been the two positions most commonly associated with the Browns . The team is unlikely to over-leverage themselves this season and risk their long-term goals. That said, trades involving players with future control make the most sense.
At edge rusher, they have been able to get contributions from free agents off the street, like Sam Williams and Derek Barnett . Although Blake Whiteheart has had some good moments blocking, depth in that area is a greater need.
Potential options : Dallas Goedert , Eagles; Tip Reiman , Cardinals
The Ravens are one of the franchises most hampered by injuries each year. The return of Lamar Jackson should revitalize Baltimore's playoff hopes, but secondary help is also important.
Potential options : Riq Woolen, Eagles; Donte Jackson , Chargers; Alontae Taylor , Titans; Amik Robertson , Commanders; Nahshon Wright , Jets
After trading away Joey Porter Jr. , Pittsburgh was left with Jamel Dean , Asante Samuel Jr . and Daylen Everette for those starting boundary roles. They may be able to get by this season, but if the plan is to maximize this window with Aaron Rodgers , then they may want more reliable options.
Safety would be another position of interest. Wide receiver has garnered significant discussion but, at some point, the team has to trust the players they have already invested so heavily in.
Potential options : Riq Woolen, Eagles; Donte Jackson, Chargers; Alontae Taylor, Titans; Amik Robertson, Commanders; Nahshon Wright, Jets
Alec Pierce was a top-dollar investment in the offseason, but the team fell out of the AFC South race before he was able to fully recover from an injury. It now sounds as though Josh Downs is on the trade block, so who will Daniel Jones be throwing to apart from tight end Tyler Warren ?

title: Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, make other defensive changes after Packers loss
summary: Evero has had the league's No. 30 scoring defense (26.3 points per game) after four years in Carolina
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers made a rare, in-season coaching change Friday morning by firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. Carolina also let go of defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley, and defensive line coach Todd Wash will serve as interim DC and call the team's defensive plays.
The Panthers' 27-19 road defeat on "Thursday Night Football" to the Green Bay Packers proved to be the last straw for Evero. In Week 7, Carolina lost by 30 points to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , marking the third-most points allowed in a home game in franchise history. The Panthers also allowed a whopping 59 points in their 2026 opener, a 59-37 defeat against the Chicago Bears . Those 59 points allowed are the most surrendered in a single game in Panthers franchise history.
Despite facing a Packers team with the NFL's worst rushing offense, the Panthers failed to contain Packers quarterback Jordan Love, who had to throw the ball all over the yard for Green Bay to win on Thursday. He threw for 288 yards, three touchdowns and an interception on 30-of-41 passing.
Panthers announce changes to defensive coaching staff https://t.co/x8rbGApRiN
Evero's unit struggled almost across the board in his four seasons running the Panthers defense. The lone bright spot was Carolina's pass defense, where they allowed the fourth-fewest passing yards per game (201.1) since 2023.
Third-down conversion rate allowed
Red zone touchdown rate allowed
Evero wasn't anywhere close to having his ideal secondary in the Thursday night loss at Lambeau Field. Cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad), Mike Jackson (groin) and Akayleb Evans (knee/triceps) were all on injured reserve in Week 8.
Carolina hopes this defensive shakeup will be enough to repeat as NFC South champions in 2026. It won the division with an 8-9 record in 2025, and it is currently tied with the Atlanta Falcons , who are also 3-4, atop the division. Atlanta can take sole possession of first place in the division with a win at Tampa Bay on Sunday.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cowboys already won 2026 NFL trade deadline with Joey Porter Jr. trade
summary: In Porter Jr.'s three games with Dallas, he profiles as the league's best cornerback
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The 2026 NFL trade deadline isn't until Nov. 10, but the Dallas Cowboys can already claim to be one of the league's victors thanks to their acquisition of cornerback Joey Porter Jr .
Dallas traded a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers in the middle of the night between Sept. 30 and Oct. 1 after contract talks fell apart between the 26-year-old cornerback and Pittsburgh. The Cowboys knew they had to do something after a 1-2 start to their 2026, and the trade for Porter Jr. has gone exactly how owner and general manager Jerry Jones could have hoped for.
Porter Jr. profiles as the NFL's No. 1 cornerback in his three games with Dallas this season. Entering Week 8, Porter Jr. ranks first in the NFL in completion percentage allowed (18.2%), passing yards allowed (10) and pass yards per attempt allowed (0.9) among the 254 players with at least 10 passes thrown their way.
The Houston Texans didn't throw toward him once on his 19 coverage snaps in the Cowboys' 34-30 road win. He then missed "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a game Dallas lost 24-16, because of a stomach bug . Porter Jr. returned to face the Green Bay Packers on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6, and he didn't allow a catch on the five times Jordan Love threw his way on his 25 coverage snaps in a 23-13 defeat. On "Monday Night Football" against the Philadelphia Eagles , he allowed his first two catches of the year for a total of 10 yards on the six times quarterback Tanner McKee threw Porter Jr.'s way on his 30 coverage snaps.
"I love it man. I love it when we have a player like that who you can just throw on anybody's top guy, and then just say 'if you're going to beat us, beat us with that guy on him.' Lately, he's done a great job," Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb said after practice on Thursday. "I don't think he's had a completion on him yet. I don't know the facts behind that, but just off what I've seen, when the ball is thrown his way, it somehow ends up on the ground. Soon enough it's going to be in his hands."
Porter Jr. knows exactly how many completions he has surrendered this season: two. Both of them were against the Eagles in Week 7. The first was a five-yard gain to Philadelphia tight end Dallas Goedert for five yards on a third-and-6, and the second one was a five-yard gain to Eagles first-round rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon on a second-and-20. He is still seething about both of those completions even though it's past the "24-hour rule" NFL players will cite as the amount of time they have to process the previous week's game before moving on to prepare for the upcoming week's game.
"Two little 5-yard outs or whatever. I was pissed about it. … As a DB, you never want to give up anything," Porter Jr. said after practice on Wednesday . "I really hold myself to a high standard when I'm on the field. I definitely don't want to give up any passes to anybody I don't think I should be giving up passes to."
Completion percentage allowed
Pass yards per attempt allowed
Passer rating against as primary defender
Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker knows he'll soon be talking to Porter Jr. about teams simply deciding to avoid throwing his way for the vast majority of Dallas' games. It's a talk he's had to have with the likes of All-Pro corners he has coached in previous stops like Denver Broncos 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Pat Surtain II and Philadelphia Eagles 2025 first-team All-Pro Quinyon Mitchell .
"I've coached guys where it gets to that point, but then you're going to play certain teams who have a receiver where they don't care if Deion [Sanders] came out of retirement to go cover him," Parker said on Thursday. ... "So he knows that because as soon as you're playing in that way, and you think that you're not getting those targets, you're getting those targets. And so you have to stay aggressive, you have to stay dominant, your technique has to be perfect every play. Corner is one of those positions where you could have 99 perfect snaps, and that one could cost us. So that focus level and that intensity has to remain, and he's [Porter Jr.] done a good job of maintaining that."
Whether it's erasing a top-flight wide receiver from the game through teams deciding not to throw at him or having a flurry of action come his way, Porter Jr. has fun because he knows his opponent isn't. He had chances to defend Packers wide receiver Christian Watson , who ranks seventh in the NFL with 595 receiving yards, and Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden , who ranks 10th in the NFL with 512 receiving yards, and he didn't allow a catch on five targets. That's the most fun he's had this season.
"That's my whole job. I get any type of satisfaction when I get the opponent upset or whatever they're going through," Porter Jr. said. ... "It's both. I enjoy when I get games where they try me like the Packers game. I had fun because I got a lot of targets. I don't really get that often. So when you're in the kitchen and in the fire like that, it's kind of fun to show off your talents."
Hearing Porter Jr. talk like that and seeing him trash talk opponents' top receivers on the field is quite the juxtaposition from his off-field persona. In the locker room, Porter Jr. maintains a low profile while opening up to his new teammates. Joey Porter, Porter Jr.'s father, who was a four-time Pro Bowl linebacker and member of the 2000s All-Decade team, was known for his fiery on-field demeanor. Porter Jr. channels his dad on the field but enjoys relaxing off of it.
"Ever since I was a kid, it's been that comparison. I'm like my mom on the outside, but when I get on the field, I'm kind of like my dad," Porter Jr. said. "I'm cool, calm and collected for the most part, but when I'm on the field, I turn it on a little bit to try to be an energizer and be there for teammates as much as possible."
The Cowboys are already enjoying Porter Jr.'s desire to "run to the smoke" on the field while bolstering what has been an up-and-down pass defense in 2026.
"I think you watch him from afar. I think his personality, he's a real laid-back dude, but on the field when he crosses those white lines, he runs to the smoke," Parker said. "So that's what we value with him is he has an energy about himself. He affects others with his energy and his play. Then off the field, he's very kind of low-key, but when he steps on the field, he turns into a different person."
Dallas four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has already noticed a dramatic uptick in his performance since Porter Jr's in-season arrival. Williams leads all NFL defensive tackles in tackles for loss with nine in 2026, and seven of the nine have come since Porter Jr's Cowboys debut in Week 4. The Cowboys have also allowed under 24 points in three straight games, something they didn't do in either of the two prior seasons.
"He's a baller. I joke with him and tell him all the time 'I've been playing better since he got here, so he's the reason I've been playing better,'" Williams said after practice on Thursday. "He's a baller man. He brought energy. He brought swag. Just the confidence he has when he is on an island by himself is unbelievable man. The player that he is is great to have on our team."
The scariest part of the NFC East and the rest of the Cowboys' opponents is that Porter Jr. produced like the league's top cornerback while still learning both Dallas' playbook and his teammates. Now, his new-team adjustment period is over from a schematic perspective, meaning Porter Jr. could be even better going forward. For the cost of what's essentially a third-round pick (the sixth-round pick in 2027 and the second-round pick in 2028), Jones gave his team an All-Pro-caliber, No. 1 cornerback. That makes the Cowboys the 2026 NFL trade deadline's undisputed winner with a couple of weeks to go.
"I wouldn't say I'm going through the growing pains…

title: Steelers legend Kordell Stewart changes narrative on his NFL career in new HBO documentary
summary: Stewart wants his career to be remembered for what happened on the field
full_text:
For NFL fans of a certain age, Kordell Stewart is remembered as an exciting player who starred as "Slash" before becoming a Pro Bowl quarterback, leading the Pittsburgh Steelers to two AFC Championship game appearances in the late '90s and early '00s. That's how Stewart wants to be remembered.
He doesn't, however, want his career to be defined by a rumor that nearly derailed his career and now takes center stage in HBO's new documentary, "Kordell Stewart/Slash & Burn."
"I just wanted people to appreciate my experience of being a Steeler in Pittsburgh," Stewart recently told CBS Sports. "Not appreciate it from the standpoint of liking, disliking, but just identify it for what it really was. I thought that, truth be told, it was arguably one of the best runs that I can think of where I was able to do so much on the football field that was different than most.
"I had my ups, you know. I had my downs. I never complained. I never blamed. All I did was just work. ... I would like to say I had a lot of success in Pittsburgh, and we had some failures. You know, I'm a glass half full guy. I'm always about being objective and transparent, but also real."
For Stewart, what was real was an exciting, two-year stint playing quarterback/receiver/running back/punter (yes, even punter) and six seasons as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback. The fiction, however, included an unfounded rumor that Stewart had been caught engaging in lewd activity with another male in a city park.
The rumor, started by a local police officer, came out just two days after an ugly loss during the 1998 season, a loss that ended with a fan calling Stewart a racial slur and throwing beer at him as he was walking off the field.
While there was no merit to the rumor, it lingered over Stewart and the Steelers, who staggered through a 7-9 season.
Things got worse before they got better. Stewart was benched in 1999 and briefly returned to his role as Slash. After starting the 2000 season on the bench, Stewart returned to the starting lineup with the Steelers sitting at 0-3. With Stewart at the helm, Pittsburgh went 9-4 that season. He was the last quarterback that season to defeat the Ravens and their historically dominant defense.
Stewart and Co. carried that momentum into the 2001 season. That year, Stewart piloted Pittsburgh to a 13-3 record, the team's best record since 1978. He set a single-season franchise record for completion percentage, was named to the Pro Bowl and finished fourth in league MVP voting. He was also named the Steelers' MVP.
The Steelers dethroned the Ravens in the AFC divisional round, but they were defeated at home by the eventual Super Bowl champion Patriots (who were later punished for stealing opponents' signals, including Pittsburgh's ) in the AFC Championship game. The loss hurt, but that season was nonetheless validation for Stewart after all he had been through the previous four years.
"Oh, it was the greatest," Stewart said of that '01 season. "You know how bad I wanted to go to the Super Bowl that year? Because of all that I had to go through with that rumor and just people doubting me, telling me what I couldn't do and telling me what I should do and not appreciating what I was doing. ... And we came so close."
Both of Stewart's best seasons (1997 and 2001) ended in AFC Championship games. In both games, the Steelers lost close games to the eventual Super Bowl champions led by iconic quarterbacks in John Elway and Tom Brady .
"Looking back on it, I'm not going to say I accept it," Stewart said. "But hey, if those are the two guys [I lost to], I don't think that's too bad."
Those losses are part of Stewart's story in Pittsburgh, but they aren't the story. In Stewart's case, the destination was truly the journey.
You'd be hard-pressed to find a more exciting season than the Steelers' 1997 campaign, Stewart's first as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback. That season, the Steelers overcame deficits of 21-0 (in Baltimore), 21-7 (against Denver) and were 3-0 in overtime games. That was also the season when then-Steelers coach Bill Cowher nearly tackled a Jaguars player on "Monday Night Football."
Individually, it was an historic season for the then-25-year-old Stewart. He became the first player in NFL history to throw 20 touchdowns and run for 10 scores in the same season. Stewart also became the first player to throw three touchdowns and run for two scores in multiple games.
Stewart was part of Pittsburgh's prolific offensive trio that also included Jerome Bettis and Yancey Thigpen. That season, Bettis ran for 1,665 yards, the second-highest single-season total in Steelers history. Thigpen set a then-single-season franchise record for receiving yards (1,398).
The Steelers' most memorable game that season came in Week 16, a late afternoon game in New England. Against the defending AFC champions, Pittsburgh overcame 14-0 and 21-13 deficits to pull off a stunning, 24-21 win in overtime. Pittsburgh forced overtime after Stewart led a drive that included a fourth-and-7 completion, a touchdown pass on third-and-goal and a successful two-point conversion.
In overtime, Stewart, under duress, completed a 41-yard pass that set up the game-winning field goal.
"In the pros, there was not a better moment in my career," Stewart said.
OTD 1997 #Steelers #Patriots @KSlash10 leads Pittsburgh down the field for a touchdown late and gets the 2 point conversion to send the game to OT. Johnson would kick the winning FG giving the #Steelers their 3rd OT win of the season. 24-21 #HereWeGo pic.twitter.com/iSD13ZV5ui
Moments like that, Stewart said, are what he hopes Steelers fans remember when they think about his career, one that he believes will eventually be immortalized in the Steelers Hall of Honor.
"For me, playing ball in that city and the things that I had to go through, I think that would really vindicate and cap off a successful run in Pittsburgh," he said. "I think it will do a lot of people proud once that day actually comes. But it's gonna happen, and I'm gonna be here to see it."
HBO's new original documentary "Kordell Stewart/ Slash & Burn" is now streaming on HBO Max. It tackles Stewart's career and the devastating rumor that has followed him for decades.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Josh Jacobs explains controversial touchdown celebration vs. Panthers that seemed to mimic arrest
summary: Jacobs says the celebration was a reference to a gospel song titled "Break Every Chain"
full_text:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was recently reinstated from the commissioner's exempt list after serving a six-game stint on the list. He was there in the wake of disturbing domestic violence allegations stemming from an offseason incident, but has been back on the field for the last two games.
On Thursday night, Jacobs scored a short rushing touchdown against the Carolina Panthers and, during his celebration, appeared to put his hands behind his back as though he were being arrested and handcuffed. At least, that's how many observers saw it.
TOUCHDOWN PACKERS 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/JGV2fIEObP
He was asked about it following the game, and Jacobs said the celebration was not a reference to his being arrested, but instead to a gospel song titled "Break Every Chain."
"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said, referring to the Amazon Prime broadcast. "It was one second that they just saw me. Anyways, me and (wide receiver Savion Williams ), we came up with the celebration, if they would've seen the whole celebration.
"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was gonna thank God. That's what I did last week. Second one was gonna be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was gonna be the next celebration. It's just a correlation. But like I said, the media's gonna run with it. They're gonna make it something that it wasn't. But it is what it is."
A longer video of the celebration shows Williams running over to Jacobs and seemingly unlocking the chains on Jacobs' wrists, after which Jacobs breaks free.
The full TD celebration in question: https://t.co/jUhME09rjn pic.twitter.com/xMu1702t1f
Jacobs' explanation seems reasonable, if you see the full video and know the context and content of the gospel song in question. But it's also reasonable that people would assume, based on what they saw on Prime, that the gesture was a reference to his arrest. (It wouldn't be the first time a player has celebrated a touchdown that way, after all.) The confusion is understandable, and probably not entirely a media creation.
Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, battery and damage to property, from an arrest in May after police responded to his home following a domestic violence incident. He later pleaded no contest to the charges in September, resolving the court case. He also filed an action seeking to prevent the public release of evidence related to the case, including alleged video of the incident.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Deshaun Watson vs. Steelers' suffocating secondary: How pivotal AFC North duel will be won
summary: How Watson attacks Pittsburgh's zone coverage will be crucial
full_text:
First place in the AFC North is on the line in Week 8 between a team used to these stakes, the reigning division champion Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2), and a newcomer to these types of games, the Cleveland Browns (5-2).
It's been a long time since this matchup meant this much. The Steelers' and Browns' Week 8 game this season possesses the third-best combined record (10-4, .714 winning percentage) entering a matchup this late into the season in the last 50 years. After Cleveland defeated Pittsburgh 27-24 on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 4, it now has a chance to sweep the Steelers in the regular season for the first time since 1988. That's the longest regular-season sweep drought (34 seasons) for any divisional matchup since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
So, where could this matchup between two hard-hitting defenses and battle-seasoned quarterbacks in Pittsburgh's Aaron Rodgers and Cleveland's Deshaun Watson be won? Let's take a closer look.
After struggling on and off the field for the vast majority of his five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million contract, Watson has begun to give the Browns some value. He is just the third quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season, along with Troy Aikman (1990) and Matthew Stafford (2016). Watson produced at least three completions and 30 yards on all five of his game-winning drives this season.
In Cleveland's latest comeback, a 27-24 win against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7, the Browns trailed 14-0 in the first quarter, marking the team's largest comeback win since 2023. Watson had his most prolific game yet as a Brown with 308 yards passing, his most since Week 17 of the 2020 season, and he snapped a streak of 25 consecutive starts without 300 yards through the air.
So how will the Steelers slow down a reinvigorated Watson? Well, they entered Week 8 with the league's No. 5 scoring defense (19.7 points per game allowed) and the league's No. 6 total defense (303.7). The matchup that will decide this showdown will be how Watson pilots the Browns' passing game against the Steelers' zone coverage.
Pittsburgh runs zone at the fourth-highest rate in the NFL , 82.2% of the time, per TruMedia, and it is allowing the ninth-lowest success rate in the league (42.2%) when running zone coverage, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. When the Steelers specifically utilize their Cover 3 zone, their success rate allowed decreases to 37.2%, the sixth lowest in the NFL. Of Pittsburgh's seven interceptions in 2026, four have occurred in Cover 3, tied for the league lead.
However, Watson's 49.4% passing success rate against zone coverage is tied for the fourth-best among qualified quarterbacks this season. The good news for Pittsburgh is that success hasn't typically come from big plays, as his 10.6% explosive play rate vs. Cover 3 is the sixth-lowest in the NFL. That means the Steelers can allow a few papercuts, but they should be able to keep everything in front of them when facing a physically diminished version of the three-time Pro Bowler, thanks to the litany of injuries he has suffered in his Browns career.
Whoever wins the battle of Watson vs. the Steelers' zone coverage unit will likely dictate which team will sit atop the AFC North standings entering Week 9.

title: Jordan Love picks Panthers apart; Christian Watson's midgame hospital trip; top 50 MLB free agents
summary: Plus, predictions for this weekend's college football and NFL games
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
With the World Series complete and the book closed on the 2026 MLB season, it's just about time for the Hot Stove. This offseason will be defined by collective bargaining negotiations between MLB and the MLBPA, and the nearly certain lockout that seems destined to begin in December casts a ton of uncertainty over free agency. But players will move at one point or another. So who's on the market? We ranked the top 50 free agents .
The No. 1 available player is no secret. If you follow baseball even somewhat closely, you probably know that Tarik Skubal is the biggest prize. Expect the top World Series contenders to be in play for his services. Behind him is a mix of reigning stars and incoming international standouts. One of the players in that latter group you should know is Teruaki Sato , the NPB Triple Crown winner. Our Mike Axisa has the scouting report on the third baseman.
Closing out the rankings is a tier of left-handed pitchers who should fill out the back end of whichever rotation they land in.
47. LHP Matthew Boyd 48. LHP David Peterson 49. LHP Robbie Ray 50. LHP Patrick Sandoval
Week 9 delivers another light slate with only two ranked matchups and no top 10 showdowns. That doesn't mean this week is a complete nothingburger, though. Every game for College Football Playoff hopefuls from this point forward is meaningful, and if last week taught us anything, it is that a lack of top 25 battles is the recipe for a number of upsets .
It's also that time of year when conference title races heat up. This far out from championship weekend, there are more scenarios than the mind can comprehend . But the permutations will decrease with each week, and some teams are bound to fall out of the hunt on Saturday.
One team that might not need to worry about losing to an unranked foe is No. 11 Texas . Tom Fornelli's Lock of the Week shows how the Longhorns might not need many points to defeat Mississippi State .
Here are our picks for every key matchup:
It's hard to say that Lamar Jackson and Josh Allen can ever truly upset one another, because they are arguably the two best quarterbacks in football, and their teams are always generally very good. But one side is a three-point favorite over the other in their Week 8 meeting, so if the Ravens go on the road and take down the Bills , it would qualify as an upset. And guess what? A bevy of our NFL experts think it will happen.
Tyler Sullivan would not be surprised if Jackson shows no rust in his return. The two-time MVP is expected to be in the lineup for the first time in a month after he missed three games with an ankle sprain, and if he is fully healthy, he could return to the same career-best form he showed early in the season. title: NFL's 'scariest' good, bad teams: Why Seahawks strike fear, Titans fans should be terrified
summary: With Halloween arriving, these teams sure are spooky
full_text:
It's the last week of October, which means spooky season is in full effect. Whether you're dressing up, partying, handing out candy, watching scary movies and visiting haunted houses, or partaking in none of the Halloween festivities on Saturday, the NFL season will continue rolling Sunday — a great way to enjoy all that leftover candy.
With the season nearly halfway done, we know which teams are trending toward the postseason and which ones aren't. But which teams are truly scary in a good way — no opponent wants to see them — or scary bad to the point their own fans want to hide their eyes?
We break down the nine scariest teams, six scary good, three scary bad, this season.
Yes, the reigning Super Bowl champions still belong here, even if they're "only" 4-3, and a 20-3 domination of the Chiefs should be all the reason you need. Even their defense is called the "Dark Side," and any unit that combines Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy up front with safety/weapon Nick Emmanwori and star cornerback Devon Witherspoon should strike fear in opponents. Sam Darnold has had some turnovers that make Seahawks fans hide their eyes, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba is scary enough to keep any defensive coordinator up at night. Overlook last year's champs at your own peril.
The offense may not strike fear in many opponents' hearts, but that defense? Downright terrifying, especially for quarterbacks. Brian Flores' unit blitzes on 71% of opponents' dropbacks, which is 27 percentage points higher than the second-highest rate. The Vikings also own the best sack rate in the NFL (10.6%). Only one team has scored more than 16 points on this defense, which might as well be the Purple People Eaters 2.0. And just when you think you have the offense under control, Justin Jefferson can produce a big play anytime, anywhere. If Kyler Murray can settle in, this team will be frighteningly good, and with blitzes that will give even the most poised quarterbacks a jump scare or two.
Could we really get another installment of the Reign of Terror from Kansas City? Looking for his fourth Lombardi Trophy already, Patrick Mahomes has been impressive early this season after returning from a torn ACL. Kenneth Walker III has been the best offseason addition by any team, able to seemingly disappear in a pile of would-be tacklers and reappear down the field. His seven carries of 20+ yards are tied for most in the NFL. Steve Spagnuolo's defense may be young, but his cornerback tandem of Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams can make opponents feel like they can't escape anywhere. The Chiefs need more firepower in the passing attack, but everyone knows by now that Mahomes is the scariest of sights come the postseason.
The 49ers ' injury report makes it look like the team survived a month full of terror, but after the bye week, Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel, and a host of other standouts could be on their way back. And no one will want to see this offense in full gear. Brock Purdy and mad scientist play caller Kyle Shanahan can expose any defense's weakness, and no one wants to mess with George Kittle or Trent Williams in the trenches. On defense, newly acquired game-wrecking defensive lineman DeForest Buckner makes San Francisco a lot scarier, too.
Simply put, we have evidence that Josh Allen is an alien who's come to take over planet Earth.
How did Josh Allen make this TD pass to Keon Coleman? BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CNLw6KW2tC
If you cannot stop the run game, the Bears will hammer you over and over again, with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai proving to be double trouble. But what gets really scary is when Caleb Williams starts doing his thing. Always capable of using dark arts to finagle his way out of trouble and making a big play, Williams has gotten terrifyingly accurate this year, too. Oh, and there aren't many scarier sights along the defensive line than newly acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who will have opposing offensive linemen quaking in their cleats.
The Chargers won 11 games in back-to-back years, but this team is a perfect example of how scary expectations can be. Mike McDaniel was a highly anticipated addition as offensive coordinator, but Justin Herbert's play has been hard to watch. Add in injuries along one of the NFL's worst offensive lines and struggling pass catchers all over the place, and Herbert is doomed. The echoes of Jim Harbaugh saying, "Who's got it better than us?" haunt the nightmares of any Bolts fan this season. In the midst of a brutal stretch of the schedule, it might get worse before it gets better.
The Titans hoped a new coach, a new offensive coordinator and new weapons would help Cam Ward , but here they are with a 1-6 record and Ward having thrown for over 200 yards just once this season. Tennessee might have a bright future, in part thanks to the two first-round picks they acquired for Simmons, but without its best defensive player, this team could continue to spiral for the rest of the season. Can Ward help them escape the nightmarish run of quarterbacks they've been on? Nashville's known for country music, but this has been a sad-song franchise for quite a while.
The Colts are in the scariest situation of them all. Just a year ago, the Colts traded two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner . Now, they're selling at the trade deadline and tanking ... without their 2027 first-round pick. If the season ended today, Indianapolis would have the seventh pick ... and send it to the Jets . Horrifying. The Colts just fired GM Chris Ballard, Daniel Jones keeps turning the ball over in truly disgusting ways, and there's no telling who will still be on this team come Nov. 11, when the trade deadline has passed. The Colts have dug themselves a deep, deep hole, and who knows how long it will take for them to escape?

title: NFL Week 8 bold predictions: Jared Goff tears up Vikings D and Justin Herbert plays a clean game?
summary: Plus, an AFC South running back has a huge game, and Jets WR Garrett Wilson reconnects with Geno Smith a week after sideline shouting match
full_text:
Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 8 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea.
With the Green Bay Packers ' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers , they prevailed to 5-3 despite having under 500 rushing yards as a team (485) this season. Green Bay is the first team ever to have a winning record through eight games while also rushing for under 500 yards. They are also the third team since 1950 with no individual players with 50-plus rushing yards in a game through that span. The Packers' ability to continue to win without any semblance of offensive balance is simply unprecedented.
What other astounding things can happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 8 slate on Halloween weekend? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's last undefeated team, but it's not because of their offense. They have scored the fewest touchdowns (10) during a 6-0 start since the 1934 Detroit Lions . Minnesota is 6-0 because defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unit is a horror movie for opposing offenses.
The Vikings defense leads the NFL in the following statistics:
However, Lions five-time Pro Bowl quarterback Jared Goff will overcome his struggles against the Vikings to light Minnesota up for 250-plus passing yards and three-plus touchdowns while being sacked no more than once. In each of his last two games against the Vikings, Goff was sacked five times each.
This time will be different because Goff is on an all-time heater to start the 2026 season. He enters Week 8 leading the NFL in passing yards per game (298.0), touchdown-to-interception ratio (14-0) and passer rating (112.5). Goff's 223 throws without an interception are the most through the first six games of a season in NFL history. His 14 touchdowns without an interception are also tied for the most in NFL history in that span, along with Russell Wilson in the 2019 season. Goff has never played better, and he'll stay locked in to shred the Vikings and hand them their first loss of the season.
Entering Week 7, it looked like Tennessee Titans Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard was washed up at the age of 29. He was averaging just 58.2 rushing yards per game and 4.0 yards per carry with just one rushing touchdown. But against the Cleveland Browns , Pollard turned back the clock to run for 129 yards and a career-high three rushing touchdowns.
On Sunday, at the Cincinnati Bengals , Pollard will do it again, rushing for over 120 yards and multiple scores. Yes, the Bengals are a much-improved defense after completely remaking their defensive line with the additions of three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence , two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jonathan Allen , Super Bowl champion edge rusher Boye Mafe, and rookie second-round pick edge rusher Cashius Howell .
In 2025, Cincinnati ranked as the league's No. 30 scoring defense (28.9 points per game) and the NFL's worst rushing defense (147.1 rushing yards per game). This season, the Bengals are the league's No. 8 scoring defense (20.3 points per game) and the NFL's No. 19 rushing defense (116.3 rushing yards per game). Despite that dramatic improvement, Pollard will remain in the zone and go berserk, despite a non-threatening passing game led by 2025 first overall pick quarterback Cam Ward .
Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is having a career year. His 855 yards from scrimmage stood as the fourth most in the league through Week 7, and his 705 since Week 3 are the most in the entire NFL in that span. Warren's 6.8 yards per touch this season would be the most in a season on 15-plus touches per game (he's had 18 touches per game this season) since C.J. Spiller's 6.8 yards per touch back in 2012 with the Buffalo Bills .
Facing a Browns squad that surrendered 129 yards rushing and three rushing touchdowns to Pollard in Week 7, Warren will go off for a career-high 200 yards from scrimmage to even the season series against the Browns at one win apiece.
In most years, this prediction of multiple touchdown passes and no turnovers for the Los Angeles Chargers' two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert wouldn't be considered bold, but he is struggling mightily. He is tied for the league lead in both interceptions (8) and turnovers (10) this season. Herbert is also the first quarterback in NFL history to start 0-6 with an interception and multiple sacks taken in each of his team's first six games.
Against his SoFi Stadium neighbors, the Los Angeles Rams , Herbert will have a clean game. Three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald looks every bit of a 35-year-old who took two seasons off as he is sackless in five consecutive games, the longest streak of his career. Los Angeles will ride former first-round running back Omarion Hampton , control the clock and allow Herbert to play a much more relaxed style of football. That will lead to a big day for the struggling Herbert.
Week 7 couldn't have been uglier for the New York Jets . They allowed the previously-winless Miami Dolphins to tally their first victory of the season, and No. 1 wide receiver Garrett Wilson shared an animated conversation with quarterback Geno Smith and passing game coordinator Seth Ryan. It made sense: Wilson registered season lows in targets (3), catches (2), receiving yards (26) and no touchdowns.
The great news is that Week 8 provides Smith with a revenge game against the slumping Las Vegas Raiders . After their 3-0 start, the Raiders have now lost four in a row because their defense is crumbling. They have allowed 35.8 points per game and 11 passing touchdowns during the four-game losing streak. Smith will light up his old defense, and Wilson will produce over four times his receiving yards total from Week 7 on Sunday with over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown.

full_text: Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love (4) runs with the ball in the second quarter, Sunday, October 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Maybe it is finally going to happen. Jeremiyah Love is good to go on Sunday for the Arizona Cardinals, per Mike LaFleur pic.twitter.com/6ZZotrYJFu — Bo Brack (@BoBrack) October 30, 2026 This is huge because the Arizona Cardinals need to focus their offense around the rushing attack, especially going up against what has statistically been the worst rushing defense in the NFL, where the Dallas Cowboys have already allowed over 1000 yards on the season. title: NFL predictions: Falcons must slow down Bucs run game
summary: The Falcons shocked the NFL by coming away with the big upset victory over the previously-undefeated 49ers in Week 7. That win put Atlanta at 3-4 and, somehow, in the driver’s seat for the NFC South heading into Week 8. With the Panthers falling to the Packers on Thursday Night Football, the Falcons now have […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 11: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs with the ball during the third quarter of the NFL game against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on December 11, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons shocked the NFL by coming away with the big upset victory over the previously-undefeated 49ers in Week 7. That win put Atlanta at 3-4 and, somehow, in the driver’s seat for the NFC South heading into Week 8. With the Panthers falling to the Packers on Thursday Night Football, the Falcons now have an opportunity to take sole possession of first place in the division for the first time this season. Standing in their way are the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who managed to claw their way back to 2-5 despite an 0-4 start to the season. The Bucs are fresh off a thrashing of the aforementioned Panthers, where they ran the ball over 40 times and capitalized on four Carolina turnovers. Whether that performance is replicable or simply a blip on the radar remains to be seen. The consensus seems to be leaning towards the Bucs, with Tampa Bay currently 2.5-point home favorites over the Falcons in Week 8 per FanDuel. Can Atlanta take care of business on the road to get back to .500 and take control of the division? Falcons vs Bucs Week 8 predictions The Bucs are certainly not the pushover everyone thought they might be after a very rough 0-4 start to the season. Tampa Bay’s defense has largely played well, creating turnovers and stopping the run at a high level. That’s kept the team in games despite an offense that’s been among the league’s worst and most inconsistent. Tampa Bay’s offense looks and performs a lot like the Falcons offense of the previous two years under Zac Robinson. In case you haven’t heard, he’s coaching the Bucs offense now—so that shouldn’t be a surprise to anyone. When Tampa can run the ball effectively, they can have a lot of success on offense. In both their wins, the Bucs piled up over 240 rushing yards. However, the passing game has been horrible. Tampa Bay is the NFL’s worst passing attack, 32nd in yards and 32nd in N/YA. When the Bucs have had to lean on Baker Mayfield (or rookie Jalon Daniels), things typically went off the rails. Baker, in particular, has been turning the ball over at a high rate. It’ll be up to Atlanta’s defense to force the Bucs out of their comfort zone and into passing situations, where the Falcons will have the clear advantage. Doing that is twofold: the Falcons will have to play the run effectively, but they’ll also need to avoid their characteristic slow start on offense. Building a lead and winning the time of possession battle will be key. If the Bucs can’t lean on their run game, they don’t appear capable of winning with the passing game. That’s likely a combination of a depleted receiver room—now without Emeka Egbuka once again—Baker Mayfield’s struggles, and a poor scheme from Zac Robinson. Offensively, the Falcons are facing an objectively bad matchup. The Bucs excel at stopping the run, and they’ve typically leaned on the blitz and bringing extra rushers. Atlanta played the Ravens and Bears very poorly, and hasn’t managed a good rushing game since Week 4. However, Michael Penix Jr. and the passing game showed a lot of growth against an excellent 49ers defense in Week 7. They proved they could win with an efficient quick passing attack, and Penix has continued to improve and deciphering and managing pressure looks. We know the Falcons can win, and even dominate, when the run game is working. If it’s not, this team has typically gotten stuck in the mud. This Bucs matchup is another where Atlanta will have to show their passing game chops. Tampa Bay has been great at taking the ball away defensively, but they’ve also given the ball away at a high rate. Turnovers could once again play a major role in this one, for or against Atlanta. I should also mention that the Falcons have won their last three games in Tampa Bay, and the Bucs are currently 0-4 in their home stadium this season. Will those streaks continue? title: Ravens vs. Bengals: Rookie Report
summary: The Ravens rookies lost the first two division games of their careers in back-to-back games. Both were ugly second-half collapses that the franchise is all too familiar with, and now so are these rookies. All three of the losses in their young NFL careers have come from blowing second-half leads. Let’s hope they learn to […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 25: Bryan Cook #6 of the Cincinnati Bengals tackles Josh Cuevas #85 of the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter at M&T Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens rookies lost the first two division games of their careers in back-to-back games. Both were ugly second-half collapses that the franchise is all too familiar with, and now so are these rookies. All three of the losses in their young NFL careers have come from blowing second-half leads. Let’s hope they learn to shake the habit faster than some of the vets on the team… OG Vega Ioane The rookie, who’s played well enough to earn talks about rookie-of-the-year voting as a lineman, played less than a quarter against the Bengals. The Ravens will have to continue to wait to see their ideal offensive line play a game together after Cam Jurgens finally made his debut. The word is Ioane has an MCL sprain that isn’t too severe but will have him miss some time. OLB Zion Young The second-rounder’s snap count stayed at about the 40% mark despite Tavius Robinson’s injury, which is going to sideline him for the season. As it was for most of the defense, it wasn’t a banner day for Young. It was low PFF grades, no pressures accounted for, no run stops, and a missed tackle. We won’t look too hard into it with the entire defense sucking. WR Ja’Kobi Lane Lane continued to flash after last week’s return with another three catches this week. They only totaled for 25 yards, but two of those catches did go for first downs. Lane’s hands have flashed with catches in traffic and big third-down grabs. It’s easy to get excited about what Lane’s role could grow to once Lamar Jackson returns to the lineup. WR Elijah Sarratt Sarratt was a healthy scratch once again this week. TE Matt Hibner Hibner returned to the lineup after missing the game in Cleveland. More than half his snaps came as a run blocker and what few snaps were routes run, he didn’t draw a single target. That might have been designed to have Hibner focus on the run game after his hand injury. With Andrews continuing to struggle and now Cuevas really flashing, TE Josh Cuevas After a solid showing in Cleveland, Cuevas only played 16 snaps in Cincinnati. He made a solid impact on his eight routes, catching two of his targets for 35 yards for a solid 4.38 yards per route run. His run-blocking is still coming along; he registered grades below 50.0 in each of the last two weeks. CB Chandler Rivers Rivers was active this week but received no snaps on defense as Keyon Martin has taken the slot role firmly back. P Ryan Eckley Eckley was not as busy as one would expect given the Ravens’ offensive struggles. His first-quarter 49-yarder flipped the field, but his 57-yarder in the third quarter did not have enough hang time, leading to a big return. His final punt traveled only 39 yards and went out of bounds at the Bengals’ 21-yard line. OLB Ethan Burke Ethan Burke’s 78.5 PFF grade actually led the team (for whatever that’s worth). He stepped up in Tavius Robinson’s absence with stout run defense and won a few pass rushes, but could not finish a clear opportunity to take down Joe Burrow. Joe Fagnano was the active backup this week behind Huntley but saw no action. Running back Adam Randall remains on injured reserve, with defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny on the practice squad.

summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will return from a three-game absence to play on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday. Jackson, 29, suffered a high ankle sprain in the Ravens’ Week 4 over the Tennessee Titans. He missed the team’s next two games and returned to practice last week […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks to pass against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will return from a three-game absence to play on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday. Jackson, 29, suffered a high ankle sprain in the Ravens’ Week 4 over the Tennessee Titans. He missed the team’s next two games and returned to practice last week in a limited capacity. The two-time MVP was initially listed as questionable for Baltimore’s Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals but was ruled out on Saturday. The Ravens lost, 35-13, due partially to subpar play from backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jackson was upgraded to full participation on Wednesday and remained there for the entire week, clearing the way for him to take the field in Buffalo. After practice on Friday, he said that his ankle had progressed to the point that he was ready to play. “I feel like I’m no longer a statue,” Jackson explained. “I’m able to move around a little better, so I can give it a shot.” He is still dealing with pain when he plants on his injured left leg, but noted that it was “bearable.” He also emphasized the Ravens’ “extremely high” sense of urgency following two straight losses, which landed them in last place in the AFC North. And when asked about fans and media doubting his willingness to play hurt, he replied, “Why would you second-guess me?”

title: How do the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens stack up?
summary: During the bye I decided to compare all of the Josh Allen era seasons of the Buffalo Bills on both offense and defense. I determined that this year’s team has both the best offense we’ve ever seen with Allen, it’s being paired with the worst defense he’s ever had in the NFL. In order to […]
full_text: During the bye I decided to compare all of the Josh Allen era seasons of the Buffalo Bills on both offense and defense . I determined that this year’s team has both the best offense we’ve ever seen with Allen, it’s being paired with the worst defense he’s ever had in the NFL. In order to make that determination, I needed to pull some data which led to a semi-valid but completely fun rating system. I figured it would be a fun sendoff to this exercise to use it to compare the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore offense vs. Buffalo Defense If you’re seeing this methodology for the first time, you can click on either of the links above to get a more full picture, or read this very short description. I took seven mostly distinct metrics and put those into the table along with the respective league ranking in each measure. Then I add up the rankings to get a complete score, with lower being better. Got it? Here’s the chart. I started with the side of the conversation that I think most people have an idea of what to expect. The Ravens’ offense against the Bills’ defense. I know Bills fans (myself included) are quite down on the defense and remember, there’s good reason! It’s the worst one we’ve seen in a long time. Numerically with the completed score on the right, I think the numbers suggest what we’re all feeling; this is a poor matchup. There’s 98 points of separation between the two teams. What does that number mean? It means there’s a big gap; the metric is mostly for fun after all and isn’t meant to be a precise measure of anything really. Disclaimer alert! Lamar Jackson was out for three weeks with an injury so these numbers might be skewed down a bit. With that aside, so far the Ravens’ offense has been average almost entirely. Their lone bright spot is avoiding turnovers, and their sole sore spot is that they allow a lot of sacks. If you’re interested in the splits; Lamar Jackson has been taken down seven times, while Tyler Huntley is at ten. They both have one interception on the season. I don’t know if there’s any surprises here, and if we’re being objective I think we all know Lamar Jackson can play. I’m not counting on this Bills defense making too many stops unless their bye week prep was near miraculous. The question this year seems to be this; can the Bills offense dominate opponents and outscore them? Let’s see if the gap between the Bills’ offense and Ravens defense is larger or smaller than “98.” Ravens defense vs. Bills offense If you trust my scoring system, then it should predict a Baltimore win. There’s 55 points between the two which you might have picked up is smaller than 98. That said, these matchups are fantastic for Buffalo and this also shows why I don’t think the scoring total is strictly accurate. No one score more often or more total points per drive than Buffalo. While the Bills are turnover prone and Josh Allen has taken his fair share of sacks; the Bills are overcoming these flaws and scoring at an incredible pace. It’s also possible the Ravens hold true to form and basically avoid getting a turnover off of Buffalo which would be nice. My final verdict is that despite the numbers of the total score, it comes down to my tiers. The Bills’ defense is terrible but flirting with merely “bad.“ That’s going against an average offense. On the flip side you have a mediocre defense taking on an elite offense. Yes, you could flip this statement around and make it about anchors/deadweight/etc; but there’s only one team with an elite side at the moment and it’s the Bills. Until that changes, I like their odds.

title: Parker Brothers Tailgate Menu for the Buffalo Bills 2026 season
summary: Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team. And I’m writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I’ve been friends with […]
full_text: Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team. And I’m writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I’ve been friends with Rory and Ray since Kindergarten and have remained close friends with these brothers through a lot with the Bills over the years. It’s a bond that has always extended beyond Bills tailgates, but as we’ve gotten older, the Bills tailgates have become our central meeting ground, a guaranteed place to reconvene every fall and winter. And I sincerely cherish the yearly regathering with these two. I’m sure you know the exact feeling of camaraderie with your tailgating group. What started as a nano-tailgate with a deep fryer for wings and fries has gradually morphed into a full-scale tailgating operation, often feeding 50-plus patrons thanks to multiple flat tops, cooking apparatuses, and condiments galore. I cannot recommend the Parker Brothers Tailgate enough. And here is their menu for the 2026 Bills season. (Rory and Ray will be situated in the new “white” lot — behind Prohibition 2020 — for the 2026 campaign, and they welcome you to join them.) Week 2 – September 17: Detroit Lions, 8:15pm — Birria tacos This was a new menu item in 2025, and it went over like gangbusters. And who hasn’t experienced the birria taco craze at their local Mexican restaurant or taqueria? Well the Parkers are bringing that succulent experience to the grand opening of the new Highmark Stadium. Slow-cooked, marinated beef, melted Oaxacan cheese, and a consomé that knocks your socks off the moment you take your first bite. Birria tacos will hit the spot on a momentous evening in Orchard Park with weather that should still feel like summer… before literal and figurative fireworks inside the new stadium. Week 3 – September 27: Los Angeles Chargers — No tailgate (wedding in Lake George) For the first time I can remember, Rory and Ray will not be at a Bills tailgate, working tirelessly to feed the masses before unwinding while watching their Bills play. Family wedding in the Adirondacks will keep them away for this one, but trust me, they’ll be back with more energy than ever after their own bye week. Week 4 – October 4: New England Patriots, 1pm — Stingers What wings are to Buffalo, stinger subs are to the Parkers tailgate. Well, stingers and garbage plates. Every year, the stinger tailgate attracts more friends and random passers-by than any other because of the Parkers’ attention to detail with their stinger construction. Thick chicken fingers, dipped in country sweet sauce, combined with perfectly cooked shredded beef, with any combination of lettuce, cheese, onions, banana peppers, and mayo on a fresh sub roll that can be toasted if you’d like (highly recommend it). All ahead of a colossal showdown with the defending AFC champs in the House That Josh Built. Week 8 – November 1: Baltimore Ravens, 1pm — Surprise, Surprise Despite the pestering of my Parker Brothers sources, this tailgate remains a mystery. All I could manage to coax from said source was this, and it’s awesomely cryptic, it’s actually making me hungry right now: “This tailgate has never been done before, maybe never again,” and “I’ll go out on a limb and say no one has ever tried it ever.” ….as if you needed more encouragement to get to Bills-Ravens. Week 11 – November 22: Miami Dolphins, 1pm — Turkey 2 Ways Have you ever had deep-fried turkey? If the answer is no, this is one glorious sliver of life you have yet to experience. The Parkers call this Turkey 2 Ways because you can get a few slices of classically cooked Thanksgiving turkey. And if that’s your jam, I respect that. I recommend a taste of the Parkers deep-fried version that of course features a crunchy exterior and impossibly juicy meat as the focal point around mashed potatoes, corn, and everything else you’ll eventually eat on Thanksgiving with your family. Week 12 – November 26: Kansas City Chiefs, 8:20pm — Cheesesteaks Why aren’t the Parkers doing a Thanksgiving tailgate on Thanksgiving night? Well, they figured the tryptophan would probably be overwhelming at this stage of Thanksgiving, so they’re venturing away from all the food you’ve likely eaten in the hours leading up to this perennial enormous regular-season battle between the Bills and Chiefs. And the Parkers Cheesesteaks could hold their own on any corner on the streets of Philadelphia. Trust me. Ask for extra cheese. Thank me later. Week 15 – December 19: Chicago Bears — Italian beef A cousin of the Cheesesteaks, I actually slightly prefer the Italian beef — my last name should be a dead giveaway I’d have this take. Of course, this menu item from Rory and Ray is a nod to one of Chicago’s most revered culinary offerings, which just so happens to be the city’s version of the beef on weck. The spicy giardiniera — finely diced peppers, carrots, celery — elevate this sandwich into the stratosphere. And the warm, seasoned roast beef will warm your insides ahead of this super-fun AFC-NFC showdown between two of the best improvisational quarterbacks in the NFL. Week 18 – January 10: New York Jets, TBD — Smash burgers I adore smash burgers, and every time I eat one, I wonder… how and why were we not always eating burgers this way… two patties, pressed thin, with ample amounts of melted cheese to hold them together? And the Parkers have perfected the on-site smash burger… Ray is normally on the flat-top, precisely flattening each patty before loading with cheese. Rory’s responsibilities come in the made-to-order building of your burger. And he will walk you through the process once your patties are ready to be assembled between two buns. Because the Parkers have gotten so good with the presentation — and taste — of their smash burgers, this is an exquisite cap to the Bills 2026 regular season at this tailgate. Playoffs — TBD Among the menu items the Parkers have done in the past that would be possible during a Bills playoff run: Garbage Plates (unequivocally my favorite, thanks in large part to Mrs. Parker’s meat sauce) Hibachi (a gigantic undertaking but Michelin-star worthy) Burritos (made to your exact specifications, Chipotle-style) Breakfast (bacon, sausage, eggs, all sizzling on the griddle) Deep-fried everything (bring anything you want, the Parkers will deep fry right in front of your eyes) Spaghetti and meatballs (I never knew I needed this Italian classic before a football game, until I went to a Parker Tailgate) What is your tailgate scene like? Are you already planned out with specific menu items? Leave a comment explaining everything in detail!

title: Game-day food: Bills-Ravens calls for a poetic finishing butter
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. This weekend, we have something a bit spooky thanks to a perfect matchup with the Baltimore Ravens — and the ever-frightening darkness ushered in with the clock change. If you weren’t aware, the Ravens are thusly named due to one Edgar Allan Poe and his connection to Baltimore… forevermore. Ravensbutter I know what you’re thinking and yes, the photography this week was more work than the recipe. I stand by this decision. I’ve been deviating from team inspiration and going into mascots and the like, so this week I asked the question: “What was Edgar Allen Poe’s favorite food?” It turns out the answer was likely “booze” and I’ve recently done a cocktail. As an aside, Poe was notably broke as a professional writer, and it’s believed he subsisted on bread and butter quite a bit. I figured I could elevate the butter in this equation with a simple but delicious finishing variant that was great on bread but could be used for a whole lotta other good things. You might remember that Baltimore was the first Wingin’ It, and there’s a ton of history there. I tapped into that and went with flavors inspired by the Baltimore treat known as the “lemon stick.” You may look at the ingredient list and wonder “Hey Skare, where’s the Buffalo inspiration?” Well, we sure do love animals made out of butter. So… butter ravens! Way more sinister than lambs. Silence! Ravensbutter Makes: 1 cup of finishing butter Active time: 10 min Total time: 10 min Ingredients 2 sticks of salted butter Sage leaves, about ten (see below) Mint leaves, about ten (see below) 1/2 tsp lemon juice Essentials: Food processor (It shall make the undertaking considerably less arduous), measuring spoon, silicon molds if you want to get fancy, food color also if you want to get fancy Allow butter to come to room temperature. Wash and dry sage and mint leaves. Pulse leaves in food processor until finely minced. Chop up butter into large chunks; add to food processor. Add lemon juice; pulse all together until well blended. Spread blended butter into molds using butter knife, if you’re getting fancy. Freeze mold for at least 15 min; carefully remove butter. Wingin’ It tips The only tip I have is balancing the flavors. I went three to one with the sage being the heavier note compared to the mint. I added just enough lemon to bring the two together but to also avoid making the butter citrusy. Feel free to play around and adjust. Aside from that, enjoy the gallery! Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! Skarekrow likes certain products. Skarekrow likes money. title: Ed Oliver’s return can unlock Buffalo Bills defense
summary: There has been much conversation around the defensive play of the Buffalo Bills this season and the shortcomings under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. While many Bills fans have been frustrated, myself included, there is one piece of the equation that has not been discussed enough this season. Thanks to multiple injuries, star defensive tackle […]
full_text: There has been much conversation around the defensive play of the Buffalo Bills this season and the shortcomings under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. While many Bills fans have been frustrated, myself included, there is one piece of the equation that has not been discussed enough this season. Thanks to multiple injuries, star defensive tackle Ed Oliver has only appeared in three games for Buffalo this season. Oliver missed week two after suffering a hip injury in warm-ups, and then excited the game early after taking a shot to his left knee during week 4. Much of the focus on the defense’s shortcoming have been centered around the play of the secondary and linebacker corps, I would argue that Oliver’s absence has had the greater impact. Statistically speaking, the Bills defense has performed at a higher level with Oliver on the field. The team has given up 25.3 points per game when Oliver plays, compared to 31.7 per game when he does not. The Bills also allow less yards per game when Oliver plays, and have 17 quarterback pressures during those games (as opposed to six total in the three games he missed). Looking past the statistics, it should also be noted that opposing offenses have marched down the field late in games to score late touchdowns in games that have been missed by Oliver (Los Angeles Rams, Las Vegas Raiders, and after exiting against the New England Patriots). If you want to take it one step further, Oliver’s absence seems to be having an adverse affect on the play of Greg Rousseau. In games played by Oliver, fans saw Rousseau tally four sacks to go along with six tackles for a loss. Without Oliver proves to be another story, where Rousseau did not have any tackles for loss in those games. There has also been an impact on Deone Walker as Oliver has missed time, with the second-year defensive tackle being double-teamed on 71% of defensive snaps. While much of the conversation has focused on the secondary, I am optimistic that the anticipated return of Oliver will provide a much needed jolt for the Bills defense on Sunday. Let’s hope that I am right as the Bills face a tough challenge against Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens.
author: Anthony Marino

title: 5 Baltimore Ravens to watch at the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills are set to host the Baltimore Ravens this weekend in a tough matchup that could have playoff implications. Buffalo is vying for the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and they currently sit two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Baltimore, on the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are set to host the Baltimore Ravens this weekend in a tough matchup that could have playoff implications. Buffalo is vying for the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and they currently sit two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Baltimore, on the other hand, is currently in fourth place in the AFC North, but at 4-3, they are firmly involved in the AFC playoff picture. While the Bills and the Ravens may not be divisional foes, they very well could find themselves fighting for seeding once January hits. A head-to-head victory not only helps Buffalo maintain their divisional lead, but it could also make a big difference in their playoff path. Baltimore isn’t a typical last-place team; they are far too talented to be taken lightly, and the Bills know they have a fight on their hands this week. If they want to earn a win this Sunday, they’ll need to account for these five avens to watch. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Lamar Jackson After missing the last three games with an ankle injury, Jackson is poised to return, and just in time for the Ravens. Baltimore is always dangerous, but with Jackson back, an already dangerous offense becomes a big challenge for a struggling Buffalo defense. The Bills have traditionally hemmed Jackson in fairly well, but with a new coordinator and a new scheme on the defensive side, there’s no way to know if that success will translate this year. So far, Buffalo’s defense has had next to no success, as they sit 30th in points allowed and 31st in yards allowed this season. If Jackson’s mobility is limited, it could limit his effectiveness, as he consistently makes huge plays with his legs. While Jackson is perfectly capable of beating teams from the pocket, Buffalo has to force him to stay there and make him do it for four quarters. WR Zay Flowers After signing a big extension this offseason, Baltimore’s top receiver has justified that deal with a huge start to the season. Flowers has 40 catches for 608 yards and three touchdowns on 53 targets. He can operate from the outside and from the slot. He has tremendous speed, he runs great routes, and he can attack the defense at every level. In short, he’s a nightmare for a struggling pass defense like Buffalo’s. Hell, he’s a tough cover for anyone . After watching Christian Benford travel with Brock Bowers last week, it wouldn’t surprise me at all to see him draw the same assignment for Flowers. Benford can use his size and length—he’s 6’1” with 31” or 32” long arms, depending on the source—to jam the 5’9” Flowers at the line. Physicality is going to be the name of the game this week, as giving Flowers a free release is a recipe for disaster. Limiting him and making Jackson look elsewhere will be a key part of the game plan on Sunday. LB Roquan Smith The veteran is still one of the best in the game, and this seaosn, he’s performed better in coverage than he has at any point in his career. So far, he’s allowing just 53.8% of passes thrown his way to be completed; opposing quarterbacks have a rating of just 56.3 when targeting Smith in the passing game. Those numbers are both career bests for the 29-year old five-time All-Pro. Normally, I’d say he’s someone to target in the passing game, as he allows better than a 70% completion rate against for his career. And, while I think that the Raven will use Kyle Hamilton to guard Buffalo’s tight ends over the middle, they could very well use Smith to do that if he’s matched up agaisnt someone like Dawson Knox or Jackson Hawes. Smith is also big enough and physical enough to act as a spy on quarterback Josh Allen, and while he has dealt with a knee injury, he seems ready to return to a full-time role this weekend. Keeping track of No. 0 has to be a big part of Sunday’s plan on offense. S Kyle Hamilton The versatile defensive back is always worth watching, as he has the toughness to erase tight ends and the quickness to deal with most wide receivers over the middle. Hamilton is a long, sturdy defender who can neutralize even high-end talents; however, he’s been limited a bit of late thanks to a lingering knee issue. He sat out of Wednesday’s practice before logging a limited session Thursday and a full session on Friday. He enters the game without an injury designation, but he hasn’t quite been as dominant in the early going of this season as he has been in years past. He’s allowing 67.9% of passes to be completed when he’s the closest man in coverage, and he’s allowing a career-high 8.9 yards per completion. He’s also missed five tackles so far this season, and his missed tackle percentage so far is a career-high 9.1%. Sure, opposing quarterbacks have just an 80.8 quarterback rating when targeting him, but for a three-time All-Pro, it’s a small step in the wrong direction. I assume that Hamilton’s main mark will be Dalton Kincaid this week, who is questionable to play thanks to a chest injury. If Buffalo has Kincaid, Khalil Shakir, and DJ Moore, then Hamilton can’t erase all of them. Whichever player he’s on should be targeted with caution, but there will be opportunities for Buffalo over the middle. CB Nate Wiggins With all due respect to veteran Marlon Humphrey, it’s Wiggins who is their top corner, in my eyes. Wiggins has allowed just 55.6% of passes thrown his way to be completed; he has four pass breakups on the season to give him 31 in 39 career games. Despite how talented Wiggins is, he was repeatedly abused by Josh Allen and the Bills during last season’s wild 41-40 comeback victory. Allen targeted Wiggins’ man seven times, completing six of those passes for 78 yards. Allen was outstanding that night, throwing for 394 yards and two touchdowns while completing 33-of-46 passes. Wiggins is too good to take lightly, however, and he’ll likely be matched up against either Keon Coleman or DJ Moore. Buffalo can’t ignore those guys, so they’ll need to win their reps against Wiggins in order to give the Bills a chance at victory.
