title: NFL predictions: 3 underdogs set to surprise for Bills vs. Ravens
summary: The Buffalo Bills are back in action this weekend, ready for a fresh start after a relatively early bye week away from football. Since 2018, the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen are 8-0 in games after the bye. It’s a record that’s also neatly tied to former head coach Sean McDermott. Now, new head coach […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 07: Jackson Hawes #85 of the Buffalo Bills catches a pass with pressure from Nate Wiggins #2 of the Baltimore Ravens during the fourth quarter at Highmark Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are back in action this weekend, ready for a fresh start after a relatively early bye week away from football. Since 2018, the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen are 8-0 in games after the bye. It’s a record that’s also neatly tied to former head coach Sean McDermott. Now, new head coach Joe Brady gets his first crack at establishing his own post-bye legacy in tandem with Allen. Standing in the way are the Baltimore Ravens, a team that should be plenty motivated to reset the narrative after a crushing loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. If the Ravens struggled to stop quarterback Joe Burrow and company last weekend, what’s in store for them against the league’s top-scoring offense on Sunday? A track meet, of sorts, may be necessary in Week 8 — with Buffalo and Baltimore potentially lighting up the scoreboard on offense. Given the recent history between these two teams, there’s very little to plant one’s flag in the ground while staking a bold claim. What’s bold in most arenas trends typical when quarterback Lamar Jackson and Allen renew their friendship. No one would be shocked to see Allen and/or Jackson put up five touchdowns, or even surprised to learn that running backs James Cook III and Derrick Henry took more than one football more than 50 yards to paydirt en route to a 150-plus effort on the ground. Instead, what would reverberate across the NFL is if Bills-Ravens ended with a 9-6 score, or that Buffalo’s defense clamped down and provided the only score en route to victory. Or perhaps that Baltimore found a way to win a shootout without touchdowns from either Jackson or Henry. It’s going to take incredible performances by unsung heroes for anyone to be surprised by Sunday’s outcome. Here are a few potentially bold options to consider… TE Jackson Hawes scores his first TD of 2026 NFL season For those who celebrate, National Tight Ends Day was October 25, 2026. Unfortunately, the Bills weren’t able to take part in the festivities thanks to their bye. A week later, Buffalo’s quadruple alliance at tight end returns to the field ready to party. Well, for the most part: We don’t know if Dalton Kincaid will play due to his questionable status based off a current chest injury, but it’s not a great sign to see him limited in each practice session this week following a week off. The Bills love to run 13 personnel, and that offers plenty of chances for tight ends Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes to see action. If Kincaid can’t go, it’s easy to land on Knox as the biggest beneficiary in terms of snaps and targets. Instead, I believe it’s Hawes who leaps into a featured role, thanks to his otherworldly blocking ability and a set of very capable hands. Interestingly, Hawes has been a few steps below an afterthought as a receiver this season. Hawes has zero offensive stats on one target through the first six games. This comes after a rookie season in 2025 that saw Hawes make 16 catches (19 targets) for 187 yards and three touchdowns. It’s fair to say that Brady and Allen have a one-track mind regarding Hawes this season, which is status as a blocker. That may change in Week 8. But understand this is a pretty deep dig into “bold” territory. The oddsmakers at Fanduel Sportsbook list only eight options for Jackson Hawes in Week 8 , and most of them carry long, yet potentially rewarding odds. The next touchdown pass that Josh Allen throws will vault him above Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Jim Kelly and to the top of the Bills’ record books as the new all-time leader in touchdown passes. Is Hawes on the receiving end of that historic moment? Well, let’s just say there’s a possibility, albeit slight. Current options find Hawes with +5000 odds to be the game’s first touchdown scorer. There are of course a few more semi-realistic options that find Hawes as an anytime touchdown scorer (+850), anytime first-half touchdown scorer (+1600), or anytime second-half touchdown scorer (+1300). Better yet, well if you’re looking for a really crazy option that involves Hawes. How’s +25000 odds for Hawes to be first touchdown scorer among all 1 p.m. EST games? In all honesty, Kincaid is viewed as the tight end more likely to accomplish any one of those feats mentioned above. His questionable status does however do just enough to open the door a bit wider for a player Buffalo should do more to get involved. So you’re wondering how Hawes did against Baltimore last season, his first regular-season game? Hawes caught his lone target for 29 yards on 16 offensive snaps (hat tip to Pro Football Reference ). He has plenty more to offer than that for Round 2! RB Ty Johnson leads Bills in receiving yards What brand of sorcery is this?! Allen’s favorite third-down specialist, Ty Johnson has roared to life since his return from a hamstring injury at the end of training camp this past August. Though perhaps still viewed as an unfortunate and unfair slight to Cook, it’s now clear that Johnson takes priority on most third downs simply because of his talent as a receiver. Johnson is a legit threat to take any screen pass or otherwise the distance. He’s a deceptive speed demon who wastes no time getting from A to B, and then, C, D, and often Z. Still, predicting Johnson to lead the Bills in receiving yards is about as bold as it comes in Week 8. Yes, Kincaid is questionable, as is wide receiver DJ Moore. Johnson would still have to compete with wide receivers Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman, and on a smaller share of snaps. Johnson is similar to Shakir in ways, a pinball wizard with a more direct sort of attack. Give Johnson a football, and he’s off to the races, running around, through, and past anyone unfamiliar with his game. What might it look like if Johnson were to lead the Bills in receiving against the Ravens? He’ll probably need north of 60 yards, which carries +1280 odds at Fanduel. Think he can do it? The last time Johnson faced the Ravens, he was held without a catch on two targets. In four games this season, Johnson has gone over 50 yards twice. S Damar Hamlin’s play rallies D Damar Hamlin will start at safety alongside Cole Bishop on Sunday, stepping in for safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (suspended Week 8). Despite the concerns fans have with Gardner-Johnson’s play, and the performance of the defensive backs in total, many worry what starting Hamlin means for a 31st-ranked defensive unit. It’s worth wondering how many of Hamlin’s plays the constant naysayers have watched over the years. Hamlin is a sound tackler who has often served as the last line of defense in scoring moments. He’s not an elite athlete by most standards, but he is an intelligent player who’s more than capable and wholly comfortable calling coverages and offensive looks from the back seven. He’s also a fantastic special teams player. To this point, Hamlin’s football story has been dominated by an against-all-odds full recovery following a play few will ever forget, but one that he fails to remember following his body’s response to trauma. But there’s far more to Hamlin’s game than most people understand. In McDermott’s scheme, Hamlin was put in position to succeed, and did well as someone with a knack for interceptions. I see good things happening for Hamlin against the Ravens on Sunday. Watch for him to pick off one of Jackson’s passes in a huge moment, or perhaps force a fumble of Henry or someone else. Strong play by Hamlin could be a huge part of the defense’s ability to rally toward victory in Week 8. You might recall the last time that Hamlin started against the Ravens, a game in which he made a touchdown-saving solo tackle on Henry, and forced a fumble of Jackson . Think you’ve got what it takes…
author: Matt Byham

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the Baltimore Ravens
summary: The Buffalo Bills take on the Baltimore Ravens this week in what will be the first post-bye week game of head coach Joe Brady’s tenure. Under former head coach Sean McDermott, the Bills were a perfect 9-0 following a bye. Can the Bills continue that trend under a new head man? The week of rest […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills take on the Baltimore Ravens this week in what will be the first post-bye week game of head coach Joe Brady’s tenure. Under former head coach Sean McDermott, the Bills were a perfect 9-0 following a bye. Can the Bills continue that trend under a new head man? The week of rest came at a good time for Buffalo, as they were plenty banged-up for their last contest against the Las Vegas Raiders. Thanks to that extra week of rest coming into this game, it appears that the Bills will have some of their top players returning for what should be a tough matchup against a strong AFC foe. Here are our five players to watch this week as Buffalo battles Baltimore. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR DJ Moore After missing Buffalo’s last two games thanks to a flare-up of the same shoulder injury that caused him to miss time against the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots, Moore is trending towards playing this week. He will be a welcome addition to a Buffalo passing game that has been outstanding this season. The Bills rank No. 12 overall in passing yards and No. 17 in passing touchdowns despite coming in at just No. 30 overall in passing attempts. This week, quarterback Josh Allen should be even better than he has been with his top wideout back in the game. Moore has 12 catches for 178 yards and a score on 20 targets this season. In the two games where he’s been able to start and finish the contest, Moore has 11 of those catches for 167 yards and a score. In those two games, Allen totaled 538 passing yards and two scores. Moore opens up the Buffalo passing attack, and thanks to the emergence of Keon Coleman this year, the Bills now have two solid wideouts joining Khalil Shakir at the top of the receiver depth chart. Look for the Bills to ease Moore back into action, but if it’s as tight as I think it will be, expect No. 2 to see plenty of targets in the second half in big moments. WR Khalil Shakir Given Baltimore’s success in stopping the run this season—they’re allowing just 3.8 yards per rush so far—I think the Bills might be wise trying to attack via their “11” personnel grouping more often than through their heavier packages. That means there should be plenty of targets for someone like Shakir, who has taken a bit of a back seat in the early going after serving as Allen’s top target over the last two seasons. Shakir is on pace to catch 62 passes for 821 yards and three touchdowns on 91 targets. Those be his lowest totals in targets, receptions, and touchdowns in a season since 2023, which is when he had Stefon Diggs absorbing the majority of the targets. Shakir is as dangerous as anyone in the NFL in space, and he can operate at all levels of the defense to create mismatches. I like Buffalo’s slot targets—Shakir and tight end Dalton Kincaid—this week against the interior of the Baltimore defense, and I especially like Shakir if the Ravens use safety Kyle Hamilton to neutralize Kincaid. OLB Greg Rousseau After a white-hot start to the season, Rousseau has cooled over the course of the Bills’ last three games. Groot began the year by earning Defensive Player of the Month honors for September, totaling 15 tackles, six sacks, three forced fumbles, eight tackles for loss, 12 quarterback hits, and a pass deflection in Buffalo’s first three games. In the three games the Bills have played since, Rousseau has six tackles, seven quarterback hits, four pass deflections, and zero sacks or tackles for loss. Granted, teams took notice of Rousseau’s play and have responded by devising blocking schemes to neutralize him as a result; however, Rousseau can’t be invisible in the pass rush for Buffalo’s beleaguered defense to turn their performance around. Against Lamar Jackson, who should be set to return from an ankle injury this week, the Bills will need to be sound in their assignments and force their opponents to beat them from the pocket. Jackson is excellent within structure, but he is absolutely devastating when allowed to scramble. Rousseau has always done a great job setting the edge, but he’ll need to play up the elite status of his first three games this week in order for the Bills to come out with a win. DL Ed Oliver I was between Ed and linebacker Terrel Bernard for this spot, and while I think it’s essential for Bernard to perform, I’m really intrigued to see what Buffalo’s defensive line can do with a healthy Oliver back in the fold. If teams want to commit their resources to Rousseau on the edge, that likely means that someone like Oliver will have a one-on-one inside, especially given how good nose tackle Deone Walker has been this season. Oliver has dealt with hip and knee injuries this season, and just as the story of his career has gone, the injuries have prevented him from playing consistently enough to make an impact. Look for Oliver to lasso Jackson in the backfield at some point on Sunday for his first full sack of the season (he notched a shared sack during Buffalo’s 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots). S Damar Hamlin I’ve already outlined the reasons why I think the starting safety spot alongside Cole Bishop should go to rookie Jalon Kilgore instead of the veteran Hamlin, but all signs point to Hamlin being the one to take C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s place for most of the snaps on Sunday. Hamlin is limited in coverage, and while he remains a solid tackler, he’s best suited for special teams work. If he finds himself in one-on-one situations against Mark Andrews, or worse yet, Zay Flowers, the Ravens will capitalize. Perhaps Hamlin’s mental acuity will help to settle the defensive secondary, but I’m more concerned that his lack of speed will lead to some big plays. Baltimore is going to try to find No. 3 and use him to their advantage this week. Just as he’s done for the majority of his career, Hamlin will have to rise to that challenge. Here’s hoping he turns in a solid performance, but don’t be surprised if we see some Jalon Kilgore out there at times, as well.
author: Sean Murphy

title: Jalon Kilgore, not Damar Hamlin, should start alongside Cole Bishop for Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills will be without starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for their matchup with the Baltimore Ravens this week. As we know, Gardner-Johnson is suspended for the game after spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers in the first half of Buffalo’s 33-30 victory two weeks ago. That means that someone needs to […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Jalon Kilgore #29 of the Buffalo Bills defends in coverage during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills will be without starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for their matchup with the Baltimore Ravens this week. As we know, Gardner-Johnson is suspended for the game after spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers in the first half of Buffalo’s 33-30 victory two weeks ago. That means that someone needs to step up and take his snaps this week, and while the coaching staff has indicated that veteran Damar Hamlin will be the one to do so, I think that rookie Jalon Kilgore is a better option. Hamlin, 28, has proven his mettle throughout his career. Hamlin has made 28 starts in his career and played in 59 games across six professional seasons. No one would have blamed him if his NFL career ended in his second year after he suffered a cardiac arrest during a Monday Night Football matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Against all odds, however, Hamlin returned to the field, contributing on special teams and serving as a starting safety for most of the 2024 season. For all his value on special teams, though, Hamlin is what he is at this point in his career: He’s a heady player who understands where he needs to be, but he doesn’t always have the speed to make it to that spot in time to make a play. He wasn’t a high-end athlete, at least by NFL standards, before his injury, and he isn’t one now, either. While he remains a steady tackler, those athletic shortcomings often show up in pass coverage. This season, Pro Football Reference credits receivers as having caught eight of ten passes for 140 yards when Hamlin is the closest man in coverage. For his career, Hamlin has allowed 61-of-88 passes to be completed (69.3%) while he is the closest man. Those passes have gone for 983 yards and five touchdowns. Opposing quarterbacks have a 115.9 rating when targeting Hamlin in coverage. Buffalo’s pass defense this season has been atrocious, as the team ranks No. 31 in pass yards allowed and No. 30 in passing touchdowns allowed. Given his struggles in coverage throughout his career, inserting Hamlin into the lineup doesn’t seem like something that is going to help the pass defense overall. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has given Hamlin credit, saying that the veteran safety likely doesn’t receive enough praise for his contributions to the team. Leonhard thinks that Hamlin’s presence in the back end will simplify communications and help the secondary to avoid some of the confusion and breakdowns in coverage that have plagued them this season. Hamlin played 68% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps against the Raiders, nearly all of which came in the second half of the game. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins led scoring drives of 70, 91, and 66 yards in the second half. Hamlin was the closest man in coverage on two of Cousins’ passes; both were completed for 47 yards. Hamlin also managed six tackles without missing one, and he has yet to miss a tackle this season. So, with all of that about Hamlin, what’s the case for Kilgore? We all remember Cousins’ final touchdown pass, a gorgeous 44-yard strike to Tre Tucker, who had slipped behind the safety on what should have been an obvious “nobody behind you”-type coverage. The safety Tucker beat, of course, was Kilgore. Why start the kid if he didn’t have the wherewithal to give the best deep threat on the Raiders more cushion in a situation where the only way Buffalo could lose was via a quick-strike touchdown? Well, Kilgore also nearly had the speed and athleticism to bring himself back into the play after initially losing Tucker in coverage. Just one drive prior, Kilgore made a great play to break up a pass intended for Tucker, driving on an in-breaker to force a punt. No one is perfect, and for a young player in his first real extended action, Kilgore showed off athleticism that Hamlin just doesn’t have. Should that athleticism buy him time on the field despite his inexperience and the potential for mental mistakes? Given Buffalo’s defensive struggles, I have to go with yes, it does. There is only one way to build the mental acuity necessary to process NFL games at NFL speeds, and that is to play in NFL games. While Damar Hamlin is a known quantity, Jalon Kilgore has tremendous potential based solely on his athletic ability. That athleticism gives Buffalo some flexibility in their alignments, as he possesses the speed to play from multiple places in the secondary. Hamlin, for all his solid tackling, is really best as a deep-third player, which helps to compensate for his lack of quickness overall in giving him more time to reach his coverage assignment. Kilgore might make some mistakes, but he also might make some plays. Using Kilgore in tandem with Cole Bishop gives Buffalo a young, athletic safety pairing that can make plays from multiple different alignments. Adding Hamlin into the mix clarifies the safeties’ roles a bit, but it clarifies those roles and assignments both for the defense and the opposing offense. Hamlin isn’t guarding anyone man-to-man, and asking him to do so is usually a recipe for disaster. Kilgore, on the other hand, has the speed, size, and toughness to stick with tight ends and receivers alike. The Bills have allowed their young players to work in on defense, building their rep count while also keeping heady veterans fresh. There is no doubt in my mind that Kilgore is a more physically talented player than Hamlin, and I similarly believe that the best thing for his development is to play. To borrow a phrase from Paul McCartney, if we’re to believe that Buffalo’s defense is getting better, I have to answer with John Lennon’s counter to that line: “It can’t get no worse.” With that in mind, I would much rather see the Bills give Jalon Kilgore a chance rather than going back to the well with Damar Hamlin.

full_text: Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Panthers took an ugly 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday Night Football, and Carolina responded to that loss by parting ways with defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. Todd Wash was named interim defensive coordinator and will call the defensive plays, according to a release from the Panthers shared by Joe Person of The Athletic. Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive pass game coordinator Ejiro Evero. DL line coach Todd Wash named interim DC. pic.twitter.com/7zFf3cZeYj — Joe Person (@josephperson) October 30, 2026 Ejiro was hired by the Panthers as the team’s defensive coordinator in 2023 after one season in the DC role with the Los Angeles Rams. He was hired during Frank Reich’s tenure as the Panthers’ head coach, but Dave Canales retained him when he was hired by Carolina. Wash spent five seasons as the Jaguars’ defensive coordinator. From the Panthers’ release : Wash originally joined Carolina’s staff in 2023 and has 31 years of coaching experience, including 20 in the NFL. He spent five seasons (2016-20) serving as the defensive coordinator for the Jacksonville Jaguars, including in 2017 when the team had the second-ranked defense in the league and advanced to the AFC Championship Game. It wasn’t just Thursday night’s loss that led to the decision. The loss to the Packers on a short week came on the heels of an embarrassing 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. But Baker Mayfield only threw for about 63 yards, and the Buccaneers ran all over Carolina. On Thursday night, the Panthers let Jordan Love throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns while Bryce Young took six sacks and finished with a QBR of 36.2. In addition to the termination of Evero and Cooley, the Panthers announced that OLB/run game specialist AC Carter will also take on defensive line coaching responsibilities. Secondary coach Renardo Hill will retain his position. The Panthers are sitting at 3-4 and remain in first place in a very weird NFC South, but if the Falcons win this week, that will change. If you’ve paid any attention to the Atlanta Falcons, you know that’s always a big “if.” We will update this story as more information becomes available.

title: The Optimist: That could have been worse
summary: The Carolina Panthers put up an honestly decent showing against a superior opponent. Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers were the best combination of quarterback and defense Carolina has faced this season. They faced them with their worst and worsening combination of secondary and offensive line injuries. It was a match made in some […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers put up an honestly decent showing against a superior opponent. Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers were the best combination of quarterback and defense Carolina has faced this season. They faced them with their worst and worsening combination of secondary and offensive line injuries. It was a match made in some Wisconsinite cheese-fever dream. Factor in the deflation of team ego off last week’s embarrassment against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and you could easily have expected worse than a one possession loss. Instead the team was outmatched on almost every level and still hung in to make a game of it. If they have to lose a corner and a guard every week of the season then at least they can keep things entertaining along the way. If Jaelan Phillips, Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Will Lee III, and Brady Christiansen can all come back from injury by the end of the season then maybe things can turn around. Even one of them making one more impact play last night could have made the difference in a one possession game. Nobodies presence was more missed than Lewis’, who left the Bucs game with a knee injury. Unlike most Panthers players this season, that did not immediately land him on injured reserve. He is the lone bright spot on the Panthers current line, with rookie Monroe Freeling coming close to being a second one. There is more to be said about both the offensive line and the secondary, but now isn’t the time. I’m not nit-picking the day after an eight point loss when the only thing I know about the Panthers Week 9 starting corners and left guard is that they weren’t on the roster during training camp. We’ll be back next week with more information than that. For now, take heart in the fact that this was an infinitely better team than we saw against the Bucs. That loss showed us a low discipline floor more than anything closely resembling Carolina’s current ceiling. Last night was more a middle ground, a shadow of what could be. But a loss is what you get when your quarterback has no time to throw, your opponent has all day, and half your team is probably wondering if they’ll be the next ones carted off. Still, not all losses are created equal and this one was vastly more promising than the last. Also, the season isn’t over yet. In fact, if it ended today, we might get to watch the funniest matchup in the history of the playoffs. All four NFC North teams would make the playoffs. The 5-3 Packers are in fourth place in the division and would be the seventh seed. They would play the 3-4 Panthers in Charlotte in a wildcard game. If you can’t love the Panthers right now then you have to at least love the NFC South.

title: Chicago Bears Week 8 Flashbacks: A Pair of Walk Offs and a Franchise Record
summary: We’re already nearly half way through the 2026 NFL season, in the blink of an eye at that! But that doesn’t slow this time machine, let’s take a look at three more SPoooooooKY games from the Bears past! Happy Halloween! 1. 2005, Bears @ Lions: Peanut walks it off in overtime October 30, 2005 | […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 22: Eddie Jackson #39 of the Chicago Bears reacts after the Bears intercepted the football in the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field on October 22, 2017 in Chicago, Illinois. The Chicago Bears defeated the Carolina Panthers 17-3. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re already nearly half way through the 2026 NFL season, in the blink of an eye at that! But that doesn’t slow this time machine, let’s take a look at three more SPoooooooKY games from the Bears past! Happy Halloween! 1. 2005, Bears @ Lions: Peanut walks it off in overtime October 30, 2005 | Bears win 19-13 (OT) The 2005 Bears were still finding their identity when they traveled to Detroit for a Week 8 matchup with significant implications for the NFC North standings. Chicago entered at 3-3, tied with Detroit for first place in the division. Rookie quarterback Kyle Orton put together one of his better performances of the season, completing 17-of-31 passes for a career-high 230 yards and a touchdown. His 23-yard scoring strike to Muhsin Muhammad capped a 99-yard touchdown drive, helping Chicago build a 13-3 halftime lead. Detroit battled back, tying the game at 13 early in the fourth quarter. Neither offense could break the deadlock, sending the game into overtime. That’s when Charles Tillman decided he’d seen enough. Lions quarterback Jeff Garcia rolled to his right before attempting an ill-advised throw back across the field toward Mike Williams. Tillman stepped in front of the pass and raced 22 yards for the game-winning touchdown. Chicago improved to 4-3, taking sole possession of first place in the NFC North. The victory also carried historical significance, as the Bears became the first franchise in NFL history to reach 650 regular-season victories. 2. 2006, Bears vs. 49ers: Chicago scores 41 points before halftime October 29, 2006 | Bears win 41-10 The 2006 Bears entered Week 8 undefeated, having survived their unforgettable Monday Night Football comeback against Arizona two weeks earlier. Apparently, they were interested in making this one a little less stressful. Chicago welcomed San Francisco to Soldier Field and proceeded to put together one of the most dominant first halves in franchise history. The Bears scored 24 points in the opening quarter alone, establishing a franchise record for first-quarter scoring. By halftime, Chicago had built an absolutely ridiculous 41-0 advantage. Quarterback Rex Grossman rebounded from his disastrous outing against Arizona, completing 23-of-29 passes for 252 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. His 137.4 passer rating was among his best performances of the season. Throwback to Oct. 29, 2006, when the Bears dropped 41 points on the 49ers in the first half pic.twitter.com/afuUx09wZp — Depressed Bears Fan (@ImBearsFan) December 27, 2025 Tight end Desmond Clark caught six passes for 86 yards and two touchdowns, while Thomas Jones contributed 111 rushing yards and another score. The defense was equally impressive. Brian Urlacher delivered one of the afternoon’s most memorable plays, batting an Alex Smith pass into the air before securing a remarkable one-handed interception. Chicago forced four first-half turnovers, converting each into a touchdown. The 41 first-half points tied a franchise record established against Washington in 1948. The Bears eventually cruised to a 41-10 victory, improving to 7-0 for the first time since their legendary 1985 season. 3. 2012, Bears vs. Panthers: Cutler and Gould pull off a Halloween miracle October 28, 2012 | Bears win 23-22 The 2012 Bears entered Week 8 riding a four-game winning streak and sitting comfortably atop the NFC North at 5-1. For three quarters against Carolina, however, Chicago looked nothing like a division leader. The Panthers thoroughly dominated the Bears, building a 19-7 advantage while making life miserable for Jay Cutler. Cutler was sacked six times in the first half alone, throwing an interception and losing two fumbles. At one point late in the third quarter, Carolina had outgained Chicago 369-59. Then things got weird. With just under seven minutes remaining, Cutler connected with Kellen Davis for a 12-yard touchdown, trimming Carolina’s lead to 19-14. Eight seconds later, the Bears were winning. On Carolina’s very next offensive snap, receiver Steve Smith slipped while running his route, allowing Tim Jennings to intercept Cam Newton and return the football 25 yards for a touchdown. Chicago had somehow scored two touchdowns in eight seconds. The Panthers weren’t finished, though, reclaiming a 22-20 lead on a 45-yard field goal with 2:27 remaining. That left Cutler one final opportunity. He completed six of seven passes for 52 yards on the ensuing possession, including several crucial completions to Brandon Marshall, setting up Robbie Gould for a 41-yard field goal as time expired. Good as Gould. Bears win, 23-22. Cutler finished 19-of-28 for 186 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Marshall caught nine passes for 98 yards, while Jennings recorded two interceptions, including the game-changing pick-six. Chicago improved to 6-1 despite being outgained 416-210. title: Hot Take Friday: Super Bears, Super Bowl
summary: Hot Take Tuesday is coming at you a few days late, thanks to an illness that had me at death’s door earlier in the week. I’ll spare you the details, but I think I felt about how Jabba the Hutt looks. Wasn’t sure when I was going to surface, but I started ticking up Thursday […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - JANUARY 26: Head Coach Mike Ditka of the Chicago Bears gets carried off the field after they defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX January 26, 1986 at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Bears won the Super Bowl 46-10. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hot Take Tuesday is coming at you a few days late, thanks to an illness that had me at death’s door earlier in the week. I’ll spare you the details, but I think I felt about how Jabba the Hutt looks. Wasn’t sure when I was going to surface, but I started ticking up Thursday and Friday and was trying to get back into the swing. It makes it a lot easier to get some motivation to sit down at a keyboard when the Chicago Bears go out and trade for Jeffery Simmons. Let’s say it loud and clear for the Green Bay Packers fans in the back: the Chicago Bears are set up to win a Super Bowl. They have taken their chips and pushed them to the middle of the table. They have placed a bet on Ben Johnson, they have placed a bet on Caleb Williams, and they have placed a bet that they have everything they need to win it all. Guess what? I think they’re right. What’s great about this all-in move is that it’s not a sacrificial all-in move. The Bears are still set up really well for the next few years. The Bears won’t have first-round picks the next two years, that’s true, but if the Bears are as good as I think they are, those picks are probably going to be in the last four picks of the first round; hopefully it will be quite literally the last pick. If the Bears gave up the 32nd pick for Jeffery Simmons, who’s complaining? Hell, they already gave up the 32nd pick once upon a time for Chase Claypool. Draft capital is critical for rebuilding teams; clinging to first-round picks doesn’t matter nearly as much when you are picking in the late 20s or early 30s. It’s time to rewire your brain. I know, first we had to rewire our brains to understand what it was like to have an actual quarterback in Caleb Williams. Then we had to rewire our brains to understand what it’s like to have an offensive genius as a coach with Ben Johnson. Now it’s time to rewire our brains and understand how to operate as a winning franchise. The LA Rams say F them picks. Why? Because trading away picks in the 20s for star players is a far better hit rate on those picks than picking a player. The Rams don’t actually say F them picks. They say F them first-round picks. They always have plenty of day 2 and day 3 picks, and they draft well and find plenty of quality players with those picks. Then they use trades and go out and get the likes of Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett, Davante Adams, etc. I understand the Rams are having a trainwreck season (for now), but their sustained success over the last several years has been something we’ve all witnessed. If the Bears have the same mindset, I’m all for it. The Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber head coach. The Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber quarterback. The Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber offense. And now, the Bears have a Super Bowl-caliber defense. How good is this defense going to be? That’s hard to tell, but Simmons isn’t just adding an excellent player into the mix. He’s a multiplier. He’s one of the most double-teamed players in the NFL. Which means less attention to the other three linemen, which gives them consistently winnable one-on-one situations. Simmons, despite those double teams, will still make plenty of impact plays each game. And his presence will allow those other linemen to make their share as well. When the line is this far improved, it improves the back seven as well. Devin Bush will stop getting tied down with blockers because they’ll all be blocking Simmons. He will be able to make more plays. The Bears will be able to bring more pressure without blitzing, allowing more defenders to roam the secondary. The Bears will be giving QBs less time to throw, which means less of a chance to expose their weaker coverage players. Everyone on the defense just got better thanks to Jeffery Simmons. Is Ryan Poles done adding? I think there’s a strong chance we see one or two more moves that probably only involve day three picks, but yes, Khalil Mack can be had for a day 3 pick. I would love to see the Bears add Mack, and I would love to see the Bears add a solid CB into their secondary. But even if this is the only move they make, it was one hell of a move. Well done, Ryan Poles. The Chicago Bears have put the league on notice. Their time is now. And as Jake Taylor in Major League said, there’s only one thing left to do… Win the whole f*ckin’ thing.

title: Bears at Seahawks Q&A: Great Offensive and Defensive Minds Clash
summary: This should be a lot of fun on Monday Night Football. The Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears are set to meet in a huge game that has NFC Playoff implications. The Bears are red-hot, winning every game since Caleb Williams’ return, but Seattle just handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss of the year. […]
full_text: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (11) rushes for yards during the second quarter of an NFL football matchup, Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025, at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fla. The Seahawks defeated the Jaguars 20-12. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co This should be a lot of fun on Monday Night Football. The Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears are set to meet in a huge game that has NFC Playoff implications. The Bears are red-hot, winning every game since Caleb Williams’ return, but Seattle just handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss of the year. To get you set for this matchup, we sat down with John Gilbert from Field Gulls (SB Nation’s Seattle Seahawks site) to get you the inside scoop on the Bears’ opponent. Here’s that Q&A with John. 1. This matchup looks like it could be a lot of fun. The idea of arguably the best defensive mind in football against one of, if not the best offensive minds in football makes for great theater. What is it about Mike Macdonald that has made him such a great head coach so quickly? Macdonald’s biggest strength is his ability to relate to players and to be authentic in stating that he doesn’t have all the answers, looking to his players to tap into their experience and expertise, along with a flexibility to do what works, rather than stay committed to a specific scheme. The matchup between Macdonald and Ben Johnson is a rematch of the 2024 meeting between the two when the Lions put 42 points on the board, which is tied for the most put up against a Macdonald defense in the NFL. (The Miami Dolphins beat the Baltimore Ravens 42-38 in Week 2 of the 2022 season in Macdonald’s first year as defensive coordinator for the Ravens.) It’s the second straight week that Macdonald will face off against one of the best offensive play callers in the league, so it will certainly be interesting to see what he can do after shutting down Andy Reid and the offense of the Kansas City Chiefs to the tune of three points. 2. What’s going on with Sam Darnold? His 2024 and 2025 were both so good, and this season he doesn’t look the same. Is this a loss of Klint Kubiak problem, or is there another underlying issue? Darnold put up big production numbers in 2024 and 2025, but in all of his worst games across both seasons, he was susceptible to pressure. Most of those bad games over those two years involved pressure, which led to sacks, fumbles, and interceptions. Between the performance of the Seahawks offensive line regressing a bit compared to its 2025 performance and a glute injury Darnold suffered early in the season opener against the Patriots, the issues pressure has created for Darnold have not gone away. Add in a run game that has struggled with the loss of Kenneth Walker in free agency, Zach Charbonnet having yet to play in 2026 coming back from a surgically repaired ACL, and rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price landing on injured reserve. With that said, there is no doubt that there has been enough of a difference from Kubiak to new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury that there has been an adjustment period for Darnold, and his decision-making has not been where it should be in the new system. He looked better against Kansas City, but still tossed an interception on an ill-advised throw. A Klint Kubiak chart? pic.twitter.com/li2eXUOVeG — Box Score Scout (@boxscorescout) October 16, 2026 The hope from fans now seems to be that the addition of Nelson and the return of Charbonnet and Price to the field can take some of the pressure off Darnold, requiring him to do less and just let the defense do its thing. 3. Hey, both our teams made a big trade! How is the Seahawks offensive line, and how much does Quenton Nelson help fortify Seattle up front? It’s no secret that the Seahawks had an offensive line that struggled for a very long time, and the 2025 line seemed to have brought about an end to that era. The 2026 line has taken a small step back in terms of both opening holes in the run game and protecting Darnold in the pocket due to the arrival of a new offensive coordinator and an injury to starting right guard Anthony Bradford, which had Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens rotating in as replacements. Bradford returned against the Chiefs, and the difference was noticeable, but when given the opportunity to add a six-time All-Pro guard in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, it’s a no-brainer. Add in that Bradford reappeared on the injury report Thursday as limited, and the move to add Nelson makes even more sense. With Nelson now in the fold, he’s set to take over at left guard, with 2025 first-round pick Grey Zabel sliding to right guard and Bradford taking a seat on the bench. It’s the first time Bradford has been out of the starting lineup for any reason other than injury since his rookie season in 2023, so how he handles it will be an interesting situation for Seattle fans to monitor, even if it has no impact on the Week 8 matchup between these two teams. 4. Is there any way to stop JSN? How do you propose is the best way to try to slow him down? The best way to slow down or stop JSN seems to be to hire Shane Waldron as offensive coordinator. On a serious note, the only way opponents have found to slow JSN is to slow down the run game and then pressure Darnold before he’s able to get the ball to JSN in passing situations. As noted above, an inability to move the ball on the ground on early downs and the offense finding itself in third and long, or other unfavorable passing situations, has created a situation where Darnold may not have the time to get to JSN in the progression. Teams have tried jamming him at the line, bracketing him, and everything else, but the reality is JSN is simply on another level and delivering All-Pro performances week in and week out. "OK let's bracket JSN and get four eyes on him. Let's jam him at the line, too. That'll do it." *33 yards later* pic.twitter.com/zEsP9iBVAD — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 29, 2026 5. How do you think this plays out on Monday Night Football, and do you think Jadarian Price and/or Zach Charbonnet play this week? I guess that Charbonnet makes his return to the field against the Bears, but that Price won’t be back in the lineup for another week or two. As for a prediction on the outcome, in primetime matchups between evenly matched teams, if there is a difference of two or more time zones between their home cities, the team whose home city is further West wins a disproportionate amount of the time. Thus, for the second week in a row, I am expecting the Seahawks to win at home in primetime. Seattle 27, Bears 24

title: Jeffery Simmons is a ‘red-level’ defender that Super Bowl teams need
summary: What do Leonard Williams, Jalen Carter, Chris Jones, Fletcher Cox, and Aaron Donald all have in common? They’re all difference-making, All-Pro-level interior defenders who won Super Bowls. The Chicago Bears believe they just acquired one who can help them get there. At his press conference earlier today, Bears general manager Ryan Poles was asked what […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Indianapolis Colts during the third quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images What do Leonard Williams, Jalen Carter, Chris Jones, Fletcher Cox, and Aaron Donald all have in common? They’re all difference-making, All-Pro-level interior defenders who won Super Bowls. The Chicago Bears believe they just acquired one who can help them get there. At his press conference earlier today, Bears general manager Ryan Poles was asked what the trade for Jeffery Simmons means to him after a “five-year journey” to get the position right. “Yeah, you probably go all the way back to the first free agency when I took a shot there,” Poles said about his signing of Larry Ogunjobi, who failed his physical and had the contract rescinded. “I remember having conversations with you guys, and I hear it all the time; it’s like, ‘Does Poles see value in offensive linemen and defensive linemen?’ I’m well aware of the impact that those guys have on football teams,” he said. “If you do the research, you know, Super Bowl teams, really, probably you go back to 2018; since then, they all have what we call a red-level interior defensive lineman. So in order to get to there, you need one. I really believe that.” “So we’ve been searching, but the draft, again, when you go best available, sometimes the draft doesn’t provide that to you. Sometimes I know free agency really doesn’t do that at that level. It’s very hard for guys to get out of the building when they have all of those things that we’re talking about. So, we’ve been searching.” The 29-year-old Simmons has 4 Pro Bowl nods and has been named to 3 All-Pro Teams. “It was an opportunity that we had to jump on,” Poles said af the chance to trade for Simmons. “I’ve talked to you guys before in a lot of different situations. We’re going to stay opportunistic. We’re going to stay flexible. If something presents itself, we’ll see how does this fit, and this is one that we felt like we could make work. And again, it’s going to help us short-term and long-term.” Simmons is at practice today, and he’s scheduled to meet the media after. Getting right to work 💪 pic.twitter.com/iuu9xTjHS9 — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 30, 2026 Poles said it was up to the coaches if Simmons will play this week. The Bears will have one more regular practice tomorrow and have a walk-through before playing the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen held a pre-practice presser and said , “The more he (Simmons) can digest, the more opportunities there will be for him on the field. This will be a work in progress.” My guess is he’ll make his Chicago Bears debut under the lights in Seattle.

title: Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks: Keys to a Chicago victory
summary: In the race for the NFC crown, the Chicago Bears and the Seattle Seahawks each took big swings this week to shore themselves up for the second half of the season. The Bears obviously made the huge trade for Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, while the Seahawks landed Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks catches a touchdown pass against Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the race for the NFC crown, the Chicago Bears and the Seattle Seahawks each took big swings this week to shore themselves up for the second half of the season. The Bears obviously made the huge trade for Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, while the Seahawks landed Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. Now the Bears and Seahawks face off on Monday Night Football with a lot at stake. These two teams play in the two best divisions in the conference. The Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions. Their record may be 4-3, but they’re hitting their stride, coming off a 20-3 beatdown of the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs. This game should be a great Monday night game, truly a playoff-type atmosphere. The Bears are eager to show they’re ready to hang with the NFL’s best. The Seahawks want to show they haven’t fallen off from their Super Bowl run. So we got our crew to weigh in on what it’s going to take for the Bears to go to one of the toughest stadiums in the NFL and come back with the W. Sam: The biggest defensive test since the Vikings game looms for Caleb and Ben as they go on the road to one of the toughest and loudest stadiums in the league to play in. The Bears will have to take what the defense gives them and grind out long drives to keep JSN off the field. On defense — pressure Sam Darnold and double, heck, triple JSN if you have to. Thieneman over the top, please. Josh: Caleb needs to level up and display all of his powers, ranging from sack avoidance to completion percentage to explosive plays. Monangai is likely out, and the run game is not as powerful. Defense is just going to have to mitigate damage. Ben needs to be smart and tricky at the same time. Jeff Berckes: The Seahawks have the best defense by DVOA. The Bears counter with one of the best offenses in the league with Caleb Williams under center. Best on best in a hostile environment – Ben Johnson needs to use that extra rest to his advantage with a game plan that gets the running game back on track to maximize play action. On the other side of the ball… make someone other than JSN beat you. He’s the best receiver in the league and the corners have been rough all year – special attention to him every single play. Mongo Peanut: The Bears have to contain JSN. He’s the lone offensive weapon that can beat you on a Seattle team still trying to figure out their running game. You won’t keep JSN from catching the ball, but you have to keep him from turning 10-yard catches into 40-yard house calls. ECD: Offense: Keep as balanced as possible and stay ahead of the chains. It’ll be a classic “immovable object vs unstoppable force” matchup that’ll require strict discipline and situational awareness. Defense: Do… something. At least bracket JSN as much as possible and find a way to rattle Sam Darnold’s cage. This unit has to play much better on the road than they have in previous weeks. P.S. Let’s wrap up that trade for a defensive difference-maker soon. (Editor’s note: This piece was mostly written before Thursday’s big trade!) Special Teams: Let Zavion Thomas cook. He’s recording longer kick returns each week as he gets more opportunities. And keep the FG attempts to a minimum – Seattle is a notorious place to attempt long-range kicks. What are your keys to the game?

title: NFL Predictions: Can the Bears’ defense slow down the Seahawks’ offense?
summary: A Monday Night Football matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Seattle Seahawks is a circle-the-calendar game that NFL fans got excited about on schedule release day. Those games don’t always feel quite as big once the season gets rolling, but this one gets the full court press of hype (even more so with each […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 26: Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks is tackled by safety Jonathan Owens #36 of the Chicago Bears during the third quarter of an NFL football game, at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images A Monday Night Football matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Seattle Seahawks is a circle-the-calendar game that NFL fans got excited about on schedule release day. Those games don’t always feel quite as big once the season gets rolling, but this one gets the full court press of hype (even more so with each team making a big-time trade). The (5-2) Bears are coming off a prime-time win over the New England Patriots, and the (4-3) Seahawks are coming off a prime-time win over the Kansas City Chiefs. These are two legit Super Bowl contenders. Ben Johnson’s Bears have one of the NFL’s most explosive offenses, and Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks again have one of the league’s most suffocating defenses, but this game might come down to the other side of the ball. Can Chicago’s defense slow down a Seahawks offense with a refocused rushing attack and one of the game’s best wide receivers, Jaxon Smith-Njigba? The Bears’ huge trade for Jeffery Simmons, who has more tackles for loss since 2021 than any other defensive tackle in the NFL, will immediately help the run defense, and his ability to collapse the pocket will immediately help Chicago’s pass rush. I could see him on a limited snap count since he won’t know the calls, twists, and stunts, but he’ll play in some obvious passing or running situations. But JSN will still be a problem. Smith-Njigba, the 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year, is having an even better 2026, averaging 8.3 receptions and 123.9 receiving yards per game. He’s the type of game-altering talent who can win a game on his own. So far, Chicago’s defense has played better than many expected, but I don’t know how they’ll limit JSN. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have his over/under on receptions at 7.5 and receiving yards at 99.5, and while those are high — relatively speaking — they seem easily attainable for him vs. Chicago’s secondary. The Bears don’t have a corner on the roster who can hang with him. But to be fair, neither do most teams. I like the over on both of those. My guess is the Bears will be focused on stopping the run, knowing JSN will get his, while trying to heat up Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold into making mistakes. And now with a game-wrecking defensive tackle in Simmons, the Bears won’t need to blitz as much, so they’ll be able to keep a safety over the top of JSN a few more times. Another over I like is Caleb Williams’ rushing yards, which is at 21.5. This will be his third game back after the hamstring injury, and the extra rest following their Thursday nighter should have his legs feeling good enough to take off when the opportunity presents itself. If you were wondering about the over/under for Caleb’s passing yards, it’s at 227.5. Considering the most passing yards Seattle’s defense has allowed this year is 189, by Justin Herbert and Brock Purdy, that’s a decent-sized leap by the oddsmakers and what they think of Williams. I like the over here as well, but not by much, and mostly because I think the Bears may try the short passing game in place of the run, especially if Kyle Monangai misses another game. As for the game itself, the Bears are a 3-point underdog, and I was teetering on who to pick in what I expect to be a close game, but the Simmons deal has me feeling too good to pick against the Bears. title: Bengals ditched under-center during 35-point second half vs. Ravens
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ attempt to be a more balanced team by playing more under-center has not gone well so far this season. Sunday was another example of that. The Bengals ran under-center on 37% of their plays during the first half. The result of that was 59 total yards with no points scored, as they […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals’ attempt to be a more balanced team by playing more under-center has not gone well so far this season. Sunday was another example of that. The Bengals ran under-center on 37% of their plays during the first half. The result of that was 59 total yards with no points scored, as they trailed 13-0 at halftime. During the second half, the Bengals came out and went under-center on 2 of their first 4 plays. After that, they decided to mostly ditch under-center for the rest of the game. They ran only 2 of the next 27 plays from under-center for the rest of the half. One of them was a Samaje Perine touchdown from the 1-yard line, and the other was a Drew Sample touchdown reception for the final score of the Bengals’ 35-13 victory. Those two plays show that there is still going to be times for the under-center offense, but they should use it sporadically to supplement what Burrow does best, and that is scanning the field from out of shotgun. The Bengals ran just 13% of their plays from under-center during the second half when Joe Burrow was on the field. He was able to sit with a commanding lead for the final drive of the game, so that is not factored into the percentage here. The result of the five second-half possessions he played was five straight touchdown drives. The Bengals let Burrow operate almost exclusively from the shotgun, hitting big play after big play during the second half. Tee Higgins was the biggest beneficiary of that move after halftime. After being shut out in the first half, Tee went off for 6 receptions, 148 receiving yards, and the touchdown that gave the Bengals their first lead of the game. Burrow to Higgins for the touchdown and the Bengals go up 14-13. pic.twitter.com/rAjpkkWrc1 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 I thought playing from the shotgun even helped the running game out this week. While it wasn’t a big rushing day statistically, the running backs were able to make some guys miss when their number was called. Perine had a nice 15-yard run out of shotgun, and then finished off the third straight scoring possession of the second half with a touchdown run from under-center. That is the perfect time for them to use the under-center game. Samaje Perine, I love you man pic.twitter.com/ek8qiDEHS0 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Samaje Perine runs it in for the Bengals third straight possession ending in a touchdown of the second half. pic.twitter.com/yK7k47tcFV — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Chase Brown and Samaje Perine will still need to produce at a higher clip at times this season, but ditching under-center and letting Joe Burrow do what he does best in the second half of this Baltimore game was the right call. That decision helped the Bengals move to 4-2 on the season, and they notched a critical divisional win on the road.

title: Cashius Howell could redeem the Bengals for their Shemar Stewart selection
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals beat the Baltimore Ravens in a wild 35-13 blowout that saw Joe Burrow and the offense completely shut out in the first half. It’s not often you see a team pull off a comeback and a blowout in the same game. Buried beneath the headlines, though, was the fact that 2025 first-round […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals beat the Baltimore Ravens in a wild 35-13 blowout that saw Joe Burrow and the offense completely shut out in the first half. It’s not often you see a team pull off a comeback and a blowout in the same game. Buried beneath the headlines, though, was the fact that 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart was a healthy scratch, meaning the Bengals decided they had a better chance of winning without him on the field. That’s not normal for a guy selected No. 17 overall. Stewart has two sacks to his name so far in his career but has played just 17 snaps this season. He missed the first few weeks after suffering a hyperextended knee at the very beginning of training camp, but he’s healthy now. Despite his freakish athleticism, the Bengals still decided they didn’t need him to help rush the passer against Baltimore. That decision could also reflect the confidence they have in rookie second-round pick Cashius Howell, who brought down Tyler Huntley in the backfield on Sunday for the first sack of his young career. Howell was the Bengals’ first selection in the 2026 NFL Draft, coming in the second round after the team traded its first-round pick to the New York Giants for Dexter Lawrence. He’s been showing flashes of his potential throughout the season, and it’s becoming increasingly clear that both Howell and former sixth-round pick Cedric Johnson have moved ahead of Stewart on the depth chart. What’s interesting about the situation is that Stewart and Howell, both former Texas A&M edge rushers, are practically physical opposites. When the Bengals used their first-round pick on Stewart, they drafted the player they believed he could become, not necessarily the player he already was. At 6-foot-5 and 270 pounds, Stewart has the prototypical size the Bengals covet in their 4-3 edge rushers, along with an almost absurd combination of strength and athleticism. What he didn’t have was production. Despite all those physical gifts, Stewart recorded just 4.5 sacks over his three-year college career at Texas A&M. Howell, meanwhile, is a little smaller than the edge rushers the Bengals typically target in the draft. At 6-foot-3 and 250 pounds, he doesn’t quite fit their traditional mold. What he does have, however, is production. Howell racked up 11.5 sacks during the 2025 season for the Aggies, proving he could consistently get into opposing backfields. When he was still available in the second round, it was a pleasant surprise to see the Bengals step outside their comfort zone and select a productive pass rusher who didn’t necessarily check all their usual boxes. So far, that decision appears to be paying off. According to PFF, Howell ranks fifth among rookie pass rushers with 13 total pressures. He’s also played 158 snaps this season compared to Stewart’s 17. That’s a pretty telling difference, especially considering Stewart was selected 17th overall just one year earlier. There are reports that multiple teams are keeping an eye on Stewart ahead of the trade deadline, hoping they can develop him into the player the Bengals envisioned when they drafted him. And if Stewart is going to spend his Sundays watching from the sidelines in street clothes, why shouldn’t the Bengals see what they can get for him? It’s still early in Stewart’s career, and his physical tools haven’t gone anywhere. There’s certainly a chance he could develop into a productive NFL pass rusher. But right now, the Bengals appear to have more confidence in a second-round rookie and a former sixth-round pick than they do in a player they invested the 17th overall selection in just a year ago. If Howell and Johnson continue producing, the Bengals may become even more comfortable with the idea of moving on from Stewart. And considering how much the Bengals invested in him, that would be a pretty remarkable development.
author: Jason Garrison

title: Even without Jeffery Simmons, the Titans are still a team to be wary of
summary: The Tennessee Titans may have traded away one of the most dominant defensive tackles in the NFL, but don’t expect Cincinnati Bengals center Ted Karras to shed any tears over Jeffery Simmons’ departure. And don’t expect him to take the Titans lightly when they come to town this Sunday. With Cincinnati sitting at 4-2 and […]
full_text: The Tennessee Titans may have traded away one of the most dominant defensive tackles in the NFL, but don’t expect Cincinnati Bengals center Ted Karras to shed any tears over Jeffery Simmons’ departure. And don’t expect him to take the Titans lightly when they come to town this Sunday. With Cincinnati sitting at 4-2 and an opportunity to improve to 5-2 in an increasingly competitive AFC North, Karras knows exactly what’s at stake. The Bengals have a chance to strengthen their position in the division, and the veteran center isn’t about to let the absence of one superstar turn a must-win game into a trap. “I’m out here bleeding on a Thursday to win this ball game.” Ted Karras on Titans trade of Jeffery Simmons to Bears: “That’s a top three dynamic D-tackle in the league. So obviously, there's going to be some adjustments made. But we still got Franklin-Myers. Still got a good group coming in, and so we got to be ready to go and beat the… pic.twitter.com/gPFaSeb50A — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) October 29, 2026 That pretty much sums up the mentality of a player who has spent 11 seasons in the NFL and understands that there are no automatic victories, regardless of who’s lining up on the other side of the ball. Simmons’ departure certainly changes the equation. The Titans sent the All-Pro defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears, removing one of the league’s most disruptive interior defenders from a matchup against a Cincinnati offense that has been finding its rhythm. Karras acknowledged just how significant that loss could be for Tennessee. “That’s a top three dynamic D-tackle in the league,” he said. “So obviously, there’s going to be some adjustments made. But they still got Franklin-Myers. They still got a good group coming in, and we got to be ready to go and beat the Titans.” Karras isn’t assuming the Titans’ defensive front will suddenly become an easy assignment. In fact, he singled out John Franklin-Myers as a player who demands considerable respect. “We have to take a deeper look at it and kind of try to predict how they’re gonna play without him,” Karras said. “They got good players. John Franklin-Myers has been playing at the top of his game for a long time. I remember him when he was young on the Jets. He’s been dangerous forever.” For Cincinnati, the bigger picture extends well beyond Sunday’s opponent. “We’re in a position to go 5-2 and kind of set ourselves up in a tight divisional race here with everyone still winning,” Karras said. “And luckily, we got two divisional opponents playing each other this week. This is a stretch in the season where hopefully we can take some control. So, we gotta go.” The Bengals’ offensive line has been an important part of the team’s recent success, and Karras believes the unit is beginning to develop the consistency necessary to sustain that momentum. “When we’re scoring points, obviously the O-line is doing their job appropriately,” he said. “We still have a lot to keep working on, but I thought we put some solid performances out there and we need another one on Sunday.” Karras credited both the coaching staff and the players for the improvement, emphasizing that preparation and individual execution have helped the line work more effectively as a unit. “I think we’re preparing well, I think the coaches have us prepared well, and the guys are going out there and executing great individual blocks and working together really well,” he said. “So proud of these guys and gotta keep it going.” But the veteran center also understands that October success means little if a team cannot continue improving as the season progresses. “We got to keep growing and hit our stride here in November, December, and that’s what separates NFL football teams.”

summary: The Cincinnati Bengals put the NFL world on notice this past weekend with an eye-opening 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens. full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals put the NFL world on notice this past weekend with an eye-opening 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The Bengals were horrendous, and I truly mean horrendous, in the 1st half but put together the best 2nd half in recent memory in all three phases. The reason Cincinnati was able to turn things around was that the stars stepped up on both sides of the football. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins were quite literally flawless offensively for the Bengals, scoring five touchdowns in all five possessions. Burrow finished the day with 292 passing yards and four touchdowns while Higgins racked up 148 yards and a touchdown on six catches. Chase reeled in five catches for 62 yards and a touchdown but also demanded an astronomical amount of attention from the Ravens’ defense. An interesting fact after this game is that the Bengals are now 13-4 in their last 17 games when Burrow, Chase, and Higgins are on the field together. The #Bengals hold a 13-4 record in the last 17 games in which Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins, and Ja'Marr Chase are all active. #WhoDey — SleeperBengals (@SleeperBengals) October 27, 2026 Burrow and Higgins have had their fair share of injuries, and the trio has not been on the field together as much as everyone may think. But when they are, the Bengals have been borderline unstoppable.

title: Bengals vs. Titans odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 8 matchup
summary: The NFL world was shaken on Thursday morning when the Tennessee Titans sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. Much of the NFL is still grading the trade, but the Cincinnati Bengals are likely relieved by the timing, as they host the Titans this week. This matchup pits two teams that seem to be going […]
full_text: The NFL world was shaken on Thursday morning when the Tennessee Titans sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. Much of the NFL is still grading the trade, but the Cincinnati Bengals are likely relieved by the timing, as they host the Titans this week. This matchup pits two teams that seem to be going in opposite directions. Tennessee is 1-6, and their offense is struggling to gel together around quarterback Cam Ward. Meanwhile, Cincinnati just took off like a jet last week, scoring 35 unanswered against the Baltimore Ravens. It seems pretty clear-cut how this game is expected to play out, but how do oddsmakers and experts feel about it? Odds The Bengals are currently 11.5-point favorites against the Titans, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the biggest spread Cincinnati has had this season. They were only 6.5-point favorites against the Miami Dolphins coming off two straight losses. Safe to say the number got a little bigger after Tennessee traded Simmons this week. The point total is set at 46.5 points combined. The real wild card for these bets is which Bengals’ defense is going to show up. Are they going to give up 200 rushing yards, or will they be able to shut it down like last week against Derrick Henry? Expert Picks All of ESPN’s 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has a consensus of Cincinnati winning from their six experts None of NFL.com’s five experts are taking the Titans NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick Initially, I was worried this may be a trap game at home for the Bengals. Sometimes this team will just drop a terrible game after a huge win. That happens especially when they are playing down to a bad team’s level. I’m not sure how the Simmons trade might impact that, but I am hopeful the Titans are a bit more deflated coming out than fighting even harder. Either way, Burrow and this offense shouldn’t have any trouble scoring and moving the ball. Their job got a lot easier without Simmons in the middle of that defense. The only thing I’m worried about offensively with the Titans is their running backs breaking off a few big runs. Bengals 41, Titans 13 Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! title: Bengals Film Room: Joe Burrow is firmly back in the MVP conversation
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals struggled to get anything going offensively in the first half against the Ravens. Joe Burrow was just 6/12 for 43 yards passing through the first two quarters of the game. Ja’Marr Chase gave a fiery speed at halftime, and Joe Burrow and the rest of the offense came out looking like a […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals struggled to get anything going offensively in the first half against the Ravens. Joe Burrow was just 6/12 for 43 yards passing through the first two quarters of the game. Ja’Marr Chase gave a fiery speed at halftime, and Joe Burrow and the rest of the offense came out looking like a completely different team. They looked like the one we have grown accustomed to seeing over the years offensively. The Burrow second-half performance is going to put him right back in conversations for league MVP this season. If the Bengals keep winning, that stuff will take care of itself. Burrow and the Bengals received the opening kickoff of the second half. Burrow made one of the most anticipatory throws I have ever seen on the drive. He hit Tee Higgins over the middle on a ball that Roquan Smith certainly felt was coming directly to him. The level of trust that Burrow has in Tee Higgins has been apparent all season. It has never been clearer that the Bengals have two No. 1 wide receivers on this team. The ultimate level of trust for Tee Higgins from Joe Burrow pic.twitter.com/xT46rx8ZlZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Bengals were able to cash in the touchdown later in the drive. Burrow knew he would have outside leverage on Mike Gesicki, and he motioned him closer to the line. He placed the ball with pinpoint accuracy, allowing his big-bodied tight end to go up and make the catch. This cut the Ravens’ lead to 13-7 and showed that the Bengals were ready to come out like a different team than in the first half. Burrow knew he was going to Mike G all the way here, and the Bengals cut the lead to 13-7. pic.twitter.com/1fnRPJrcWu — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The defense held the Ravens offense to a three-and-out on their first series of the second half. After an electric Dohnte Meyers return of 31 yards, the Bengals started their second offensive series with less than 50 yards to the end zone. A destination they quickly reached with a couple of big plays to Tee Higgins again. Burrow first hit Higgins for a 19-yard gain on the outside, and then found him over the middle for a 13-yard touchdown pass. Just like that, the Bengals had taken the first lead of the game. One of several chunk plays from Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins in the second half. pic.twitter.com/e0GFuCDutv — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Burrow to Higgins for the touchdown and the Bengals go up 14-13. pic.twitter.com/rAjpkkWrc1 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Ravens were able to drive down the field on their next possession. Instead of opting for the short field goal and regaining the lead back, they chose to roll the dice on a fourth down. The Bengals defense forced the turnover on downs, and the offense went back on the field. They continued finding the hot receiver in Tee Higgins. This time for another big gain of 44 yards. He absolutely toasted Marlon Humphrey to get open for his quarterback. Even though the ball slipped out of Burrow’s hand, it was another huge chunk play. It wasn’t pretty, but Joe Burrow completes the wobbler to Tee Higgins for a 44 yard gain. pic.twitter.com/N2ofH6oyrW — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Bengals were able to even get an explosive run for a big 15-yard gain on this drive. Samaje Perine took the handoff from Burrow out of the shotgun and bulldozed his way for the big run down inside the Baltimore red zone. Shortly after that, he was able to run through the Kyle Hamilton tackle attempt at the goal line, extending the Bengals’ lead to 21-13. Samaje Perine, I love you man pic.twitter.com/ek8qiDEHS0 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Samaje Perine runs it in for the Bengals third straight possession ending in a touchdown of the second half. pic.twitter.com/yK7k47tcFV — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Bengals again were able to get multiple explosive plays on their next possession. The first was a catch-and-run by Ja’Marr Chase for a 30-yard gain. There goes that man again, Ja’Marr Chase with the catch-and-run of 30 yards. pic.twitter.com/GsaDKrOWvE — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The very next play, Burrow went deep down the sideline to Higgins. Perfect placement on the throw while standing in with pressure in his face, Burrow delivered a fantastic ball. This gain went for 43 yards to Higgins. Burrow stands in and delivers another big play down the field to Tee Higgins. Higgins finished the game with 6 receptions for 148 yards and a touchdown on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/Fmnehb8V8k — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Then, it was Ja’Marr Chase’s turn to find the end zone for Cincinnati in the second half. He absolutely torched corner Nate Wiggins off the line. He made sure to let him know about it afterward too. This score put the Bengals up 28-13. Chase cooked his ass and let him know about it for the Bengals 4th straight touchdown drive of the second half. pic.twitter.com/kvgHKxWyRM — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 After a Barrett Carter tipped pass led to a Demetrius Knight Jr. interception, the Bengals offense was once again right back on the field. This time Joe Burrow was able to hit Drew Sample for one of the most majestic touchdown plays you will ever see. This capped off a 16/18 for 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half for Burrow. Just an electric offensive performance from Burrow, putting him squarely back into the conversation for MVP. Slow Motion + Foo Fighters Music = My love letter to Drew Sample pic.twitter.com/kLE2fxtX2k — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026
