title: Despite the narrative, Browns’ pass rush is better than Myles Garrett’s group last year
summary: Like most things in life, two things can be true while seeming counterintuitive to each other. While the Cleveland Browns are winning games, sitting at 5-2 and at the top of the AFC North, there are regular concerns about the team’s ability to get quick pressure off the edge to impact the quarterback. DE Jared […]
full_text: Like most things in life, two things can be true while seeming counterintuitive to each other. While the Cleveland Browns are winning games, sitting at 5-2 and at the top of the AFC North , there are regular concerns about the team’s ability to get quick pressure off the edge to impact the quarterback. DE Jared Verse doesn’t have a sack , leading at least one of us to wonder if the Browns should trade the prize piece from the DE Myles Garrett deal . The concern is indicated by all the NFL trade deadline rumors connecting Cleveland to pass rushers . While the narrative that edge pressure is a problem is true, the Browns defense has also been very good and, as a whole, has been getting a lot of pressure, just not in the way that fans are used to with Garrett. In fact, this year’s defense has gotten more sacks and pressures than last year’s , when Garrett was on the way to setting the single-season sack record: “Four equals one. We say it all the time,” a Browns source tells me. “There’s a rush plan within the game plan. It’s worked on and met about. It’s practiced.” The Browns’ 20 sacks and 108 pressures to this point outpace the 18 sacks and 81 pressures at the same time last year, when Myles Garrett set the all-time single-season record for sacks… But they’ve gotten more production from the interior of the defensive line. Mason Graham and Maliek Collins have combined for 7½ sacks. Would it be helpful if Cleveland was able to get quick pressure off the edge? Certainly. It does seem, however, that DC Mike Rutenberg’s plan is about causing havoc, more than creating immediate pressure from just the edge players: “Our DBs have been really good in coverage,” says a second team source. “Creating pressure with his exotic looks up front and rush stunts, especially with the defensive tackles. Better rush discipline with the group.” Rutenberg has also quickly adjusted from the blowout loss in Week 1, showing signs of a good coordinator whose focus is to put his players in the best position to succeed: Removing the Week 1 game against Jacksonville when the Jaguars put up 34 points, the Browns rank fourth in the NFL in total defensive EPA, behind only the Vikings, Seahawks and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The defense has kept Cleveland in games long enough for the offense to put together five game-winning drives. In total, 11 defenders have sacks for the Browns so far this season: Mason Graham – 4 Maliek Collins – 3.5 Isaiah McGuire – 3 Adin Huntington – 2.5 Sam Kamara – 1 Quincy Williams – 1 Sam Williams – 1 Mike Hall Jr. – 1 Carson Schwesinger – 1 Ronnie Hickman – 1 Grant Delpit – 1 Somehow, without Garrett or anyone getting a ton of quick pressure off the edge by themselves, Cleveland’s defense continues to be top-notch and is racking up sacks and pressures at a higher rate than last season. Adding a quick pressure player off the edge could make things better, but the key will be whether they fit into the system Rutenberg and company have put into place and found success with already. Are you surprised by the pressure and sack numbers this year compared to Garrett and company last year at this time? Join the conversation! title: Myles Garrett, Micah Parsons injury updates could impact Browns NFL draft stock
summary: For two teams that do not play against each other this season, the Cleveland Browns and Los Angeles Rams are uniquely linked this season because of the Myles Garrett trade. While the Rams bounced back in Week 7, injuries continue to be a big story for a team that was expected to be the Super […]
full_text: For two teams that do not play against each other this season, the Cleveland Browns and Los Angeles Rams are uniquely linked this season because of the Myles Garrett trade . While the Rams bounced back in Week 7 , injuries continue to be a big story for a team that was expected to be the Super Bowl favorite and started the year with four losses already. It all started with Los Angeles’ loss in Week 1, in Australia , which was followed by Garrett having surgery and going on injured reserve . In early October, the Rams still didn’t have a timeline for when Garrett would return , and he is now set to miss Week 8 , with uncertainty about when he could return to practice. Once Los Angeles opens Garrett’s return-to-practice timeline, it still could be multiple weeks before he’s back on the field. With the NFL trade deadline two game weeks away, the Rams could be in a difficult position after Week 10. On top of that, with or without Garrett, LA looks like they will be facing fellow star pass rusher Micah Parsons on Thanksgiving Eve against the Green Bay Packers: Sources: The #Packers and star Micah Parsons are targeting a Thanksgiving Eve return to the field in the showdown against the #Rams . The full story: https://t.co/X7M40l6dbk https://t.co/X7M40l6dbk — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 31, 2026 Parsons had ACL surgery after being injured last year, but has taken longer to return to the field than others who had a similar injury and timeframe. The NFL is a week-to-week league, so assuming anything about what will happen in Week 12 of the season is a bit foolhardy. By then, Garrett could have returned and helped the Rams turn their season all the way around, while the Packers could have hit a slump without their top pass rusher. For now, Browns fans will continue to keep one eye on anything and everything related to the Rams, while looking for their team to make a big push to the NFL playoffs.

title: As the trade deadline approaches, should Browns listen to Jared Verse offers?
summary: This time during the NFL season, two things are the most topical: Game results each weekend and the looming NFL trade deadline. The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a great start with a 5-2-0 record. Could a trade help this roster, or perhaps the Browns should sit tight and ride with what brought them. […]
full_text: This time during the NFL season, two things are the most topical: Game results each weekend and the looming NFL trade deadline. The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a great start with a 5-2-0 record. Could a trade help this roster, or perhaps the Browns should sit tight and ride with what brought them. RELATED: VERSE UNAFRAID TO TALK DESPITE ZERO SACKS The NFL trade deadline is November 10. The league instituted a deadline for teams to prevent clubs from stacking rosters right before the playoffs and keep competitive balance towards the end of the season. This year’s trade deadline has generated a lot of interest in the defensive line. This market has already begun. The Indianapolis Colts traded DE DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers. The Tennessee Titans traded star DL Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. The Browns’ pass rush is not getting quick pressure from the defensive ends this year and hasn’t been the same since the team traded away All-World pass rusher Myles Garrett. In that trade, Cleveland received Jared Verse, who had gone to two Pro Bowls in two seasons, and was voted the “NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year” when he came into the league in 2024. The idea was that Verse would fill in for Garrett, but not take his place. In just seven games, the Browns have 20 sacks collectively. Verse has zero. This is a guy who had 7.5 last year and 4.5 as a rookie. What exactly is wrong with Verse? Should the Browns coaching staff keep waiting for him to blow up the opposition during passing plays? Is there a scheme or fit issue? Or maybe, should Cleveland make him available before the trade deadline? Well-Versed For months since the Garrett trade, all we have heard is that Verse wasn’t going to fill Garrett’s shoes, but was an exceptional athlete and would provide a very good pass rush. While with the Los Angeles Rams, Verse had 58 tackles last year and 66 the year before. Ink noted that he was a good run stopper, along with his sack numbers and his ability to get into the backfield and hunt quarterbacks. 27 QB hits in 2025, along with 36 pressures. And that Verse is a much younger version of Garrett, being just 25 years old. Browns DE Jared Verse said he’s been waiting for rematch with Steelers, not worried about what Cam Hayward said. pic.twitter.com/xs0BRzryND — Scott Petrak ct (@ScottPetrak) October 29, 2026 And yet, here are his stats for this year: Seven starts, 302 defensive snaps,17 total tackles (2.4 on average per game), 4 tackles for loss, 5 QB hits, 0 sacks, 0 forced fumbles, 0 fumble recoveries, 0 batted passes, 0 hurries, 4 knockdowns, 4 pressures, and 3 missed tackles. Other than tackles, he isn’t averaging one of anything per game. This year’s version of the Browns defense, coached by DC Mike Rutenberg, keeps receiving praise week after week. Just not the edge rush portion. On the other side, the Browns lost DE Alex Wright for the year after he was placed on season–ending IR after suffering a ruptured Achilles tendon during training camp. In his place came Isaiah McGuire, who isn’t a better pass rusher or run stopper, with Derek Barnett as his backup. Verse just isn’t getting into the other team’s offensive backfield whatsoever. Plus, he is weak at staying home and offering containment. On occasion, Verse will do this unusual maneuver where he won’t go directly towards the quarterback, but will travel towards the center and then take a hard right. And it’s not like he is playing full games. Currently, his snap count is just 66% of all defensive reps. His pressure rate has dropped significantly this year to just 6.6%, which ranks him #71 among all NFL EDGE rushers. Verse posted a 16.8% pressure rate during the 2025 season while playing for the Rams. His Pro Football Focus pass-rushing grade was 82.2, which ranked him #13. That has sunk to 59.9, which is #73 among 113 qualified EDGE defenders. Needless to say, the Cleveland version of Verse is not the Los Angeles edition the Browns were anticipating. Nobody expected Verse to ball out for 20 sacks, but geez. What is going on? Perhaps it surrounds the fact that Verse came from a 3-4 alignment while with the Rams and is now grouped in the 4-3. Sounds logical, right? This has led to offensive tackles neutralizing his power-first and bull-rush moves. And earlier in the season, because of his reputation, teams were double-teaming him. But that suddenly ceased as offensive coordinators realized it wasn’t necessary. And while Verse has struggled, his backup, Sam Williams, has played pretty well in spite of getting just 36% of defensive snaps while playing part-time. Williams has played in all seven games with zero starts, and has 20 total tackles, 5 tackles for loss, 1 sack, 3 QB hits, 0 forced fumbles, 0 fumble recoveries, 1 batted pass, 1 hurry, 2 knockdowns, 4 pressures, and 4 missed tackles. Unthinkable decision? The league has several pass rushers that are projected to be traded soon. The market for defensive linemen has already begun. The only other pass rushers rumored to be traded, at least as of now, before the November 10 deadline are Los Angeles Chargers EDGE rusher Khalil Mack and Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals. Should the Browns throw Verse’s name into the hat and see if anyone bites? Would the team jump at a strong offer? Verse is one of those EDGE rushers who has had good to very good numbers every year on a consistent basis, but he isn’t going to blow the doors off. This year, his production is more often viewed as mediocre to poor. Then there is the money issue. Verse is in the third year of a four-year $15.1 million deal, with all of it guaranteed. This year he has a cap hit of $2.2 million. Next year that increases to $2.9 million. Next season, the Browns will need to make a decision on Verse’s fifth-year option. That is currently projected to be a fully guaranteed $27.9 million that would be paid in 2028. Verse qualifies for the largest tier as a multi-time Pro Bowler. But there is a hitch: he isn’t playing at that high level. His production is way down. Yes, the Browns could stick it out and see if this is just a one-off, or perhaps he will wake up and produce in the second half of this season. Because Verse was a part of the Garrett trade, everyone has had high expectations for him. This year. Cleveland has a timeline, and currently Verse is included in that plan. Some media folks have pointed out that his presence along the defensive line during passing downs has generated sacks and stats for other Browns defensive players. That rings true in a lot of games across the league. Often, a player will engage two offensive linemen so that another defender can loop around and get to the quarterback on a stunt. For now, everyone is waiting for Verse to show why he was the necessary piece in the Garrett trade. Every team in the NFL is looking for an EDGE rusher. The big question for Cleveland GM Andrew Berry: Which is better for the Browns this year and in following seasons? Have Jared Verse on the roster, or have whichever rookie player they select with whatever draft pick(s) they would receive in a trade? What do you think: Should the Browns look to trade Verse if they get a good enough offer? Even selling low? What trade compensation would you expect to get in return for Verse? Join the conversation! full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns hit the road again this week as they take on the Pittsburgh Steelers. It was just four weeks ago that these two teams met in Cleveland, with the Browns picking up an important divisional win. Since then, the Browns have won two of their past three games, while the Steelers have enjoyed a stretch of patsies to build a three-game winning streak. Sunday’s game is not going to be an easy one for the Browns – you may have heard that they have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003 – but when is anything ever easy for the guys in the orange helmets. A win on Sunday and the Browns not only maintain their hold on first place in the AFC North, but it will give them their first season sweep of the Steelers since 1988. It is the Browns vs. the Steelers in Cleveland’s house of horrors, which is appropriate for Halloween weekend. Jared's already learned how much this one means to the #DawgPound @getspectrum | @jaredverse1 pic.twitter.com/fpPqDvXagl — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 29, 2026 News & Notes In Week 4, Cleveland’s defense had five sacks and two interceptions of Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Cleveland’s defense is ranked No. 7 in red zone defense, while the Steelers are just No. 27 in red zone scoring. The Browns played man coverage on 61 percent of pass plays in the first game against the Steelers. The Steelers are ranked No. 24 in total EPA against man coverage (-5.16) and No. 27 in total pass EPA (-2.91), according to The Athletic. Cleveland’s defense has allowed an opening-drive score in six of their seven games. Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards in Week 7, his first 300-yard passing game as a member of the Browns. The Browns rushed for a season-high in yards (183) and rushing touchdowns (three) in the Week 7 win over Tennessee. In their last five games, the Steelers are No. 5 in third-down conversions (44.8 percent), No. 1 one in rushing yards per carry (5.1) and No. 8 in points per game (26), according to The Athletic. Cleveland’s defense is No. 5 in pressure rate (40 percent) and No. 6 in sacks (20), according to The Athletic. Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren is No. 4 in the league with 855 yards from scrimmage. Cleveland’s defense is No. 1 in the league in tackles for loss (46). The Steelers have one rushing touchdown on the season. Sunday’s game will be just the fifth time since 1999 that the Browns and Steelers have played a game where both teams have a winning record. A Final Quote Cleveland defensive end Jared Verse on the plan for Sunday’s game: “I’m not worried about Cam (Heyward). I’m not worried about their O-line. full_text: The Browns had yet another game-winning drive against the Titans last week, their fifth to correspond with five victories — to improve to 5-2 on the season. Week-to-week, fan confidence increased by 3 percentage points up to 88%, a new season high again. If Cleveland can sweep the Steelers this week, that percentage might shoot up into the 90s. Take Reacts surveys, create Browns polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Dawgs By Nature fans. Then discuss the results with the Dawg Pound. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Besides the confidence meter, the main question we asked this week was focused on what fans felt about the Browns’ offensive outburst last week. Was it a sign that they’ve turned the corner? A fluke? Overall, 51% said that the offense was nice, but attributed much of it to the Titans just sucking. 47% of fans think the offense had indeed turned a corner, while only 2% think it was just a fluke what happened last week. One fan thinks Todd Monken is opening up the offense, but needs to keep at it and break some more tendencies: I feel like Monken is opening up the offense. I think he was going tight too often. I love TIGHT formations, but with a young line and mediocre FB/blocking TEs, I question the fetish. I hope they just dont’ settle. mix it up. go tight every now and then. make the defense rotate their personnel, and just smash them when we have a mismatch. I just hate going TIGHT, after TIGHT, after TIGHT. the defense just gets bigger, bigger and bigger. I keep saying. the defense has the advantage, and if we’re predictable getting even 2 yards into their territory is tough. speed is key. SPREAD EM WIDE!! Corley and Wallace are said to be blocking well. let’s not be too predictable. they have speed too. get them out in space, especially when PIT (or anyone else) isn’t looking for it. 1 target for the whole year on 116 snaps. that’s just not right. Another fan thinks it’s really a combination of things coming together: I think it’s a combination of the Titans suck and we are finding a groove. The offense is going to to get better. You have a lot of young guys out there and a new O-line that is starting to play better together. There are going to be bumps in the road, but this team is improving. On a national scale, fans were asked who the best team in the AFC is, and the Browns actually received 5% of the vote. Don’t shoot the messenger. title: Trade for QB Justin Herbert? Browns fans split; have strong reaction to the idea
summary: When it comes to surprises so far in the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns 5-2 record, sitting atop the AFC North, is among the biggest. There are others, including the Minnesota Vikings being the lone undefeated team and the Los Angeles Chargers being the lone winless squad, but the Browns success in Year 1 […]
full_text: When it comes to surprises so far in the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns 5-2 record, sitting atop the AFC North , is among the biggest. There are others, including the Minnesota Vikings being the lone undefeated team and the Los Angeles Chargers being the lone winless squad, but the Browns success in Year 1 under HC Todd Monken has been fun for Cleveland fans and an interesting storyline for the NFL as a whole. A win in Week 8 would change things greatly for the Browns chances of turning “surprise” into “NFL playoff participants.” Cleveland’s success has come with five come-from-behind wins, with QB Deshaun Watson regaining a version of his elite past late in both halves of games . The rest of the time, the Browns have seen inconsistent play at the quarterback position. That, along with Watson heading into free agency after the season, leaves questions about the future of the position. Enter QB Justin Herbert and the winless Chargers: 🚨This is a serious question. It is not for content or memes. I am legitimately interested in the public opinion.🚨 Justin Herbert is 28 years old. He's got four years left on his deal (+ no trade clause) worth $24M, $36M, $52M, $50.5M. What would you offer in trade for him? — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 12, 2026 So, we asked Browns fans the same question and, so far, they are split almost right down the middle: A quick look at Herbert’s season shows why the idea of trading him is even being discussed publicly at all: 59% completion percentage 5 touchdowns 8 interceptions – Which leads the NFL Career-worst yards per attempt and significantly worst adjusted yards gained per pass attempt (2 strong QB metrics) Passer rating of 68.8 and QBR of 29.3 – By far his career worsts Chargers are 0-6 So, a lot of reasons for Los Angeles to potentially look to trade what was assumed to be their franchise quarterback and lots of reasons for Cleveland fans to be hesitant (or stronger words) about trading for him: As seen in the poll, not everyone was against the idea: A couple of our loyal readers brought up interesting points. First, dawngregry brought some straight facts followed by some opinions on where a trade might land: Then, Spidey mentioned a big variable: Would the Browns be gunshy to pull the trigger on another big QB deal after the Watson failed deal? In the end, a Herbert trade seems highly unlikely for a variety of reasons, including his no-trade clause. Cleveland also seems unlikely to upset the apple cart as they’ll head into the NFL trade deadline with a winning record, at worst, and potentially a commanding lead in the AFC North. Most likely, if Herbert were to be traded, the 2027 NFL offseason would be the earliest, when the Chargers could figure out what their future holds. For now, Browns fans are almost exactly split on the idea of trading for the struggling superstar, but the poll still has a little bit of time to change drastically. title: NFL predictions: Browns-Steelers square off in meaningful midseason match-up for once
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-2) take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. It’s Been 23 Years If I could put the meme from the Titanic here, I would, with respect to it having […]
full_text: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-2) take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. It’s Been 23 Years If I could put the meme from the Titanic here, I would, with respect to it having been 23 years (which is a 22-game losing streak) since the Cleveland Browns have won a road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the regular season. We’ll always have that playoff victory over them, but we’re trying to keep focused on the unfathomable statistic of losing 22 in a row somewhere. Of course, the reason for that has largely been that the Browns have been a bad football team, while Pittsburgh has generally been good. But, it’s not like Cleveland hasn’t been able to beat Pittsburgh during that stretch at all. In fact, at home since 2003, the Browns are 10-13-1, including winning 7 of their last 8 games there. On the road, they are 1-22, with 22 straight losses. That 2003 match-up was one featuring Tim Couch as the Browns’ starting quarterback, as he went 20-of-25 for 208 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT, and 1 rushing TD in a 33-13 victory. Cleveland still have the classic quartet of Kevin Johnson , Quincy Morgan , Andre’ Davis , and Dennis Northcutt as their receivers, with Steve Heiden as their primary tight end. William Green ran 33 times for 115 yards. Pittsburgh was led by Tommy Maddox at quarterback, with Amos Zereoue and Jerome Bettis running and Hines Ward , Plaxico Burress , and Antwaan Randle El as their receivers. Phil Dawson was putting kicks through the uprights for the Browns. I was 14 years old back then, just starting high school. I’m 37 now, having been through college, had a full-time job for awhile, and started a family. It’s time we turned the corner for the Browns, isn’t it? Home-away records sometimes seem less valuable these days. I could go into context and say that Cleveland’s 2-2 road record this year was the team just not being prepared in Week 1, and also because of sloppy rain conditions against the Jets, and not because ‘they weren’t at home.’ But when you just look at the records straight up, the Browns are 3-0 at home. Also 3-0 at home this year? The Pittsburgh Steelers, with wins over the Falcons, Bengals, and Colts. They, like Cleveland, have had a relatively soft schedule this year, but it’s let them build some confidence and work out some things too. This game won’t be easy, but I’m excited for it. Those Darn Slow Starts Last week, I harped on the Browns needing to get their offense rocking, especially with KC Concepcion , and also needed the defense to stop allowing opening-drive scores. Cleveland accomplished half of that with the offense taking off, but the defense found themselves in a 14-0 hole before getting things back on track. Thinking back to the first Steelers game, Pittsburgh began the game with a 17-play, 73-yard drive that took up 9:48 of game clock. Then, until the fourth quarter, their drives were: interception, punt, missed field goal, field goal, punt, punt, and punt. It’s always been a known factor in the NFL that some teams can have greater success on their first drive with well-scripted sequences. But it’s a bit mind-blowing that this defense can play so well the rest of the game — which I’ve attributed to Mike Rutenburg’s ability to make adjustments — but they can’t get that stop, even out of dumb luck, on the first drive. I know Rutenburg would say that it doesn’t matter if that touchdown drive comes on the opening drive, or the fifth drive, they want to stop it. But setting the tone early will be a factor as some of these games get more serious. The last time these teams played, Cleveland erupted for 21 straight points in the second quarter. That isn’t going to happen every week (even though they erupted for 17 points in a row just last week, after being in a hole…) Here are some other notes: The running game was encouraging last week. I like some of the little things we’re seeing improve with team blocking, and I also like the adjustment to go under center more. I think Cleveland, in their efforts to make Deshaun Watson comfortable, have often gone from Shotgun, which can hurt the running game at times. Watson has been much more unphased this year, and I think we’re seeing how being under center can add some things to the ground game, quick passing game, and even springing someone like KC Concepcion open off of playaction. Speaking of Concepcion, the usage of him last week was picture perfect. Keep doing it — he is the one guy who can really propel this offense to the next level, and help open things up for other guys too. The number of crossing routes that Cleveland has started taking advantage of is perfect too. Jaylen Warren is the guy who the Browns need to stop. He’s averaging 5.5 yards per carry on the season, and with the return of Rico Dowdle last week, the duo has been very effective on the ground. I still fear Darnell Washington to a degree. The big tight end had a touchdown catch against the Browns, and has a touchdown catch in each of the past two games. I’d be tempted to put Emmanuel McNeil-Warren on him at times to see what happens. The big X-Factor this week that could throw a wrench in Cleveland’s chances is the fact that Tytus Howard might be out with a concussion. That would put Dawand Jones in as the starting right tackle. We all remember back in 2023, when Jones — in limited action — ‘shut down’ T.J. Watt , which got everyone excited about Jones’ future. It’s been a bit rough since then, and with injuries and lesser playing time, Jones hasn’t looked very sharp during fill-in duty. And then what happens if Jones goes down with an injury? I’m assuming that KT Leveston will be a gameday elevation from the practice squad, but remember, he was outright cut after being a contender for the starting right guard job in camp. Cleveland drafted Austin Barber to be a reserve offensive tackle, but he’s flourished at right guard. I suppose the they could shift Barber to right tackle, Elgton Jenkins to right guard, and then put Luke Wypler at center. On paper, that works for me. However, with the continuity these guys have built up, would they want to switch three linemen as opposed to just one? Fingers crossed that Jones not only stays healthy, but plays has a solid outing. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3.5 point underdogs against the Steelers. The over/under is 39.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about if the running game so a breakthrough this past week, but he just appreciated the collective effort and improvements on first and second down: “Yeah, I mean, I think a lot of the things, we have been seeing improvement over the last couple weeks, so it was great to see the production that we had on Sunday. As far as breakthrough, I don’t know. I don’t know that any of our guys really look at it that way. I think that the things that we’ve been emphasizing to improve, we’ve been. We were a lot better on first and second down, which allowed us to get more runs called. You know, the more you’re on schedule, the more you’ll be able to run the ball. So, as far as breakthrough, I don’t know. I mean, we were certainly really happy to see the production that we did, and we’ll continue to try to improve.” Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg wouldn’t really give an answer to the slow start of the defense each week, other than they treat every drive the same as far as diagnosing what went wrong behind closed doors: In everything we do, when it is to our collective standard, we are constantly trying to get it better. So, whether it’s the first drive, something else, something we’re doing really well, it’s a constant under construction through the week of why, tell the truth, try and figure it out together and fight our a—- off really to fix it. And it’s a really cool process, collectively, as a staff and players.” Special teams coordinator…

title: College football’s top Cowboys draft targets in Week 9
summary: We are getting deep into the college football season as we continue our look at possible draft targets for the Dallas Cowboys in 2027. Florida vs. Georgia Florida and Georgia meet in Atlanta with the Gators’ ground game facing one of its most revealing tests. Georgia has allowed only 91 rushing yards per game, while […]
full_text: Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are getting deep into the college football season as we continue our look at possible draft targets for the Dallas Cowboys in 2027. Florida vs. Georgia Florida and Georgia meet in Atlanta with the Gators’ ground game facing one of its most revealing tests. Georgia has allowed only 91 rushing yards per game, while Florida has built much of its offense around Jadan Baugh. That puts Baugh and Bulldogs linebacker Chris Cole at the center of the matchup. Florida: Jadan Baugh, running back Baugh has carried the Florida offense through seven games, rushing 135 times for 763 yards and 13 touchdowns. He has the frame of a volume runner, but his game contains more than straightforward power. He can make the first defender miss and accelerate through the opening before the pursuit closes. Florida can use him in gap concepts or zone runs without changing the identity of the offense. His contact balance is the trait that consistently stands out. Baugh absorbs glancing hits and keeps his feet through congestion. He’s generated some impressive yards after contact and missed tackles this season, illustrating how often he creates additional yardage without perfect blocking. His lower-body strength makes him dependable in short-yardage situations, but he also has enough lateral quickness to cut away from penetration and enough speed to punish a defense once he reaches the second level. Why The Cowboys Care We all know what Javonte Williams is but the depth chart behind him does not offer the same certainty going into next year. Baugh could enter as a physical second option, handle pass protection and receiving responsibilities, and eventually develop into the primary back. His ability to create after contact would also help an offense that cannot assume every rushing lane will be clean. Dallas should not chase Baugh if he rises into the opening round, but he becomes a serious consideration if he remains available in the Cowboys’ Day 2 range. Georgia: Chris Cole, linebacker Cole is one of the defenders most directly responsible for limiting Baugh so we get a game here where we can directly watch both players on our list face off against each other and battle it out. Cole has recorded 40 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, and three pass breakups this season after producing 59 tackles, seven tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks in 2025. Georgia uses his length and movement skills in several ways, allowing him to run with a tight end, close on a back in the flat, blitz through an interior gap or rush from the edge. His coverage ability separates him from many linebackers in this class, and with the way the linebacker position is evolving this makes him an exciting player. Cole reads releases quickly, has the range to carry routes into space and uses his length. He earned an 88.9 PFF coverage grade last season and showed the broader value of his game against Alabama, finishing with eight tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, a sack and two pass breakups. That combination suggests a three-down role rather than a player who must leave the field in passing situations. Why The Cowboys Care Jaishawn Barham has emerged as an intriguing piece of the Dallas defense, but the long-term linebacker picture stays questionable. DeMarvion Overshown’s availability has been difficult to project, and the defense still needs players who can handle coverage assignments without sacrificing pressure ability. Cole could play the weak side, match running backs and tight ends, and become another movable piece for Christian Parker. His versatility would be especially useful beside Barham. Dallas could let Barham attack downhill while Cole ranges in space. Arizona vs. Texas Tech Arizona brings a five-game winning streak and one of the country’s most efficient passing attacks to Lubbock. Texas Tech counters with a disruptive defensive front led by A.J. Holmes Jr. The Wildcats’ protection will be central to the result, giving veteran right tackle Tristan Bounds a valuable opportunity against a front that creates pressure from multiple alignments and through coordinated movement. Arizona: Tristan Bounds, offensive tackle Bounds is difficult to miss at 6-foot-8 and 320 pounds. The sixth-year senior began his career at Michigan and started eight games at right tackle for Arizona in 2025 before a season-ending injury. He returned this year and has allowed eight pressures but no sacks across 462 snaps, earning a 78.2 pass-blocking grade from PFF. His length gives him an enormous margin in pass protection. Bounds can engage an edge rusher before the defender reaches his chest and widen the path to the quarterback. He is patient enough to avoid opening the inside lane too early, and when his base is set he has the mass to absorb power. Those traits make him particularly effective when Arizona asks him to protect a defined pocket and give its passing game time to work downfield. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs a clearer long-term answer at swing tackle and more competition on the right side. Bounds has the length and pass-protection foundation to compete for a reserve role while the Cowboys coaches work on his pad level, footwork and play strength. His current projection is closer to Day 3 than the top of the draft. That makes this game especially important. If Bounds handles an active Texas Tech front, he can begin to establish himself as a draftable developmental tackle rather than simply an experienced college starter. Texas Tech: A.J. Holmes Jr., defensive tackle Holmes has been one of the most productive interior defenders in college football this seasons. He’s generated 32 pressures and seven sacks this season, leading all FBS defensive tackles in pressures while ranking near the top of the position in pass-rush grade. That production follows an All-America 2025 season in which he recorded 38 tackles, nine tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks. He wins with quickness, leverage and active hands. Holmes fires into gaps before guards can establish their base and uses lateral movement to attack an edge or redirect when the quarterback moves. His first step creates immediate stress for protection schemes, and he works well within stunts because he can penetrate or wrap into the newly opened lane quickly. He is not merely collecting cleanup sacks, his pressure total reflects how frequently he disturbs the pocket. Why The Cowboys Care Sure, Dallas has Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, but succession planning is necessary at a position that’s strong on a defense that’s still building. L.T. Overton offers a young building block, yet the defense still needs another interior lineman who can collapse the pocket and keep the veteran starters from carrying an excessive snap load. Holmes could enter as the second-wave three-technique defender, contribute on passing downs and develop behind Williams and Clark who can mentor him to become the next cornerstone on the inside. His quickness would fit the movement and pressure concepts Parker can build around the front, while his experience should help him earn rotational snaps sooner than a raw developmental tackle.

title: 3 things Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer can carry into week 8
summary: It has been a bumpy ride so far in 2026 for Brian Schottenheimer. The inconsistency and lack of plan has been on display way too much this year, but there were some things that Schottenheimer should be able to carry into week eight that could help the Cowboys win back-to-back games for the first time […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It has been a bumpy ride so far in 2026 for Brian Schottenheimer. The inconsistency and lack of plan has been on display way too much this year, but there were some things that Schottenheimer should be able to carry into week eight that could help the Cowboys win back-to-back games for the first time in 2026. 1) Commitment to the run For the first time this season, the Cowboys showed a commitment to the running game in their 38-21 win against the Eagles. Despite that being a big talking point so far this season, the Cowboys running game hasn’t been good enough to fully commit too, especially when they have been trailing as much as they have. But all things seemed to click on the ground for the Cowboys against the Eagles, and they should be able to carry those things into their matchup against the Cardinals. Against the Eagles, we saw a lot more creativity with the running game, using pin/pulls, traps, and misdirection to create explosive runs rather consistently. The Cardinals defense has been pretty successful so far this season defending the run, ranking sixth in rush EPA/play and 20th in rush success rate. Despite the Cardinals run rankings so far this year, the Cowboys should be able to have a solid night again on the ground if they commit to it and use similar creativity that they did in Week 7 against the Eagles. 2) Continue to push the ball down the field One of the major changes in the offense we saw last week was their aggressiveness to push the ball down the field in the passing game. After six weeks of seeing Dak Prescott’s ADOT rank near the bottom of the league, the Cowboys generated explosive plays at an extremely high clip against a defense that had not given up many explosive passing plays to start the season. With so many defenses sitting on the stop-routes that have been in heavy rotation to start the year, the Cowboys were able to hit multiple big plays using sluggos on the outside, which should be there for them yet again against a Cardinals secondary that has struggled to slow down opposing passing games in 2026 (31st in dropback epa/play and 20th in dropback success rate). 3) More Brevyn Spann-Ford After signing an early contract extension this offseason, their has been a lot of talk about the Cowboys showcasing Spann-Ford more and having him cut into Jake Ferguson’s snaps. Over the last two weeks, that has started to happen. Spann-Ford will likely never be a dynamic receiver, but he offers enough there to lead the team in snaps played at tight end given his blocking ability and ability to pickup yards after the catch with his physical style of play. Spann-Ford opens a lot of things up for the Cowboys running game that wouldn’t be there with Ferguson in the lineup in 11-personnel. The different looks both with the pass and the run they can give defenses when in 12-personnel makes him a very valuable piece to this Cowboys offense moving forward.

title: Cowboys news: Dallas seems to want Joey Porter Jr. beyond this season
summary: Joey Porter Jr. is performing exactly how the Dallas Cowboys wanted him to on his first several games, and it’s making the reality of him remaining with the team past 2026 more possible. This Sunday, the Cowboys will play the Arizona Cardinals, a team they haven’t beaten since 2017. Quinnen Williams will look to continue […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Joey Porter Jr. is performing exactly how the Dallas Cowboys wanted him to on his first several games, and it’s making the reality of him remaining with the team past 2026 more possible. This Sunday, the Cowboys will play the Arizona Cardinals, a team they haven’t beaten since 2017. Quinnen Williams will look to continue his recent ascension in his play. Also, it doesn’t appear that Dallas will add any players of significance via a trade. Joey Porter Jr. has lived up to Cowboys’ expectations, so is he in their long-term plans? – Jon Machota, The Athletic Ever since Joey Porter Jr. step on the field for the Cowboys, he’s shown why they traded for him. The organization appears to want him for the long haul as a result. Although the Cowboys still have arguably the NFL’s worst defense, Porter has been one of the few bright spots. It’s not difficult to see why they would want to sign him to a long-term deal after the season. If the two sides are unable to reach a long-term agreement, the Cowboys could choose to use the franchise tag on him. That could lead to an even tougher decision to make with receiver George Pickens, who is playing this season under the tag. Either way, it doesn’t sound as if they want Porter to be a one-season rental. Caleb Downs explains what it will take to break Cardinals curse – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys haven’t beaten the Cardinals since 2017. Rookie safety Caleb Downs gets candid about how they can change that. To get the victory and break the ongoing curse that’s allowed Arizona to haunt Dallas for years, Downs and his defensive compatriots will have to focus on shutting down all-world tight end Trey McBride and rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, the latter returning from injury to take on the Cowboys and, in the process, to put their run defense to the test. “I think they do a good job with their motions. and they run the ball well.” said Downs. “They have a lot of different personnel groupings, like the Rams did a couple years ago. I think, all of that combined, they have a good offense, and we’re gonna have to do our jobs.” George Pickens questionable vs. Cardinals who are down multiple 1st-round picks – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Multiple ailments have put the status of George Pickens in question against the Cardinals. Also, multiple players on the Cowboys will miss Sunday’s game. The Cowboys will be without wide receiver and kick returner KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters for the second consecutive week after both suffered injuries in the loss to the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 18. Turpin was hurt on the opening kickoff after taking a hit to his ribcage. While he has participated in warm-ups and stretching this week at practice, he has been listed as a non-participant. Winters is dealing with an Achilles strain that has yet to see him hit the practice field in any capacity in the last two weeks. Download the SB Nation app today! Quinnen Williams still not himself one year into Dallas Cowboys tenure but getting there – Clarence Hill, DLLS Dallas needed Quinnen Williams to pick up his play, and he’s done just that over the last several weeks. However, he’s still working to get back to the peak of his powers. Williams has also tallied a sack in three of his last four games Just like the Cowboys defense, Williams is improving. But he says he’s not there yet. He’s still not quite himself yet roughly one year after coning to the Cowboys in a mid-season trade with the New York Jets. “Oh, not yet,” Williams said. “Not yet. At all. I feel like I got some things I need to fix. And just keep going in the right direction. And hopefully soon I have that game that I feel like I’m myself soon.” Cowboys’ Jerry Jones downplays trade rumors: ‘Would have to be a dynamic situation’ – Todd Brock, Cowboys Wire Jerry Jones has spoken several times about the Cowboys being active before the trade deadline. That tune has changed a bit. “I don’t feel like I have to ‘keep up’ with anybody,” Cowboys owner Jerry Jones told K&C Masterpiece on 105.3 The Fan during a phone-in on Friday. “Where we are right now, it would have to be a dynamic situation for us to give up picks because we’ve used some of those picks in our future. On the other hand, I don’t like the idea of giving up, really, anybody that somebody else might want. We need him as bad as they do.”

title: Cowboys vs Cardinals: 3 causes for concern in Week 8
summary: After a win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, the Dallas Cowboys return home to host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Dallas needs a win to move back to .500 on the season and gain on the New York Giants in the NFC East race. Before the Cowboys and Cardinals square off, here are […]
full_text: Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images After a win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, the Dallas Cowboys return home to host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Dallas needs a win to move back to .500 on the season and gain on the New York Giants in the NFC East race. Before the Cowboys and Cardinals square off, here are three causes for concern in this matchup. 1) Schottenheimer’s Cowboys consistency issues In the Brian Schottenheimer era, consistency has been one of the Cowboys’ biggest pain points. In the 24 games that Schottenheimer has been Dallas’ head coach, the Cowboys have won back-to-back games just once. That lone winning streak came back in November of last year when they won three in a row against the Raiders, Eagles, and Chiefs. While Dallas is facing an inferior opponent this week in the Arizona Cardinals, the Schottenheimer-coached Cowboys teams have not been able to take advantage of these matchups and string together wins. Week 5 of last season is a perfect example. Dallas won big against the New York Jets and headed into a very winnable game against the Carolina Panthers in Week 6. The Cowboys entered the game as three-point favorites over the 2-3 Carolina team but ended up losing the contest 30-27. This week the Cowboys are in a very similar spot. They absolutely should beat the Cardinals and give Schottenheimer his second winning streak of his NFL coaching career, but given what we’ve seen from this team in the past two years, it’s hard to trust them to do so. 2) Arizona’s capable passing attack It may sound crazy to say that a Jacoby Brissett-led Cardinals offense should worry Dallas, but with how bad the Cowboys’ defense has been this season, particularly in the pass game, it’s a valid concern. While the Cardinals’ offense hasn’t been near the top of the league, they have moved the ball effectively through the air in multiple games this season. Brissett, who leads the league with 282 pass attempts, has thrown two or more touchdown passes in three games this season. One of those matchups was against the Detroit Lions, a defense similar to the Cowboys’ unit talent-wise. The veteran completed 29 of 47 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns while recording a 91.8 Passer Rating. The Lions ended up winning the game by a wide margin, but that was in large part due to their offense taking control early, something Dallas has struggled to do this season. Brissett may not be seen as much of a threat, but if you don’t get pressure on him, he’s capable of sitting in the pocket and making some solid throws. An inability to rush the passer has been the Achilles heel for Dallas’ defense in the past few weeks. If that trend continues on Sunday, look for Arizona’s passing attack to make plays all game long. 3) The Cardinals problem It’s fairly hard to believe, but the Arizona Cardinals may be Dallas’ toughest matchup over the course of the last decade plus. Since 2008, the Cowboys are a shocking 1-8 in their last nine matchups against the Cardinals, with four of those losses coming at home. Since that 2008 campaign in which they started their winning ways against Dallas, the Cardinals have a 134-164-2 regular season record as a team. Arizona has rarely been one of the better teams in the league, but they always seem to find a way to beat the Cowboys, regardless of how their season is going. Year-to-year team trends don’t mean much in the NFL, but it’s hard not to be concerned about Dallas’ struggles against the Cardinals. This game feels eerily similar to the Week 9 matchup between the two teams last season. Arizona won that game 27-17 as the Cowboys looked unprepared and undisciplined. The Cowboys have a big-time Cardinals problem that they’ll look to put to rest on Sunday.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: What the numbers say about a winner in Cowboys vs Cardinals
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 3-4 Dallas Cowboys host the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott […]
full_text: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 3-4 Dallas Cowboys host the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards on a season low 27 pass attempts. Javonte Williams was the focus, rushing for 155 yards on 25 carries. Dallas finished the game with a season high 204 yards on 38 rushing attempts. The receivers didn’t see much in the way of volume, but were productive when targeted. CeeDee Lamb snagged a pair of touchdowns and George Pickens finished with another. Brevyn Spann-Ford was the only tight end with a catch on the day, finishing with two catches on two targets. Jake Ferguson was targeted just once and drew a pass interference call. Cardinals key stats from last week The Cardinals finished last week with 94 rushing yards and 272 pass yards against the Broncos. Arizona was an abysmal 1-for-5 in the red zone. They also converted just 5-of-17 third down attempts. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett was sacked three times. The Cardinals most dangerous weapon, Trey McBride, finished the game with ten receptions for 111 yards and a touchdown. This was his season high in both catches and receiving yards Keep the Javon-train rolling Javonte Williams is coming off one of the best games of his career last week against the Eagles. The Cowboys running back was the primary focus on offense, rushing for 6.2 yards per carry on 25 attempts. Coach Brian Schottenheimer made a conscious decision to stick with the run after completely abandoning it the week prior. The decision paid immediate dividends, resulting in a huge victory in a must-win game against Philadelphia. This week, the Cowboys should plan to do the same. The Cardinals have struggled in run defense, ranking 28th in rush success percentage allowed (SumerSports). On the flip side, they rank eighth in pass success percentage allowed. This Cardinals defense has a weakness that Dallas can exploit. The strategy for the Cowboys offense should be crystal clear: let the running back room once again feast behind an offensive line that just dominated one of the better defensive interiors in the NFL. If they can do that, it’ll only make things easier for Dak Prescott and the receivers as a result. What do the numbers mean? The Cowboys find themselves clawing back into the NFC East race. They realistically cannot afford another loss until they play the 49ers on November 15th. So how do the numbers stack up this week? Dallas is the favorite in this one at home against a struggling Cardinals team. Arizona is certainly not devoid of talent – they’re a team that finds themselves out of sync and unable to play complementary football far too often. They feature one of the league’s best tight ends and several players on defense that would be starters across the league on any team. You’d never know about the talent on the field judging them by their point differential this season, however. The Cardinals currently rank dead last in the NFL with a -66 point differential through seven weeks. What makes that even more amazing is that they only allowed 14 and 16 points in week one and week six, respectively. Both of those games resulted in wins. But when this team loses, they lose big. The Cardinals only have one single-score loss this year, with the rest being blowouts. If Dallas can force a stop or two early in the game (as opposed to waiting until the third drive or after halftime), the offense has a legitimate opportunity to put the game away early. That’s a big ask, considering what we’ve seen from Christian Parker’s unit this year. But outside of Trey McBride, the Cardinals are lacking legitimate threats across the offense. Arizona has two capable backs, Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier. Both running backs are averaging less than four yards per carry on the season and Love may not even be available this week due to injury. If he is, he’s certainly the more dynamic playmaker of the two. With that said, the Cardinals simply lack the firepower to generate explosive plays and they struggle to put the ball into the end zone on a consistent basis. This should be a week where the Dallas defense once again allows 24 points or less, just as they’ve done the last three weeks. The spread from FanDuel has Dallas as the seven-point favorite for good reason. They should be able to beat the Cardinals in every phase of the game. But as we know, these games against Arizona can get funky out of nowhere. While I’m more skeptical about a Cowboys victory this week, as opposed to last week against their divisional rival, the numbers still indicate that Dallas will be the clear favorite to walk away with the win.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals: Matchups to watch in Week 8
summary: The Dallas Cowboys got a much needed victory over the Philadelphia Eagles last week and will be looking to extend their win streak in the Week 8 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. This is a team that beat them 27-17 last year in a surprising upset, and would probably love nothing more than to do […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys got a much needed victory over the Philadelphia Eagles last week and will be looking to extend their win streak in the Week 8 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. This is a team that beat them 27-17 last year in a surprising upset, and would probably love nothing more than to do so once again. To avoid another upset, Dallas needs to take advantage of certain matchups to sway the game in their favor, which we discuss below. RB Javonte Williams vs. Cardinals’ run defense Javonte Williams is coming off his best game of the season, and one of the best of his entire professional career, after rushing for 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries last week against the Eagles. His physicality and ability to pick up chunk yards helped balance out the Cowboys offense, which led to one of their most productive games of the season. The game plan should look much the same this week against the Cardinals who currently ranked 23 rd in the league and run defense, allowing 126.3 rushing yards per game. If the Cowboys offensive line continues to open holes like they did last week, Williams should have his second 100+ rushing yard game of the season and help sway the game in Dallas’ favor. Cowboys’ secondary vs. Cardinals’ TE Trey McBride Trey McBride is the Cardinals best, and most consistent, offensive weapon. He is coming off his best game of the year against the Broncos when he caught 10 passes for 111 yards and a touchdown, and will be looking to repeat that type of success against the Cowboys struggling secondary. Last year Dallas was able to hold him to just five catches for 55 yards and a TD and will attempt to do the same in this Week 8 matchup. McBride’s production and the outcome of the game could depend on who Christian Parker assigns to contain Arizona’s All-Pro TE. Will it be the young rookie Caleb Downs, or someone else? Whoever it is will have their hands full against one of the league’s best TEs. RT Terence Steele vs. Cardinals’ OLB Josh Sweat Opponents this week, teammates the next? Rumors continue to swirl the Cowboys could be planning on acquiring Josh Sweat via trade before the November 10 deadline. He only has two QB sacks on the year through the first seven weeks of the season, and there some concerns about his desire for a new contract, but that hasn’t stopped rumors will be playing for another team soon. A lot of eyes will be on him this week and how he performs against Terence Steele. He could sway the game in the Cardinals favor with a big game and also increase his odds of him getting dealt and potentially landing the new contract he’s seeking.
author: Brian Martin

title: Dallas Cowboys offensive line needs another performance like last week
summary: The Dallas Cowboys offensive line was the best unit on the field last week against the Philadelphia Eagles. Can they repeat the performance against the Arizona Cardinals? Let’s take a look. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far.  Pass Block Win Rate – 54% (9th) Run Block […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys offensive line was the best unit on the field last week against the Philadelphia Eagles. Can they repeat the performance against the Arizona Cardinals? Let’s take a look. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 54% (9th) Run Block Win Rate – 71% (28th) Pressure rate allowed – 31% (17th) Sacks allowed – 7 (1st) Last three-week trend: Improving nicely The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Do not lose track of Budda Baker The most dangerous Arizona pass rusher so far is not actually one of its defensive linemen, it’s safety Budda Baker. He leads Arizona with 3.5 sacks, ahead of Josh Sweat and Darius Robinson, who each have two. That immediately tells Dallas something about how Arizona is creating pressure. Baker has been used selectively as a blitzer. Arizona has found ways to disguise his approach and send him through gaps where offensive linemen are already occupied. One of those plays produced an A-gap sack against Jared Goff. If Baker begins close to the line, Dallas has to decide whether he is actually coming after Prescott or simply pretending to blitz before dropping into coverage. That uncertainty is the real danger. PRESSURE POINT: Josh Sweat versus Terence Steele Arizona still has one edge defender Dallas cannot ignore. Josh Sweat has only two sacks this season, and his overall production has dropped considerably from 2025. His sacks per 100 pass-rush snaps had fallen from 3.5 last year to 1.6 this year, but he remains Arizona’s most established edge rusher. The Cardinals themselves described Sweat as their best pass rusher earlier this month, and their depth chart places him at left defensive end, that naturally creates snaps against Terence Steele. Tyler Guyton has still not surrendered a sack this season despite allowing 19 pressures, and his 84.6 PFF run-blocking grade ranks fourth among qualifying tackles this year, but Steele has been the less dependable pass protector. Arizona should therefore move Sweat toward him and see whether it can create a weakness that Philadelphia failed to find. Dallas does not need to completely remove Sweat from the game, it just cannot allow him to turn a quiet season around on Sunday. Where to attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Cardinals soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Keep feeding Javonte Williams There is no reason to complicate this after Dallas finally found its running game against Philadelphia. Now Brian Schottenheimer needs to keep using it. Arizona has surrendered 884 rushing yards through seven games at 4.6 yards per carry, that’s 126 yards per game which ranks 10th-worst. It becomes even more interesting because Arizona could again be missing defensive tackle Walter Nolen III. He missed the Denver game with an ankle injury, and head coach Mike LaFleur said that he was not expecting Nolen to practice much this week, so keep watch on his status as that removes a powerful body from the middle. That means Dallas should go straight back to Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe and Tyler Booker where Williams had huge lanes against Philadelphia. There is no reason to move away from that approach this week. Arizona defensive lineman Darius Robinson has also struggled against the run. He has a PFF grading of 42.8 against the run, 106th among qualifying interior defensive linemen. That creates another target for Smith and Booker. Double-team Robinson initially, then allow one blocker to move onto a linebacker. GREEN LIGHT: Make Arizona’s four-man rush beat you This might be Dallas’ biggest statistical advantage. Arizona’s defense has generated pressure on only 25.5% of opposing dropbacks, which ranks 26th in the NFL and sits below the league average. The Cardinals have 15 sacks, 19th in the league, so they have managed to finish some of their pressure opportunities. But they are not consistently forcing quarterbacks to move. Dallas should force Arizona to prove it can win without blitzing. If the Cardinals rush four, send everyone else into a route. Do not automatically keep Jake Ferguson beside the offensive tackle. Give Prescott five receiving options and make Arizona’s defensive line beat Dallas one-on-one, especially after seeing that Philadelphia could not do it Monday and the Eagles finished without even registering a quarterback hit. Arizona’s pressure numbers suggest Dallas should trust the offensive line again. The Chaos Report Here’s the Arizona Cardinals defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 15 (19th) Pass Rush Win Rate – 52% (14th) Run Stop Win Rate – 27% (25th) QB Pressure Rate – 25% (26th) Last three-week trend: Light pressure, run defense leaking Matchup of the week Terence Steele vs. Josh Sweat This is the individual matchup Arizona needs to win. The former Eagle has not produced at his normal level this season as Sweat has only two sacks, while Arizona’s overall pressure rate is among the lowest in the league, but Dallas knows all to well what he can do. Sweat has the speed to attack Steele’s outside shoulder and enough length to prevent the tackle from easily getting his hands into position. Steele does not have to dominate Sweat, he simply cannot allow quick losses and he needs to give Prescott time to attack. Once those wins start happening and Steele handles his assignment enough times, the Cardinals coaches will need to adjust which in turn helps Steele even more. Best Route to Success The answer here is simple, do exactly what worked in Philadelphia. Run behind Smith and Booker, and let Guyton use his run-blocking ability that currently has him ranked highly on PFF, then make Arizona react. If the Cardinals bring Baker down toward the line to stop the run, use play-action behind him. If they blitz, throw quickly. Injury Updates: Dallas currently has no new injury concerns among its five starting offensive linemen. The main Cardinals injury to monitor along the defensive line is Walter Nolen III. Darius Robinson also dealt with a back injury last week but was able to play against Denver. There is some talk of Josh Sweat hitting the trade market before the deadline, but for now expect him to play against Dallas this week.
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys have chance they can’t let fly away against Cardinals
summary: Halloween weekend is fast approaching, and for a Dallas Cowboys team desperate to stack wins for the first time this season, there may be no spookier, scarier sight than the Arizona Cardinals coming to town. Yeah, seriously. Even within a bad NFC East division, the Cowboys have created a small margin of error to lose […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Halloween weekend is fast approaching, and for a Dallas Cowboys team desperate to stack wins for the first time this season, there may be no spookier, scarier sight than the Arizona Cardinals coming to town. Yeah, seriously. Even within a bad NFC East division, the Cowboys have created a small margin of error to lose games they’re supposed to win, having already dropped such games to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Giants. The Cowboys suffered their fifth loss of the 2025 season to the Cardinals in week nine at home last year, and now are looking to avoid the same amount of losses through week seven against the same opponent – one they haven’t beaten since 2017, even with three of the four meetings since that win in Arizona coming in Arlington. If not for that 28-17 Cowboys win in 2017, the Cardinals would actually have an active nine-game winning streak against the Cowboys coming into this weekend, with the last win before that one coming in 2006. The 2-5 Cardinals opened their season with what felt like an upset win at the time at the Chargers, who remain winless. In week six, they went back to SoFi Stadium and scored a legitimate upset against a division rival, beating the Rams 18-16. This snapped a four-game losing streak to the Seahawks, 49ers, Giants, and Lions, but Mike LaFleur’s team also could not stack wins as they lost last Sunday at home to the Broncos. Let’s get to our weekly look at what the Cowboys must do to finally get the monkey cardinal off their back and beat these pesky red birds, or what could throw the season back off the rails with another bad home loss. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Arizona Cardinals if… …they set the edge on defense. There was one thing the Cowboys still struggled to do for the majority of the Philadelphia Eagles game. While the offense got points early and kept the pressure on most of the night, and the defense avoided the backbreaking plays and penalties until that offense handed them a sizeable lead, and the kicking game swung the field position battle in Dallas’ favor, still, the defense had a hard time setting the edge. If ever the stage was set for a game to help prove the Cowboys are different this year, Sunday afternoon is the ultimate “do-over” game, because the defense couldn’t set an edge at all against Jacoby Brissett and these Cardinals under Matt Eberflus in 2025. A strong run game on the edge, missed tackles, and the dual-threat ability of Brissett also gave the Cowboys defense no chance to hold up in coverage, as Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride caught touchdowns – the latter making the score 24-7 in the third quarter. Christian Parker’s Cowboys defense showed new looks in the middle of the field against the Eagles with Shemar James and Demarvion Overshown at linebacker. The personnel elsewhere in the secondary is also better than when these teams met last season when Markquese Bell, Juanyeh Thomas, and Kaiir Elam all started. Now, the Cowboys have Joey Porter Jr., Malik Hooker, and Caleb Downs patrolling in the backend. Schematically, Dallas has the answers to taking away the middle of the field where McBride has been the catalyst for Arizona’s pass game. The tight end leads the Cardinals in targets in their last three games, was one away from doing so in the Giants loss, and still has double digit targets in every other game he wasn’t the team leader. The Cowboys clogging up the middle of the field passing lanes can’t come at the cost of either edge contain against the run or pass rush. Brissett is a hard quarterback to bring to the ground, so much so that it feels like it’ll take timely blitzes to finish sacks in this game as opposed to counting on an edge rusher group that’s been poor at finishing for the Cowboys. Any blitz opportunities stem from stopping the run, and the Cardinals had 116 rushing yards in their week one win and 120 to beat the Rams. They’ve only had one other game over 100 yards this season, again at the Giants. First-round pick Jeremiyah Love has a strong chance at rejoining Arizona’s offense out of the backfield for this game, and is also a load to tackle on inside runs while having home run ability outside the tackle. Zonovan “Bam” Knight led the Cardinals in rushing yards over their last two games with Love out, while veteran Tyler Allgeier has been listed as the starter. Which QBs are getting help from their supporting cast? Factors: — Pressure (%) — Drop (%) — Average Target Separation — YAC/Reception pic.twitter.com/AcGJMiryDx — Daniel Rotman (@daniel_rotman15) October 26, 2026 The Cowboys will be playing a more dangerous game against Brissett and this stable of running backs than they did against Tanner McKee, a hobbled Saquon Barkley, and Dameon Pierce last week. If they don’t maximize what Dak Prescott and the offense does in this game by getting stops, the losing streak against the Cardinals will be at risk of continuing. A third straight game with a defensive takeaway would be like a full size Twix bar in the Halloween basket. It all starts with setting a hard edge. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Arizona Cardinals if… …they aren’t a serious football team. In the spirit of trick-or-treating this weekend, this game needs to be a treat for the Cowboys at home if they want to avoid fans saying they fell for yet another trick of high expectations. In one of the two Cardinals’ wins, they didn’t score a touchdown, just six field goals. Of their five losses, only one is close, 36-30 to the 49ers. They gave up 45 points to the Lions and 31 to the Seahawks. The one deceiving score in their schedule was the 36-24 loss at the Giants, where the Cardinals had a chance to win it late but threw a pick six, but the Cowboys also have their own claim to having a chance to beat the Giants in New Jersey. The best teams in this league string together wins, something the Brian Schottenheimer Cowboys have had a ghoulishly hard time doing. If they miss out on this opportunity to do so at home against the Cardinals, they would need to beat the Colts in week nine and 49ers in week 10 to get back-to-back wins on November 8th and 15th. It was November 23rd when the Cowboys won a second straight game last season. This pattern is not sustainable, and the time is now for the Cowboys to put the losing streak to the Cardinals behind them and think about stacking wins. After a gauntlet of defensive-minded head coaches in the first five weeks of the season, where the Cowboys went 2-3, they didn’t come out with intensity at the Packers and lost to the offensive-minded Matt LaFleur. They bounced back by beating Nick Sirianni’s Eagles last Monday, and now get another offense-first head coach in his first season, Mike LaFleur. There really are no excuses and nowhere to hide for the Cowboys this weekend, if they want the win in Philly to be remembered for something and to be taken seriously going into November.
author: Sean Martin

title: Colts are now open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor, and the Broncos are among the teams interested
summary: According to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Indianapolis Colts are now open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the upcoming trade deadline. In the report, both insiders list the Broncos among the teams that have shown some level of interest in trading for the star running back. The Colts […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on prior to the start of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, the Indianapolis Colts are now open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the upcoming trade deadline. In the report, both insiders list the Broncos among the teams that have shown some level of interest in trading for the star running back. The Colts have already traded Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers, and they do not appear done having a fire sale. The #Colts are now open to trading star RB Jonathan Taylor… and those talks are ongoing and active. Story from me and @AdamSchefter : https://t.co/9CovxSRESa https://t.co/9CovxSRESa — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 31, 2026 Schefter and Rapoport name the Packers, Vikings, Giants, and Seahawks, along with the Broncos , as teams that have shown at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor. The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks, sources said. As of now, the Vikings seem like the reported frontrunner for Taylor, but as we know, things can change, and circumstances can change a team’s level of desperation to acquire a player. For the Broncos, their run game has struggled to start the season. Veteran JK Dobbins, whom the Broncos re-signed this offseason and hoped would look like the back they saw last season, has struggled to start the year. He has recently unfollowed the Broncos on social media (if you care about that) and has gotten into a back-and-forth with 9NEWS Broncos insider Mike Klis. Also, second-year running back RJ Harvey suffered a knee injury during practice this week, which isn’t considered serious per reports , but he will sit out Sunday’s big game vs. the Chiefs. Last week, the rookie running back was activated off the injured reserve and instantly took over the Broncos backfield. He led the Broncos’ backs in snaps, touches, and yards and now will get the start vs. the Chiefs on Sunday. If Coleman were to have a big game against the Broncos’ divisional rivals, it would pour some cold water on these trade talks, but any struggles or injuries could intensify these talks. Right now, the return for Taylor appears to be a 2nd-round pick + more, according to reports. This report also seems to indicate that the Colts, who have been listening to offers for Taylor, have not been satisfied with the offers and are telling teams they need to send in their best offers now. Personally, if acquiring Taylor only costs a 2nd-round pick + more, I believe the Broncos should make that deal. A 1-2 punch of Taylor and Coleman instantly gives the Broncos one of the better running back pairings in the NFL and would instantly reshape their offense. This would take a lot of pressure off quarterback Bo Nix, make teams have to defend the run game, and open up the pass game and play-action game for Nix. Plus, if you want to win in the postseason, you need to run the ball. I believe giving up the draft capital, especially if it does not cost a first-round pick, is worth it for a team that is in a Super Bowl window right now. Even if they do not acquire Taylor, I still believe they need to upgrade their running back room. Coleman is a mostly inexperienced and unproven rookie at this point, Dobbins is struggling, and Harvey has continued to struggle as a runner (excellent as a pass catcher, though). We have already seen multiple big blockbuster trades go down, and we still have a few weeks to go until the trade deadline. I would be shocked if the Broncos do not make a move during this period, but we will have to wait and see. Stay tuned to Mile High Report for all your news and updates surrounding the Denver Broncos.
