title: Which receiver trades could the Chiefs consider before the deadline?
summary: It’s deadline season, which means we’re back to wide receiver talk. There will come a time when that’s no longer the case for the Kansas City Chiefs. Today is not that day. Tyquan Thornton is (more or less) out for the year. Rashee Rice is expected back this week from his hamstring injury. Cyrus Allen […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s deadline season, which means we’re back to wide receiver talk. There will come a time when that’s no longer the case for the Kansas City Chiefs . Today is not that day. Tyquan Thornton is (more or less) out for the year. Rashee Rice is expected back this week from his hamstring injury. Cyrus Allen is playing sparingly. Xavier Worthy has once again been up and down in his performance. The Chiefs’ top wide receiver finished last week with 18 receiving yards. It’s a problem. It needs a solution. The next two weeks should help clarify the direction. I understand why fans are requesting (demanding?) a significant trade. It would be nice to see the team kill this fly with a sledgehammer, metaphorically speaking. I would love nothing more than to watch Patrick Mahomes throw the football to Garrett Wilson, Nico Collins or Devonta Smith. I suppose I could be wrong, but I think the odds of any of those trades coming together are roughly equal to the odds of me suiting up at wide receiver for the Chiefs by the end of the year. In other words, it probably won’t happen. The far more likely scenario is the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver a tier (or three) lower in the pecking order. The names won’t jump off the page. But they might be exactly what the doctor ordered to improve the passing game for the rest of the year. The next couple of weeks could be significant in that regard. Rice was finally beginning to look like his former self when he got hurt. Can he recapture that form when he returns? That would be an encouraging sign. He brings an important element to the offense, especially as a zone beater across the middle. I would like to see the Chiefs give Allen a longer look this week, as well. Maybe that’s asking too much, but he has three receptions on four targets for 45 yards in 25 total offensive snaps over the past two weeks. He’s shown he can beat man coverage. It would be nice to see what he can produce in a larger role. Maybe that’s just not in the cards for this season, but if the Chiefs think there’s untapped potential, now is the time to find out. And he’s not replacing world beaters in the lineup. Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong have combined for 4 catches for 40 yards on 154 snaps, with 10 targets over the past two weeks. That’s the extent of the internal options. The truth is the Chiefs are severely lacking an outside wide receiver with size and the ability to separate against man coverage. Those are the skills Thornton brought to the table. An ability to win deep would certainly be a plus. We saw the effect of not having a serious threat on the field last week as the Seahawks completely shut down the Chiefs’ passing attack. So where could the Chiefs realistically turn their attention if a trade becomes necessary? Here are some names to keep top of mind. Colts WR Josh Downs 2026 Stats: 26 receptions, 41 targets, 307 yards (11.8 YPR), 0 TD Contract Status: 1 yr, $3.9M At this point, you’ve heard the name, and you’re probably familiar with his game. He’s small and he’s traditionally been a slot receiver for the Colts (69% slot rate this year, 79% for his career), but he’s quite good at separating against man coverage and he’s been utilized as a downfield threat in Alec Pierce’s absence (6 targets 20+ yards downfield this year). Eagles WR Dontayvion Wicks 2026 Stats: 19 receptions, 31 targets, 284 yards (14.9 YPR), 1 TD Contract Status: Technically? 2 yrs, $10.25M. But it’s the Eagles, so there are void years, and it’s a bit convoluted. But for the Chiefs, it appears it would be 2 yrs, $4.4M. I think this is the player we probably haven’t spent enough time discussing. The Eagles are in freefall, and it’s probably more than a one-year fix. Wicks is an imperfect player, but he fits exactly what the Chiefs are missing. He lines up outside roughly 70 percent of the time this year, and more than 60 percent of the time in his career. He’s been a significant deep threat for the majority of his career (9 deep targets this year, and 32 deep targets over the past three years combined). He does his best work against man coverage, as well . He’s not a big name, and he’s not a high-volume target, but he could capably fill some of what the Chiefs are missing in Thornton’s absence. He should also come at a reasonable price. Texans WR Kayshon Boutte 2026 Stats: 15 receptions, 23 targets, 194 yards (12.9 YPR), 0 TD Contract Status: 1 yr, $3.7M Boutte was already traded earlier this year from the Patriots to the Texans, and he’s seen his snap share drop significantly in recent weeks. I don’t think the Texans are willing to give up on their season just yet, but that time might be coming. Boutte is another deep threat who lines up outside the vast majority of the time (73% this year, 86% for his career). He’s also a deep threat with seven targets more than 20 yards down the field this year. His average depth of target is more than 14 yards downfield. If you want an outside wide receiver with recent playoff success who is likely to be available for a cheap cost, this might be your man. Chargers WR Quentin Johnston 2026 Stats: 8 receptions, 21 targets, 165 yards (20.6 YPR), 0 TD Contract Status: 2 yrs, $20.5M ($1.3M prorated ‘26, $18M fully guaranteed ‘27) Hear me out. I don’t think it’s overly likely, and the money is a problem. But I’m not sure Johnston is as much of a lost cause as it might seem on the surface. He had 16 total touchdowns over the past two years, and he’s shown an ability to stretch the field. That’s a huge element to bring to the table. He also lines up outside the vast majority of the time (83% outside rate this year, 87% for his career). He’s been in a disastrous situation this year with the Chargers. Maybe the Chiefs believe he could be a transition piece in the offense for the next 1.5 years? I’m open to it. He’s probably the most talented player on this list, even if he’s also arguably the most frustrating and inconsistent. Commanders WR Treylon Burks 2026 Stats: 9 receptions, 152 yards (16.9 YPR), 2 TD Contract Status: 1 yr, $1.2M Once upon a time, I was convinced the Chiefs would draft Treylon Burks. That obviously didn’t happen, but he’s developed into a decent deep target for the Commanders this year. He’s lining up almost exclusively outside (69% outside rate this year, 74% for his career), and he could be had for a relatively low price. It’s not sexy. But it could work. Colts WR Laquon Treadwell 2026 Stats: 15 receptions, 26 targets, 197 yards (13.1 YPR), 0 TD Contract Status: 1 yr, $1.3M Another former first-round bust. Maybe I’m only mentioning him because I thought he played pretty well against the Chiefs, but he’s an outside receiver with the ability to take the top off the defense occasionally. It’s not my first (or second, or third…) choice, but if stuff hits the fan, fine. Commanders WR Dyami Brown 2026 Stats: 9 receptions, 16 targets, 94 yards (10.5 YPR), 0 TD Contract Status: 1 yr, $1.2M I feel like I’ve been waiting for a Dyami Brown breakout for the past five years. It’s never really happened. I don’t think it’s coming. But he’s similar to Burks and Treadwell in that he’s an outside receiver with legit downfield chops. That’s all I’ve got. I know, it’s not an inspiring list. But Tyquan Thornton wasn’t a headline addition when he arrived in Kansas City, either. I think this is a far more realistic list of trade deadline targets for the Chiefs than some of what’s been speculated about in internet circles. I would love to see the Chiefs add Downs to the mix, but I personally believe Wicks and Boutte are probably the best fits for what this offense currently lacks.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 27: Los Angeles Rams tight end Mark Redman (83) catches the ball for a gain during the NFL preseason game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on August 27, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are facing off against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 8 at SoFi Stadium fresh off the bye. The Chargers have lost their first six games and are the only winless team left in the league. However, the Chargers can turn things around with a win against the crosstown rival Rams. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , the Chargers are an underdog by 6.5 points. Let’s take a look at some predictions for the game. Over/Under: 45.5 Only one game the Chargers have played this season has had more than 45.5 points. That came against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4. The Chargers’ offense has not been up to par, scoring 17 points or fewer in all but one game this year. The Rams should have a boost from the crowd, which will be unfortunate to deal with while the Chargers are also at their home stadium, but it’s hard to imagine the Los Angeles “bowl” as a barnburner. Prediction: Under Chargers +6.5 Fanduel is giving the Chargers a touchdown to work with, and they are coming off a bye week when they were able to get some much-needed rest. The Rams are coming into this game knowing they need to keep their foot on the gas after their blowout win against the Las Vegas Raiders last week, when they won 35-21. This win will put the Rams at 5-0 if they can get to it. I’m expecting a focused Rams team against the Chargers, which will likely result in a multi-score victory for the Rams. Prediction: Rams -6.5 Final Score It wouldn’t surprise me if the Chargers came out of the gates with a score or two, but given how they have performed throughout the season, it’s hard to imagine that this is the week they break their spell of bad luck. The Chargers are the last winless team in the league, which is definitely a red flag as the calendar turns to November. However, the bye week could give the Chargers a true chance to reset, which would give them an opportunity to re-evaluate things in hopes of coming out on top this week. In last week’s Reacts poll, the confidence meter to determine whether the team is heading in the right direction, was at five percent. This week, that number has grown slightly to eight percent. The bye week did not necessarily do much to put the Chargers higher in the confidence meter, but perhaps the rest gives fans reason to believe things are turning around, even if it’s a slow burn. Fans can watch the game on Fox or stream it on the Fox One app.

title: Chargers-Rams Game Preview: How does Joe Alt’s return improve the Bolts’ offense?
summary: The Bolts are back inside SoFi Stadium this week to face the crosstown Rams. The Rams are also failing to meet expectations this season with a 3-4 record so far this season. Blockbuster addition Myles Garrett has not played since Week One, but that’s far from their only issue. When it’s all firing, Sean McVay […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers offensive tackle Joe Alt (76) stands by during a timeout during an NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA.(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Bolts are back inside SoFi Stadium this week to face the crosstown Rams. The Rams are also failing to meet expectations this season with a 3-4 record so far this season. Blockbuster addition Myles Garrett has not played since Week One, but that’s far from their only issue. When it’s all firing, Sean McVay and the Rams are still one of the best teams in the league, so the Chargers need to come as correct a ever (and unfortunately, the next time they do will be the first). Expectations are likely low, but they don’t say “any given Sunday” for no reason. Here are the three things I’ll be watching for when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) Can the Chargers secondary take advantage of a Rams WR unit missing Davante Adams? The Chargers are dodging longtime and All-Pro wideout Davate Adams this week after he recently landed on IR. The Rams offense is now a bit more palatable, but Puka Nacua is still the real deal as one of the most productive wideouts in the league over the past few seasons. The Chargers cornerback room has held strong with Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart staying healthy this season. Veteran Donte Jackson has been more out of the lineup than in and the same can be said for both Rodney Shelley and Deane Leonard. Cornerback could be a big need this offseason, but that’s a whole other conversation. With the Rams using a ton of motion pre-snap, I expect the Chargers to play a lot of zone to keep Still or Hart from having to travel across the formation. The lack of Derwin James continues to hurt, but overall they’ve been fine enough without him. This will be an interesting test for Chris O’Leary. Aside from the continuous short fields given by the offense, the young coordinator has done an admirable job against some of the league’s top offensive play-callers. Showing he has the stuff to take on McVay could be another early feather in his cap. 2.) Will Joe Alt switch to left tackle in his return from a neck injury? Last season when Rashawn Slater missed the entire season due to a torn patellar tendon, Alt flipped sides from right to left. This year, Alt is about to return to the lineup without Slater once more. I’m curious to see if they believe rookie Travis, who has played the past few games at left tackle, can continue to do so which would allow Alt to remain at his normal spot. Alt has been one of the best tackles in all of football. His return is huge. Knowing how bad the offense has been, I would not be surprised to see Burke go to the right side to allow Alt to protect Justin Herbert’s blindside. That seems like the most important thing to cover as far as getting this front five pinned down. Kayode Awosika was expected to return after the bye, but he remains a non-participant in practice. That leaves rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Not especially ideal given how rough he’s been as a starter, but that’s what happens when there’s three players at his position hurt ahead of him. So for Week Eight, Alt is the only returning player who wasn’t healthy before the bye. And again, his return is a big deal, but is it as big as it sounds? The offense wasn’t good when the majority of the team is healthy. How much will it really change for the offense as a whole? 3.) Will the offense look any different post-bye? This one is as simple as it sounds. The Chargers chose not to make any massive changes at the bye despite sitting at 0-6. Mike McDaniel not only still has his job, but he will remain the offensive playcaller going forward. Even if you did not expect McDaniel to get fired last week, you likely also thought there’d at least be some change on the coaching staff. So here the Chargers are, in the same boat that they rode to the league’s worst offense. Harbaugh has decided that six weeks wasn’t enough to make a decision and with no trades having been made, they whole franchise supposedly believes it’s worth keeping all their assets in order to make an effort towards the unprecedented. No team has ever made the playoffs after starting 0-5. The Chargers are 0-6. I seriously do not know what the plan is. Will 0-7 force a change? 0-8? Where is the line in the sand? If Justin Herbert avoids throwing an interception in a game for the first time all season, will that be all the team needs to believe they’ve fixed it? Does he need to do it for consecutive games? It sure feels like the bar is set way to low for things to keep chugging along like they haven’t already been off the tracks since Week One.

Allowing opponents (mostly lesser) to hang around too long, self-inflicted wounds, and horrendous special teams play has them needing this win to get back to .500 and stay within reach of the six teams that are ahead or tied with them in the wild card race. The injury bug has really embedded under the Rams skin and Week 8 is no different. title: Rams may have new longsnapper for Week 8
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are still trying to figure out their special teams. They will continue to keep trying. It’s a work in progress. Rams’ special teams unit gets more bad news with long snapper doubtful (ramswire) “Cardona did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday. If McQuaide does play, he will be the sixth specialist […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are still trying to figure out their special teams. They will continue to keep trying. It’s a work in progress. Rams’ special teams unit gets more bad news with long snapper doubtful (ramswire) “Cardona did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday. If McQuaide does play, he will be the sixth specialist to take a snap for Los Angeles this season, joining Cardona, Ethan Evans, Harrison Mevis, Blake Grupe, and Brandon McManus. McQuaide was the Rams’ long-snapper to end the 2025 season, replacing Alex Ward. He was excellent, helping the team reach the NFC Championship Game. He also played for the Rams from 2011 to 2020, earning Pro Bowl honors in 2016 and 2017. McQuaide also played for the Dallas Cowboys, Detroit Lions , Chicago Bears , Minnesota Vikings , Miami Dolphins , and Pittsburgh Steelers, either as a member of the active roster or the practice squad.“ Joshua Karty and Jake McQuaide add former Rams experience to current Rams special teams (rams.com) “McVay was asked on Wednesday if Karty would be utilized on kickoffs, to which McVay said he would “work through those things and kind of just see how the week goes.” On Friday, McVay said Karty being activated to the 48-man gameday roster would be contingent on some of the other injuries throughout the roster that have occurred throughout the week. McVay also said he thinks Karty’s ability to potentially impact kickoffs would impact that decision. The Rams decided to replace Karty with Mevis after Week 9 of last season. Karty’s production dropped from 85.3% on field goals his rookie season to 66.7% in his second season through eight games. Karty said on Wednesday that during training camp last year he was “dealing with a little hip thing” and “probably should have just rested for a bit in fall camp.” Experts overwhelmingly favor Rams over winless Chargers in Week 8 (sports.yahoo) “Of the 52 picks across USA Today, Bleacher Report, Sports Illustrated, ESPN, CBS Sports, The Athletic and NFL.com, 47 have the Rams winning. The only five picking the Chargers are all from Bleacher Report. The Rams are coming off a 35-21 win over the Raiders in Week 7, which snapped a two-game losing streak after back-to-back defeats to the Bills and Cardinals . Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 192 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 7, and Matthew Stafford threw three touchdown passes. A win Sunday would give Los Angeles back-to-back victories for the first time this season and set them up nicely for the second half of the year.“ Rams are ‘fixing’ special teams like a bad mechanic repairs a car (ramblinfan) “If you take an automobile for repairs to a bad mechanic, the telltale sign is the incessant swapping of parts that merely runs up the tab without fixing the problem. A dependable mechanic determines the problem and effects the necessary repairs. The difference is felt in the time at the shop and a much less expensive repair bill. Nobody is pointing the finger at general manager Les Snead – he’s doing what he can with a defective motor – but right now LA is merely swapping parts without a clue . Rams still grasping at straws to fix woeful special teams The entire ‘let’s see who can play?’ facade is something fans expected to be settled during training camp or, at worst, preseason. The issue is still at a tipping point approaching midseason. That’s not a good situation for a team that has struggled to stay at .500, while clinging to playoff aspirations.“ Hypothetical Rams trade sends mid-round picks for WR (ramswire) “In a hypothetical trade proposal, Nguyen has Los Angeles sending a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Jacksonville for Thomas. He argues the Rams made a mistake in the draft by not upgrading the offense that this deal could fix. The Rams tried to play it too cute in the draft and live in two timelines, taking quarterback Ty Simpson with the 13th pick when the best option this season would have been a receiver. Davante Adams is 33 and had hamstring issues last season — it wasn’t hard to predict he would miss games this season. Puka Nacua has had injury and off-field issues. How would KC Concepcion — whom I rated higher than Makai Lemon — look in their offense? They could rectify that mistake by trading for Thomas Jr. The Jaguars should be much more willing to trade Thomas Jr. to the NFC, rather than an AFC contender. Thomas Jr. would infuse much-needed speed to the offense, while his vertical route tree would complement Nacua, who makes his living in the middle of the field.“ Los Angeles Rams vs. Los Angeles Chargers Fantasy Football Matchup Breakdown For Week 8 (fantasylife) “ No way I was the only one circling this game on the schedule before the season even kicked off, thinking we’d be previewing a potential Super Bowl matchup. Can’t even tell you how many Justin Herbert MVP tickets I saw posted on socials this summer. Well, that ain’t happening — we’re seven weeks in, and these two LA teams combined for one total win in the entire month of October. Oof. “ Matthew Stafford Gets Concerning Update Before Rams Game (heavy.com) “Whittington is not a significant part of the Rams’ passing game. He has just two receptions for 12 yards on the season, and a 42-476-0 line for his career so far, which began as a sixth-round pick (213th overall) of the 2024 draft. However, while not one of Stafford’s top targets, he is a strong blocker on the perimeter. The Rams are already without Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) and Puka Nacua admitted this week that he is still managing the calf injury that popped up in practice last week.“ Rams Hit With Concerning Injury News Before Facing Chargers (sports.yahoo) “At this point in time, no one knows exactly when Garrett will return. There was hope that the Rams could open up his practice window this week, but that didn’t end up being the case . The current hope is that Adams could return in the shorter window of the original 6-to-8 week estimate. Going up against the Chargers should give L.A. a good chance to pick up another win. Jim Harbaugh and his team are 0-6 and not many positive signs of improvement have been seen. Hopefully, some of these updates receive good news before Sunday afternoon’s game. Kickoff this week against the Chargers is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to tune in and watch the game on Fox.“ Rams face injury concerns ahead of Chargers game as McVay praises defense, Aaron Donald (sportingtribune) “”Dylan McMahon has done a great job this week,” McVay said. “He’s had a lot of work. Ryan Wendell is always really good about getting a good rotation of guys, especially at that center position. Dylan’s had a lot of work this week because of the approach we’ve taken with Coleman. I think he’s handled it really well.” Whittington’s status could also affect the Rams’ special teams plans, including whether kicker Joshua Karty is elevated for the game. McVay said the staff has to consider how losing Whittington would affect the 48-player game-day roster and the team’s ability to handle injuries during the game. The Rams are already without two offensive playmakers: wide receiver Davante Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson.“ PODCAST: Chargers Football Therapy: Can Justin Herbert Spark a Reset Against the Rams? (sports.yahoo) “At the Playbook Restaurant, the discussion turns to simplifying responsibilities without becoming predictable. Can the Chargers build a smaller, more dependable collection of concepts that allows players to operate confidently? There is room to laugh, too. Reasonable Request or Chargers Fan Delusion separates realistic expectations from emotional wish lists, while the Chargers Emotional Support Draft asks which improvement would matter most: protection, rushing production, red-zone finishing or cleaner execution. Plus, get a Rams matchup framework, an appreciation for overlooked contributions and a schedule look ahead featuring Houston, Baltimore, the Jets and New England. Expect…

title: Rams fans confident in the team again; but should they be?
summary: 67% of Los Angeles Rams’ fans surveyed are confident that the team is headed in the right direction after their Week 7 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. After Week 6, when the Rams had lost to the Arizona Cardinals, fan confidence sat at 20%. One week later, one win later, and the majority of […]
full_text: 67% of Los Angeles Rams’ fans surveyed are confident that the team is headed in the right direction after their Week 7 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. After Week 6, when the Rams had lost to the Arizona Cardinals, fan confidence sat at 20% . One week later, one win later, and the majority of fans think this team is back on track, or at least confident in where the team is heading. Should fans be confident in the team’s direction after L.A.’s latest win over the Raiders? Imagine if the Rams lose to the winless Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8? What will fan confidence be at then? The fan vote seems to swing mightily after a win or a loss, and candidly, the Rams should’ve beaten the Raiders because the Rams are gunning for a Super Bowl. The Raiders are trying to compete in the future after seemingly being in a rebuild for years. L.A.‘s win over the Raiders may have increased fan confidence, but is that fair? Candidly, the Rams should’ve beaten the Cardinals in Week 6, and L.A. lost as you could argue the Rams haven’t won a game, yet, that truly indicates anything for the fans to be confident in. But, this is a week-to-week league and the Rams won last week, so by many accounts they are trending up. However, the Rams will need to keep winning to keep that confidence up. And so far, if you’ve bet against the Rams at FanDuel , you’ve likely won more than you’ve lost. At 3-4, the Rams are far from a shoe-in to make the playoffs. At the same time, there may be no better window to bet on the Rams given that many spectators may have fallen off of the Rams’ bandwagon. L.A. is no longer the favorite to win the Super Bowl. The San Francisco 49ers are . In theory, the Rams will be getting players like Trent McDuffie back this week and Myles Garrett at some point, so it’s possible this squad makes a real run. Anything is possible. What’s likely? So far, the Rams have more often than not shown an inconsistent offense, a defense that is stout but will wear down, a struggling special teams unit and are 0-2, so far, in the NFC West. The Rams have a lot to worry about. However, according to the fans, there is plenty to be confident in.

title: 5 under-the-radar wide receivers the Rams should trade for
summary: As the NFL trade deadline looms less than two weeks away, the Los Angeles Rams still face a need to bolster their wide receiver room. That need persists, even with the optimistic news on Davante Adams return from injured reserve, as L.A.’s division rivals have made trade moves to upgrade their squads for the stretch […]
full_text: As the NFL trade deadline looms less than two weeks away, the Los Angeles Rams still face a need to bolster their wide receiver room. That need persists, even with the optimistic news on Davante Adams return from injured reserve, as L.A.’s division rivals have made trade moves to upgrade their squads for the stretch run with trades already. The Rams have added some some practice squad support , but that’s not going to be nearly enough. Les Snead might have the will to swing a big deal, but with cap space barely in the black — $200k according to overthecap.com — there appears sparse room to swing any moves of consequence without re-working some current contracts. Keeping the money situation in mind, low-cost solutions to improve wide receiver are still available. While the Rams didn’t heed my advice on in-house receiver Brennan Presley, here are some options that are under contract with other teams. The cost of purchase would low and their salaries covered mostly by L.A.’s accompanying roster deletions. All would add special teams help immediately and possible playmaking to the offense. Dareke Young – Las Vegas Raiders The kind of out of the box thinking, low-cost addition that, in theory, could help on three fronts, offense, kick coverage and kickoff returns. Admittedly, Young has yet to provide any offensive fireworks in his five-year NFL career, but the basic skillset to be a playmaker is intact. He’s blessed with size (6’2” 224 lb), length (33”), and athleticism, testing a 4.44 forty, 1.54 10 yard split, 37” vertical and 11’ 7” broad jump. He compliments these markers with strength (22 bench reps), stellar agility/change of direction (6.88 3cone), and very good flexibility/burst/balance (4.19 shuttle). The Seattle Seahawks claimed Young at #233 of Round 7 in the 2022 draft. He was a tantalizing physical traits-based prospect out of D2 Lenoir Rhyne. Young has made all five opening rosters as a pro, but has battled leg injuries (quad and hamstring). Of 75 possible games, he’s played in 49, been inactive for 12, and been out with injuries on 22 occasions (two stints on IR). Where Young can help L.A. right away is his speed on coverage teams and kickoff returns. Since the beginning of 2025, his 12 coverage tackles would only trail Shaun Dolac’s 25 and his 28.5 yard kickoff return average would top all the Rams. Would Las Vegas give him up for a late draft pick? They would most likely be happy to get something, anything for a bottom half of the roster special teamer who’s a free agent at the end of the year. looking back at Dareke Young and his touches as a rookie. 7th-round WR didn't get a lot of volume, naturally, but some potential there. As Seattle assesses its WR3 situation this offseason, Dareke should be in discussion. (last catch negated by teammate penalty but whatever) pic.twitter.com/2H3hEcZKVU — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) January 23, 2023 Chimere Dike – Tennessee Titans What a difference a year makes, in Dike’s second year as a pro he appears to have fallen out of favor with the Tennessee Titans after being named All-Pro as a rookie. He’s played in all seven games, but been limited to 13 percent of Titans offensive snaps (52) for the season. Although still the primary punt and kickoff returner, Dike was targeted 74 times in 2025 and this year, has only eight to this point. Stellar burst (1.51 10-yard split) and speed (4.34 forty) with an easy glide style. Zero wasted effort. More of a linear mover, but still rates plus agility/change of direction (6.87 3cone) and good flexibility/burst/balance (4.25 shuttle). Top-tier leg strength/explosion (38” vertical, 10’ 8” broad). Dike shoehorns it into an well-proportioned, athletic frame at 6’ 1” 200 lb. and 32” arms. As a receiving prospect, I grade Dike with a very high ceiling, his current struggles in Tennessee notwithstanding. His playmaking ability in the return game is gravy. Good hands and ball-tracking. Defenses must respect his speed, but he has a very good feel for settling into soft areas of zones. With the ball in his hands, he’s not a dancer, he motors like a one-cut outside zone running back using vision burst and pretty good contact balance. With two more years on his cost-controlled rookie contract, he would, most likely, take the most capital to pry away from his current team. Under the new 2026 coaching staff, Dike may not be a fit in their plans, and the Titans will again be re-building in 2027. Packaging a late ’27 and mid ’28 draft pick or one of the Rams current receivers with a ’28 pick could seal the deal. LaJohntay Wester – Baltimore Ravens Diminutively-built at a touch under 5’ 10” and 165 lbs., Wester has the prototypical traits for a kick returner. Although he has good speed (4.46 forty) and burst, 1.53 10-yards split. He darts through traffic setting up blocks with vision and cuts made at speed, On offense, he fits into the motion system that allows him to operate in space. Mis-matched on safeties or linebackers, his one-cut move style and speed can lead to big plays. A Round 7 (#203) pick in 2025 by the Baltimore Ravens, Wester is in his second season as their primary punt returner and also has returned kickoffs. His offensive service has increased over his rookie yearoverall, but working behind Zay Flowers as the Ravens slot receiver is limiting. The Rams extensive use of pre-snap motion and condensed/stack sets could be very liberating. Wester’s open-field running skills could lead to more dynamic screen passes and jet sweeps. The value on Wester couldn’t be much, there is nary a word about his ability to be a part of the Ravens offensive future. His offensive snaps have fallen off a cliff since the first three weeks of the season. The Rams could use a little lightening in their return game. Wester is affordable, still on his rookie deal, and could likely be had for a later round pick, maybe even one in 2028. Bo Melton – Green Bay Packers Signed by the Seattle Seahawks at #229 of Round 7 in 2022, he was let go in final cuts and signed to the practice squad. Green Bay poached him late in December and declined to use him in those final games. 2023 saw Melton released and signed to the Packers practice squad and he bounced between it and the active roster. He gradually ramped up his reps over the course of 2024 to season high of 32 in playoff loss. For 2025, Green Bay cross trained him at cornerback, going two ways and working in as a kickoff returner. For 2026, he’s returned to offense full-time, along with his special teams duty. Not big framed at 5’ 11” 189 lbs. and 31“ arms, Melton is loose-limbed, strong, and has outstanding athletic traits. Timed a 4.34 forty and 1.50 split, along with 4.10 shuttle and 6.81 3cone. He showed both upper and lower body strength/explosiveness with 18 reps on the bench, 38” vertical and 10’ 1” broad jump. Versatility is the buzzword for Melton’s game and he’s actually a Rams-mold guy. Physical play style, good football IQ, and willing to block. Good depth of target rates shows he can handle the clear out responsibilities. He is an outstanding gunner, and has NFL work as a kickoff returner. Had a few punt returns in college. Does Green Bay over value him as a developable prospect and want too much? Rumors have the Pack looking to make a splash move for the stretch drive, L.A. should offer a late round pick to help them re-stock their draft coffers after such a move. Hell of a couple blocks by Bo Melton and Tucker Kraft to spring this duo run for a good gain pic.twitter.com/dYtJMzwbai — JP Acosta (@acosta32_jp) October 29, 2026 Elijah Moore – Philadelphia Eagles Former Round 2 draft pick, taken at #34 by the New York Jets in 2021. Moore has bounced through four teams since, the Cleveland Browns, Buffalo Bills, Denver Broncos and now resides in Philly. It’s fair to say he hasn’t lived up the draft pedigree, but is only a couple years past being a solid WR#2. At age 26, there’s plenty of tread left on the tires. At 5’10” 180 lbs.…

title: Former Rams coach loses defensive coordinator job
summary: The Carolina Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday following a loss to the Packers on Thursday. Evero previously spent five seasons on Sean McVay’s staff coaching defensive backs, from 2017 to 2021, prior to being hired as the Broncos defensive coordinator in 2022. Would now be the right time to bring Evero back […]
full_text: The Carolina Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday following a loss to the Packers on Thursday. Evero previously spent five seasons on Sean McVay’s staff coaching defensive backs, from 2017 to 2021, prior to being hired as the Broncos defensive coordinator in 2022. Would now be the right time to bring Evero back to the L.A. Rams? BREAKING: The #Panthers have fired DC Ejiro Evero, per @JFowlerESPN . Evero has been Carolina's DC since 2023. pic.twitter.com/lMePHTYykc — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 30, 2026 Evero’s Denver defense ranked seventh in yards allowed in 2022, but Nathaniel Hackett’s staff was quickly disassembled after a disastrous season with Russell Wilson. The Panthers next hired him to the same job and Carolina ranked fourth in yards allowed, but 29th in points allowed. In 2024, the Panthers were dead last in points and yards allowed, but the team showed patience with new head coach Dave Canales and his staff. Carolina improved the next season as they were middle of the pack defensively in 2025 and made the playoffs. However, the Panthers have fallen to 3-4 and they gave up 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, a sting that hasn’t gone away for Evero. But would he be welcomed back on a Rams defensive staff that could use some consultation in the secondary? Trent McDuffie could return to the field this weekend against the L.A. Chargers and the Rams have made a big investment there recently with McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, and Quentin Lake. Some fans think Chris Shula needs the help. If not more than just help.

title: NFL predictions: Rams commit to run game (again) vs. Chargers
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will make their running game a major priority once again when they meet the Chargers in Sunday’s Battle of Los Angeles. Expect Sean McVay to lean on his backfield early and often, using Week 7’s blueprint to control the tempo, wear down the Chargers’ defense and open up opportunities in the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Kyren Williams #23 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on prior to a preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams will make their running game a major priority once again when they meet the Chargers in Sunday’s Battle of Los Angeles. Expect Sean McVay to lean on his backfield early and often, using Week 7’s blueprint to control the tempo, wear down the Chargers’ defense and open up opportunities in the passing game. The Rams have found a successful formula by establishing the run, and there is little reason to abandon it against their cross-town rivals. Sunday’s matchup could produce another big day on the ground, with Los Angeles committing to the run regardless of how effective its passing attack might be early. Here are several predictions for what should be an intriguing divisional-style showdown between two Los Angeles rivals. 1. Rams score on opening drive touchdown Los Angeles’s offense has not been pretty with scoring on its opening drives in 2026. The Rams drives this year… Week 1 vs. SF – Punt (3 plays) Week 2 vs. NYG – Punt (3 plays) Week 3 @ DEN – Punt (7 plays) Week 4 @ PHI – Interception (3 plays) Week 5 vs. BUF – Missed Field Goal (14 plays) Week 6 – vs. ARI – Punt (3 plays) Week 7 – @ LV – Punt (3 plays) Week 8 – TBD The Rams not only get points, but a touchdown on the opening drive. 2. Joshua Karty is elevated to game day roster…for kickoffs With Karty’s signing to the practice squad and Brandon McManus being on the 53 man roster, Los Angeles is clearly eyeing Karty for its kickoff role. If the Rams are saying yes to Karty on kickoffs, I’ll be curious to see who is made inactive on gameday to give way for the team to have two kickers on the active gameday roster. 3. Rams generate five 20+ yard plays on offensee Whether its through the running game or passing game or a combination of both, the Rams will find a way to get more explosives going on Sunday. Puka Nacua is always a safe bet to catch 1 or 2 explosives. Blake Corum has shown ability to hit the running hole and take off. I think LA’s offense finds balance with its running and passing explosives. 4. Rams run the ball 30+ times for second consecutive week The Rams finally found their running game in Week 7 when they gave Kyren Williams and Blake Corum a combined 33 rushing attempts. Both players nearly went for 100 rushing yards/each. With both players providing significantly weekly contribution, Coach McVay has to stick with the recipe that made Los Angeles play its best game in 2026. I see the two getting another 15+ attempts again… Some additional context to the Rams run game's Week 7 performance that I found interesting from Next Gen Stats, especially about the effectiveness of man-concept carries pic.twitter.com/5fk3wMrrCz — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) October 26, 2026 5. Tutu Atwell catches 50+ yard pass With the Rams beginning to have an identity towards the running game and short passing game (checkdowns to running backs), opposing defenses may be inclined to bring their secondary closer to the line of scrimmage. The caveat is that Tutu Atwell is fast. And McVay will be looking for the opportunity to dial it up deep. Rams House, make some room for the SB Nation app! title: Does Josh Downs make sense for the Rams?
summary: Joshua Downs wants a trade away from the Indianapolis Colts, but does it make sense for the Los Angeles Rams to acquire him? Some would say, yes. Some would say, no. The dichotomy makes this a great debate. On the one hand, Downs is talented, he can stretch the field, but if memory serves, we’ve […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - OCTOBER 18: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs (2) during player introductions prior to the start of and NFL game between the Tennessee Titans and the Indianapolis Colts on October 18, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium at Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Joshua Downs wants a trade away from the Indianapolis Colts, but does it make sense for the Los Angeles Rams to acquire him? Some would say, yes . Some would say, no. The dichotomy makes this a great debate. On the one hand, Downs is talented, he can stretch the field, but if memory serves, we’ve seen the young man make some strong catches over the middle too. Though he’s not the biggest receiver, similar to Tutu Atwell. So, would Downs handle the level of run blocking the Rams might ask him to do? Also, would the Rams use Downs? It’s well-known Matthew Stafford sometimes just locks in on one player and goes from there. If Downs isn’t Stafford’s main target on a given day, how much work would he get? Can trading for Downs work? I believe Sean McVay could make it work. Is trading for Downs worth it? That’s the debate. As talented as Downs is, I am not sure he’s what the Rams need for the Super Bowl in 2026. I am not sure he truly moves the needle. I can be proven wrong. This story isn’t quite done being written just yet, but for me, more than any trade, the Rams need to win games. They have the pieces; it’s up to them to deliver. Los Angeles Rams Make Perfect Sense as Josh Downs Trade Suitor (sports.yahoo) “So far this season with the Colts, Downs has caught 26 passes for 307 yards, but has not found the end zone. Last year, he racked up 58 receptions for 566 yards and four scores. Throughout his entire 54-game NFL career, Downs has totaled 224 receptions for 2,447 yards and 11 touchdowns. At 25 years old, Downs would bring excellent slot production to the Rams’ offense. He would also be an addition both for this season and the future. Assuming Los Angeles worked out a contract extension with him, the move could pay dividends for years to come.“ Joshua Karty’s return is the full-circle flourish to Rams’ kicking saga (ramblinfan) “Perhaps the most hilarious, or tragic, for the doom and gloomers out there, aspect of Karty’s return is that he is in a sense replacing his own replacement, Harrison Mevis, who lasted all of 14 games after taking over last November. The Rams just can’t get this right. Rams re-up Joshua Karty in latest go-round of kicker carousel Grupe, their first stab at upgrading on Mevis, was waylaid by misfortune rather than mistake. Tearing his ACL on his second Rams kickoff was not the plan.“ 4 key matchups that will decide Rams vs. Chargers on Sunday (ramswire) “LT Alaric Jackson vs. OLB Khalil Mack Mack will play on the left and right side, so Warren McClendon Jr. will have to block him, too. But it’s imperative for Jackson to protect Matthew Stafford’s blindside because if Mack gets around the corner, he has the ability to attack the football and force fumbles.“ Chargers look to avoid 0-7 start in battle of LA (nbcsports) “Mike Florio details the nuggets in Week 8’s “battle of LA,” where the Chargers look to avoid their third-ever 0-7 start and Puka Nacua’s bid at history.“ Rams and Chargers share a city, not a rivalry as they head into their first meeting in 4 seasons (apnews) “INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Although the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers share a stadium, they don’t share a rivalry. The NFL schedule only puts these teams together once every four years, and they have neither the long history nor the recent animus necessary to make Sunday’s meeting into a true crosstown showdown. “It’s a big town to cross,” Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said with a grin. “I don’t run into those guys too often, to be honest with you. I don’t really want to make that drive. Nobody does.” Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are too potent for the Rams to ignore (ramblinfan) “In that game, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 192 rushing yards on 5.8 per carry, with each eclipsing 90. It was easily the run game’s most complete performance this season. In a recent interview on The Pat McAfee Show , Stafford described how his running back duo is perfectly suited for LA’s offense. “I haven’t had a tandem like Kyren Williams and Blake Corum where they both can do everything,” Stafford said. “We can call our entire offense with both of those guys in the game.” The offense continues to feature Stafford as its engine, propelling him to 1,989 passing yards, 14 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. But the Rams are also one of only two teams with two names among the league’s top 25 rushers.“ Puka Nacua admits he’s still managing his injured calf every day (ramswire) “He wound up playing and caught eight passes for 68 yards and a touchdown, but he’s not fully out of the woods yet with his injured calf. Nacua told reporters on Thursday that he’s still getting treatment and managing the injury, doing everything he can to suit up on Sundays. “After a Thursday practice, I’ll get some supplemental work, but it’s definitely something that, maintenance every day in the morning, moving some stuff in my insoles and stuff like that and working with everybody in the training room and ‘EQ’ [equipment staff] so I can go out there and play as free and confident as I can,” he said.“ ‘His Vertical Route Tree Would Complement (Puka) Nacua’ — NFL Analyst Urges Rams To Pursue Trade for Pro Bowl WR After Davante Adams’ Injury (sports.yahoo) “But now “The Athletic’s” Ted Nguyen is suggesting that trading for Brian Thomas Jr. could help swing the Super Bowl odds back in the Rams’ favor. His idea is for the Rams to send the Jacksonville Jaguars a third-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round pick in 2028 in exchange for the one-time Pro Bowler. “The Rams tried to play it too cute in the draft and live in two timelines, taking quarterback Ty Simpson with the 13th pick when the best option this season would have been a receiver,” Nguyen argues. “Davante Adams is 33 and had hamstring issues last season — it wasn’t hard to predict he would miss games this season. Puka Nacua has had injury and off-field issues.” Sean McVay open to having 2 kickers active on game day (sports.yahoo) “Mevis lost his job this season due to the same issues, with Blake Grupe (tore his ACL in his first game) and Brandon McManus taking over since. With Karty back in the facility, and his “knuckleball” kickoff style being pointed at as a possible solution to the team’s long-standing kick coverage issues, some wonder if the Rams will entertain the idea of having two kickers on their game-day roster. Head coach Sean McVay would not close the door on the idea. “We’ll work through all different things,” said McVay. “It all depends. When you have 48 bodies and the different guys that are filling in, you have to really ask yourself, ‘Okay, does that really make sense? Does it fit?’ There are a lot of layers to it so I wouldn’t be ready to answer that question yet.” Week 8 Preview: Los Angeles Chargers vs Los Angeles Rams (lastwordonsports) “The Rams are in the midst of the easiest part of their schedule. They must capitalize on this opportunity and come away with a win this week. The Chargers are vulnerable with several problems throughout their roster. During the offseason, the Chargers hired offensive extraordinaire Mike McDaniel as their offensive coordinator. McDaniel has struggled to find success, while Star Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has had the worst start to a season in his career. The Chargers will also be without star safety Derwin James Jr., who has missed the last three games with a hamstring injury.“ Comment od the day: Feed post of the day:

title: Raiders Mailbag: Should Las Vegas sell Maxx Crosby, Kolton Miller, other players ahead of NFL trade deadline?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have a chance to end their four-game losing streak against the New York Jets in Week 8. But we’re also less than two weeks away from the NFL Trade Deadline (Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 1:00 p.m. PST), which is the primary focus of this week’s mailbag. Let’s get to it! Q: […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have a chance to end their four-game losing streak against the New York Jets in Week 8 . But we’re also less than two weeks away from the NFL Trade Deadline (Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 1:00 p.m. PST), which is the primary focus of this week’s mailbag. Let’s get to it! Q: Would be interesting to hear your take on trading Maxx Crosby, Jackson Powers-Johnson, Kolton Miller, Isaiah Palo-Mao and Kirk Cousins? Seems like the right thing to do given the team’s realistic timeline. A: I’ll start with the elephant in the room. I was a strong proponent of trading Crosby in the offseason and still think it would be in the Raiders’ best long-term interests to get multiple high-end draft picks for the 29-year-old. I think two first-rounders is probably out of the question now, but it doesn’t hurt that Jeffery Simmons — who is the same age and was in the same draft class as Crosby — just got dealt for two firsts and a fourth, with a fifth going back to Chicago. Also, Simmons is only under contract for one more year than Crosby is. So, I think John Spytek could get at least a comparable return for the edge rusher, and I don’t know how Spytek could say ‘no’ to an offer like that after the team’s playoff hopes came crumbling down this month. It doesn’t seem like Crosby is going anywhere, though, with Adam Schefter saying on Monday that “he means so much to that franchise” while pouring cold water on the trade talk/rumors. But if I’m calling the shots, I’m pulling the trigger if I can get at least a first- and a second-round pick for Crosby. I touched on this last week ; it feels like Powers-Johnson’s days in Las Vegas are numbered after getting benched. I don’t know if that happens ahead of the trade deadline, but barring a material change, I think JPJ will be shopped in the offseason. I liken it to Tyree Wilson from this past offseason, where a fresh start might be best for both sides, and don’t expect much more than a fifth-rounder in return. I’m all the way out on trading Miller ahead of the deadline. I know he has regressed, but if the plan is to have Fernando Mendoza play at any point this year, I’m not trusting Charles Grant to protect Mendoza’s blindside. Grant has barely seen the field, and at least the coaching staff knows what it can get from Miller, who has been a good pass protector in the past and is still solid right now. Could Grant be the long-term solution at left tackle? Sure, but turning the reins over to him now would be a massive risk, especially with a rookie quarterback/the future of the franchise. In the offseason, I could be convinced that it’s worth it to trade Miller because then the coaching staff has several months to get Grant ready and can bring in a veteran insurance policy in free agency. But midseason, trading Miller would be a bad idea, in my opinion. If there’s an offer, Pola-Mao would be easy to part with since he’s just a backup and special teamer right now. I just don’t know if there’s much of a market for that, barring an injury over the next two weekends. If IPM gets dealt, don’t expect much more than a sixth- for seventh-round pick swap or just a seventh-rounder. Also, he’s an impending free agent, so I could see Pola-Mao getting waived after the deadline to make room for Dalton Johnson on the game-day active roster. I feel like I’m in the minority on this, but I would rather see the Raiders hold onto Cousins even if Mendoza is playing. Trust me, as a draft freak, I love the idea of getting more picks. However, I think it reduces part of the rationale for having Cousins be Mendoza’s mentor if the former gets shipped away when the latter takes over. I know that has to happen at some point, but I think it’s valuable for the rookie to have a peer as a sounding board when things go wrong during his first handful of starts. Especially since Cousins has seen it all in the NFL, and those two have been forming a big brother-little brother type of relationship over the last six months. A: Well, as someone who watches and breaks down the Raiders’ defense every week, the past month was already pretty unwatchable, LOL! But to your point, if Crosby does get traded, that creates a need for an edge and adds to the already rather long list of needs. That’s why I wouldn’t make that trade for just one first-round pick, and the return would have to include multiple Top 100 selections. The plan for a Crosby-less defense in Vegas would hinge on Keyron Crawford bouncing back from injury and at least proving to be a quality second edge defender since Malcolm Koonce is on a one-year contract and Kwity Paye is trending toward being a bust/role player. Then, that’s where the two picks come in because one can be used to find Crosby’s replacement or the second edge if Crawford fills that role, and the second pick fills a different need like defensive tackle. Obviously, there are a lot of variables that can go wrong in there. But the defense has given up over 35 points per game over the last four weeks with Crosby on it. Several positions need to be addressed in the offseason, and he’ll be 30 in August. So, would you rather have a very good but aging player, or two chances to improve the team for the long haul? It’s a matter of preference, and there’s a good amount of risk involved in either scenario. But, again, I’d take my chances if the right offer comes across the desk. Q: Is it time to have a realistic discussion on Spytek? A: I got a lot of questions about Spytek this week, with several people asking if (or outright saying) he should get fired. I get it, the Raiders need to get a lot more return on their offseason investments. There’s no denying that, and Spytek’s Day 2 picks have produced little to nothing. Darien Porter is the best one so far, and Porter hasn’t been able to hold down a starting spot. But part of the reason why the organization can’t get out of the downward spiral that it’s been in over the last two decades is that there has been no stability when it comes to the head coach and general manager. Granted, the Raiders didn’t have a true GM until Reggie McKenzie was hired in 2012, but it’s not like Mark Davis has been patient with his decision-makers. To be fair, McKenzie got seven years. But even he had a few dud offseasons before putting together the 2016 roster, which has been the franchise’s best team since making the Super Bowl over 20 years ago. To put it in perspective, the Raiders were 10-37 during McKenzie’s first three years. Then, he had a great draft in 2014 (Khalil Mack, Derek Carr and Gabe Jackson), signed some quality free agents (Rodney Hudson, Kelechi Osemele and Michael Crabtree), and hit on his 2015 first-round pick (Amari Cooper) to put together a quality roster. The problem was that 2017 was a major disappointment, so Davis fired Jack Del Rio and hired Jon Gruden, which essentially stripped any power away from McKenzie and led to his firing a year later. In stepped Mike Mayock for three seasons until Gruden’s email scandal led to another leadership turnover, where Davis brought in the Josh McDaniels-Dave Ziegler duo for a season-and-a-half. That didn’t work out, so it was Tom Telesco’s turn for a year, only for Tom Brady to come in and hire Spytek. At some point, the Raiders have to stick with a plan and ride it out, even if the road gets bumpy. General managers — especially ones taking over bad teams/rosters, which is the majority of them — get hired because of the long-term plan they present to the owner, which typically is a three- to four-year vision. However, Davis hasn’t given a GM three seasons since Mayock, who was hired pre-COVID, and McKenzie is the only one of the five GMs Davis has hired to get four or more years! Do I think it’s fair to say Spytek should face criticism and feel a lot of pressure right now? Absolutely. But this franchise needs stability, and firing a third general manager in five years would be a mistake. The other…

title: Las Vegas Raiders-New York Jets FEED Topic: Monitoring Geno Smith’s ‘revenge game’
summary: Quarterback Geno Smith’s tenure with the Las Vegas Raiders was certainly a brief one. With his old coach Pete Carroll running the show in Las Vegas, the Raiders gave the Seattle Seahawks a third-round pick for Smith in March during the 2025 offseason. A year later (almost on the exact date), Las Vegas sent Smith […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Quarterback Geno Smith’s tenure with the Las Vegas Raiders was certainly a brief one. With his old coach Pete Carroll running the show in Las Vegas, the Raiders gave the Seattle Seahawks a third-round pick for Smith in March during the 2025 offseason. A year later (almost on the exact date), Las Vegas sent Smith to the New York Jets for a sixth- and seventh-round pick swap. Seeing as the Raiders and Jets play this weekend, that’s arguably the biggest storyline of the Week 8 matchup. Smith’s lone season in Las Vegas wasn’t pretty. In fact, it was downright ugly. He made 15 starts, posting a 2-13 record while throwing for 3,025 yards and almost as many touchdowns (19) as interceptions (17) . The latter was the most in the NFL. On top of that, the veteran quarterback clearly wasn’t happy with the Raiders. The boiling point came in late November. After a 24-10 loss to a 2-8 Cleveland Browns team, frustrated fans showered Smith with boos as he left the field, and he responded by giving them the finger. Smith apologized for his actions , but at that point, it was pretty clear the organization would be moving on from him in the offseason. Now in New York, the 14-year veteran has had a decent bounce-back performance. He’s only thrown two picks and already has 10 touchdowns, while ranking 13th in the league with 1,623 passing yards . Granted, the Jets are 2-5, so the quarterback’s improvement hasn’t led to many wins. But there’s no denying that he’s playing better than last season. Smith has played it coy in the media this week, saying he doesn’t “really put too much stock into” facing his previous team while mixing in the “it’s just another game” cliché (h/t Randy Lang of the Jets’ website ). However, one has to imagine he’s had this matchup circled on the calendar as a “revenge game” given how last year unfolded. On top of his personal experience, Smith and Carroll are close, so he’s likely looking for retribution for his old coach, too. Meanwhile, the Raiders’ defense was atrocious in October. Vegas heads into Week 8 ranking 29th (fourth from last) with 28.1 points per game allowed for the entire season, and the unit was dead last over the last month with 35.8 PPG allowed, four points worse than any other team, per Sumer Sports . Granted, stopping the run has been the bigger problem. However, a coverage unit that allows the sixth-highest EPA per pass (0.12) and third-highest pass success rate (50.8%) on the campaign, per Sumer , certainly isn’t helping the cause either. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on Smith’s revenge game. The game kicks off at 10:00 a.m. PST and will air on FOX (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!

title: Raiders Week 8: Jets defense can turn afterburners on Las Vegas
summary: It’s easy to look at the New York Jets, see the 2-5 overall record, and be dismissive. Gang Green is on a two-game schneid losing back-to-back tilts against AFC East division foes — one of the defeats a 28-25 one against the previously winless Miami Dolphins this past Sunday. Aaron Glenn’s football team totaled 137 […]
full_text: (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s easy to look at the New York Jets, see the 2-5 overall record, and be dismissive. Gang Green is on a two-game schneid losing back-to-back tilts against AFC East division foes — one of the defeats a 28-25 one against the previously winless Miami Dolphins this past Sunday. Aaron Glenn’s football team totaled 137 point scored on offense (27th amongst the 32 NFL teams) with the 21st-ranked passing attack (1,446 yards) and 22nd-ranked ground game (675 yards). A category where the Jets ranked Top 10 in offense: Turnovers with just five (sixth-least). A feather in offensive coordinator Frank Reich’s cap in what’s otherwise a sea of mediocrity. Where the Jets are tough, however: Defense — Glenn’s specialty that got him head coaching gig in New York after a string of strong seasons as a defensive coordinator. Relying on a solid playing career as a highly respected cornerback in the NFL and coaching he absorbed, the Jets defensive play caller has his group allowing 2,208 total yards (ninth best) and 150 total points (13th best). Taking after their coach’s stingy performance as a player, New York’s passing defense is ranked fifth-best allowing 1,314 yards and limiting opponents to the sixth-best 213 passing attempts. Don’t count Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak as one who’ll sidestep the downtrodden Jets. “I see an extremely physical team. I see a very talented team. They have our full attention,” Kubiak said during his media session on Wednesday. “They’re very well-coached. And no matter who we’re playing each week, on these days, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, we’d better make sure we’re focusing on ourselves and getting ourselves better.” The Silver & Black’s rookie head coach speaks facts because while some may disregard the Jets, one could easily scoff at the Raiders who are 3-4 overall having dropped four-straight games and showcasing one of the league’s worst defenses (29th in points allowed at 197 and yards yielded at 2,616). And if Las Vegas isn’t on point, they’ll roll another snake eye’s and New York can turn on the afterburners defensively to burn the visiting Raiders. The Jets have forced 10 fumbles this season, the second-most in the league behind only LV, and the most by a Jet defense after six games since 2001. EDGE David Bailey is one of just six players with three forced fumbles on the year, and the first rookie to reach three in just… pic.twitter.com/me9spqBIdd — NYJ Communications (@NYJetsPR) October 23, 2026 We’re slated to likely see a key strength vs. strength clash when the Raiders and Jets meet this Sunday. Kubiak’s offense is imbalanced with a struggling ground game (ranked 30th in yards gained at 523) but does boast an impressive aerial assault ranking fourth-best in both passing yards (1,883) and touchdowns thrown (16). Veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins is at the helm of the air attack and ranks third in yards (1,877) and is atop the league the 16 touchdowns thrown. The 38-year-old signal caller has been sacked 10 times this season (23rd least) but with a stingy Jets pass defense in front of him that boasts talented rookie pass rusher David Bailey (5.5 sacks), Las Vegas is danger of being grounded. Bailey, the player chosen after the Raiders made Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, has lived up to the hype he created at Texas Tech but didn’t practice all week due to a groin injury and is listed as doubtful for Sunday’s clash. If he plays, though, the 23-year-old uses his 6-foot-3 and 251-pound frame well at the NFL level and leads the Jets in sacks, pressures (14), tackles for loss (seven), and forced fumbles (three), with 35 total tackles (only two missed, according to Pro Football Reference ). The group of Kingsley Enagbare (2.5 sacks), Jowon Briggs, Will McDonald, and Demario Davis (each with two sacks) have gotten to opposing quarterbacks this season. And Glenn’s defense doesn’t shy away from sending defensive backs at signal callers as safeties Andre Cisco and Dane Belton, and cornerback Jarvis Brownlee all have a sack, too. While Cousins has only been officially “dropped” 10 times, he’s been pressured more frequently in the Raiders’ string of consecutive losses and the Jets aren’t going to shy away from blitzing Las Vegas offense — both against the pass and run. Especially with defensive backs being stingy in coverage. Veteran cornerback Brandon Stephens has been targeted 39 times allowing just 17 completions (43.6 percent) while younger corners Azareye’h Thomas (24 completions on 40 targets, 60 percent) and Jarvis Brownlee (15 completions on 25 targets, 60 percent) can hold their own in coverage. Stephens and Thomas led the Jets with six and five pass deflections, respectively. New York’s run defense is 24th in the league allowing 894 yards and expect the Jets to to load the box with eight defenders to stonewall the Raiders run game — which has worked and the Silver & Black able to adjust and fix that. That said, confidence isn’t lacking from the Raiders despite the team averaging a meager 3.0 yards per carry (second-last in the NFL). Listen to starting running back Ashton Jeanty below: #Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty on facing the #Jets defense this week: "Yeah. I think we can definitely get the run game going. Get back on track. … A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names." 😳 pic.twitter.com/ySSn53MpMC — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 29, 2026 Bold talk from Jeanty, a tailback that’s below the league average of 4.2 yards per carry and sits 37th amongst his contemporaries with 3.1 yards per tote. But that’s the type of confidence the Raiders need to snap the losing skid and get to .500 instead of 3-5. “It’s a team thing. We can all do things better, running backs, fullbacks, offensive line. It’s a team thing,” Kubiak said about awakening a dormant ground game. We’re definitely focusing on different things with each player, but we can all improve.” Las Vegas will need a concentrated defensive effort, too, that keeps Jets out of the end zone and forcing three-and-outs to give Kubiak’s offense the opportunity to be balanced and not go pass-happy as it’s fallen behind severely in previous outings. “It’s tackling, it’s alignment, it’s assignment. It’s just playing a better brand of football and getting back to how we started this season,” Kubiak said of what’s needed for the team to quell getting gashed by opposing rushing attacks. Head-to-Head Sunday’s matchup marks the 50th time the Raiders and Jets clash all time. The Silver & Black lead the series 27-20-2 (25-18-2 in regular season play with playoff action knotted at 2-2) and are riding a two-game win streak dating to action in 2020 (31-28 victory) and 2023 (16-12 win). The last time Gang Green dropped the Raiders was in 2019 — a 34-3 thumping in Oakland. That 2023 contest was the most recent clash between the two teams and that featured a battle of field goals until Raiders tight end Michael Mayer (a rookie then) outjumped a Jets defender for a fourth-quarter touchdown from quarterback Aidan O’Connell. Quotes of Note “There’s not one big thing. There are plenty of things we’re working on that we’re being intentional about. I wish it was just one thing, but it never is. Whether you’re on a 3-4 team or an undefeated team, you’re always improving your weaknesses, always trying to get players better and get the young players better who are going to play one day. That’s part of the job, preparing for one week and preparing for the future, all in the same day.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak when asked if there’s one big overall thing the team is working on in practice prepping for Week 8 “Tre’s done a great job. Even more importantly, the chemistry is good. It’ll keep getting better. But I think just expanding his role and allowing him to do more and more. As we’ve given him more, he keeps showing he can do it.…
